text:
廣東鄉試錄序
嘉靖丙午秋粤當大比士監
察御史楊以誠奉
命按治寔維監臨申嚴胥飭凡簾
內外百執事咸愼簡以充先
是前巡按御史陳儲秀稽度
規恢表章令甲徵靜深等以
===
需校藝至是咸集乃以靜深
曁教諭蕭萬斛總試而分經
校閱則學正呂天恩教諭黃
繼宗雷孟冬吳珊陳英選提
調則左布政使朱紈左參政
張鏊監試則按察使屠大山
僉事何元述規畫維允罔弗
punctuated:

translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the bingwu year of Jiajing (1546), Guangdong was due to hold its triennial examination of scholars. Investigating Censor Yang Yicheng, charged by imperial command with inspecting the province, served as Supervising Official. He reiterated strict requirements and enjoined all concerned to observe them. All personnel serving inside and outside the examination curtain were carefully selected for their duties. Previously, the former Regional Inspector, Chen Chuxiu, had assessed and planned improvements to the arrangements [?], promulgated the statutory regulations, and summoned Jingshen and others in readiness to evaluate the examination essays. By this time they had all assembled. Jingshen and Instructor Xiao Wanhu were therefore put in overall charge of the examination. The evaluation of papers by individual Classic was assigned to Instructor Lü Tian’en and Instructors Huang Jizong, Lei Mengdong, Wu Shan, and Chen Yingxuan. Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Wan and Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Ao served as Proctors; Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Tu Dashan and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner He Yuanshu supervised the conduct of the examination. translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], Guangdong was due to hold its triennial examination of scholars. Investigating Censor Yang Yicheng, acting under imperial orders to inspect and administer the province, served as Supervising Official. He reiterated strict requirements and enjoined all to observe them. All personnel serving inside and outside the examination curtain were carefully selected for their duties. Previously, the former Regional Inspector, Chen Chuxiu, had deliberated and planned comprehensively, promulgated the established regulations, and summoned Jingshen and others to await the assessment of the candidates’ compositions. By this time, all had assembled. Jingshen and County School Instructor Xiao Wanhu were therefore placed in overall charge of the examination. The reading and assessment of papers, divided by Classic, were entrusted to School Instructor Lü Tian’en and County School Instructors Huang Jizong, Lei Mengdong, Wu Shan, and Chen Yingxuan. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Wan and Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Ao. Supervision of the examination was entrusted to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Tu Dashan and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner He Yuanshu. title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
寅恭事事維時兵部右侍郎
張岳奠綏南服保釐化誨人
有寧宇士咸思奮都御史顧
遂屏翰方隅燕及士類敦獎
縫掖振雅覬文總兵平江伯
陳圭雅尚儒術恤刑郎中杜
捄樂觀鉅典右參政張烜左
===
參議朱憲章右參議方民悅
副使張瑤袁載僉事陳捷都
指揮王寵則皆協志宣猷率
作于外右布政使龔輝左參
議顧中孚僉事施雨都指揮
夏忠先期次第入
賀若左布政使今陞都御史應
punctuated: 寅恭事事。維時，兵部右侍郎張岳奠綏南服，保釐化誨，人有寧宇，士咸思奮。都御史顧遂屏翰方隅，燕及士類，敦獎縫掖，振雅覬文。總兵平江伯陳圭雅尚儒術，恤刑郎中杜捄樂觀鉅典。右參政張烜、左參議朱憲章、右參議方民悅、副使張瑤、袁載、僉事陳捷、都指揮王寵，則皆協志宣猷，率作于外。右布政使龔輝、左參議顧中孚、僉事施雨、都指揮夏忠，先期次第入賀。若左布政使今陞都御史應
translation_en: …reverently attended to every duty. At this time, Zhang Yue, Right Vice Minister of War, secured and pacified the southern territories, protecting and governing them and providing moral instruction. The people enjoyed peaceful homes, and the scholars all aspired to exert themselves. Gu Sui, Censor-in-Chief, served as a bulwark for the region; his beneficence extended to the scholarly community. He earnestly encouraged men of learning, promoting refined scholarship and looking to literary accomplishment [?]. Chen Gui, Regional Commander and Earl of Pingjiang, had long esteemed Confucian learning. Du Jiu, Bureau Director charged with reviewing criminal cases, welcomed the opportunity to witness this great ceremony. Zhang Xuan, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhu Xianzhang, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Fang Minyue, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zhang Yao and Yuan Zai, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Chen Jie, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; and Wang Chong, Regional Military Commissioner, all united their purposes in carrying out the plans and took the lead in work outside the examination compound. Gong Hui, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Gu Zhongfu, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Shi Yu, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; and Xia Zhong, Regional Military Commissioner, successively went to court before the appointed date to offer congratulations. As for Ying, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, now promoted to Censor-in-Chief …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大猷按察使今陞山東右布
政使駱顒副使今陞湖廣右
參政游居敬雖先後去粵亦
皆與有聞焉者也旣圍棘鑰
院御史率衆而籲諗曰諸大
夫其有思乎衆唯唯又曰玆
役也事
===
君以人也苟弗參以衆見非忠也
其毖諸曰辭尚體要有弗誠
弗衷弗率于
訓者其麾諸曰
上再三俞議矣其祗奉
德音無侵無昵協于大公惟眞材
之務得其勗諸衆唯唯內外
punctuated: 大猷、按察使今陞山東右布政使駱顒、副使今陞湖廣右參政游居敬，雖先後去粵，亦皆與有聞焉者也。旣圍棘鑰院，御史率衆而籲諗曰：「諸大夫，其有思乎？」衆唯唯。又曰：「玆役也，事君以人也。苟弗參以衆見，非忠也，其毖諸！」曰：「辭尚體要，有弗誠、弗衷、弗率于訓者，其麾諸！」曰：「上再三俞議矣，其祗奉德音，無侵無昵，協于大公，惟眞材之務得，其勗諸！」衆唯唯。內外
translation_en:
…Dayou; Luo Yong, Surveillance Commissioner, now promoted to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong; and You Jujing, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, now promoted to Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of Huguang—although they had left Guangdong at different times, all had also been involved in these affairs.
Once the examination compound had been enclosed with thorn branches and locked, the Investigating Censor gathered everyone and earnestly addressed them: “Gentlemen, have you given thought to this?” They all answered assent. He continued: “This undertaking serves the sovereign by providing him with men. If we fail to consult the views of everyone, we are not being loyal. Be vigilant in this!” He said: “In writing, what matters is substance and essentials. Reject any work that is insincere, unsound, or fails to follow the instructions!” He said: “His Majesty has repeatedly approved the proposals. Reverently uphold his gracious words; allow neither encroachment nor favoritism, and act together with complete impartiality. Strive solely to obtain men of true ability. Exert yourselves in this!” They all answered assent. Those within and without…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
咸精白事事乃進提學副使
陳愷所簡士二千四百三試
之遵
制額拔其雋七十五人并梓其文
之粹者以
獻而靜深職務猥序首簡竊惟粵
本虞夏要服而祝融遐壤也
===
頃靜深以介聘而來也道彭
蠡泝章貢南度庾嶺煙雲杳
靄之間一翠千里星日之南
際天為壑蓋奧區也已旣乃
俊髦畢來雲蒸景附縱觀乎
所為文則深蓄濬發其體類
皆雄渾昌大而莊重秀偉其

咸精白事事，乃進提學副使陳愷所簡士二千四百，三試之，遵制額拔其雋七十五人，并梓其文之粹者以獻。而靜深職務，猥序首簡。竊惟粵本虞夏要服，而祝融遐壤也。

translation_en:
…all purified their intentions and attended to their duties. Then the 2,400 candidates selected by Chen Kai, Vice Commissioner for Education, were brought forward and examined in three sessions. In accordance with the imperially prescribed quota, seventy-five outstanding candidates were selected, and the finest of their compositions were also printed from woodblocks for presentation to the throne. As part of my duties, I, Jingshen, have presumptuously written this preface for the opening leaves. I humbly reflect that Guangdong was originally within the outer zone of submission under Yu and Xia, a distant domain of Zhurong.
Recently, when I, Jingshen, came upon an invitation conveyed through an intermediary [?], I passed by Pengli, traveled upstream along the Zhang and Gong rivers, and crossed the Yu Ridge southward. Amid dim banks of mist and cloud, an unbroken green stretched a thousand li. South of the stars and sun, valleys extended to the horizon: this was indeed a secluded region. Then the outstanding scholars all arrived, gathering like clouds and following like shadows. Surveying their compositions, I found deeply stored learning expressed with profound insight. title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
達也冲和浩放而洋洋纚纚
其究也淵邃貞明而變見鼓
奮蓋阜和之委溟浸之光
聖人之錫極均是乎得焉吁盛矣
可為嶺南重矣彼云職方者
謂清淑不類中州而多乎瑰
奇瑋麗之産蓋末也何也山
===
之入中國昉崑崙經岷嶓數
萬里而窮於海故盤為五嶺
嶺至峻位離得天地禮信光
亨之氣而上應乎
嚮明之治是故鍾英炳靈逢期
翊
運後先名碩固種種也乃斯文
punctuated: 達也，冲和浩放而洋洋纚纚；其究也，淵邃貞明而變見鼓奮。蓋阜和之委，溟浸之光，聖人之錫極，均是乎得焉。吁，盛矣！可為嶺南重矣！彼云職方者，謂清淑不類中州，而多乎瑰奇瑋麗之産，蓋末也。何也？山之入中國，昉崑崙，經岷嶓數萬里而窮於海，故盤為五嶺。嶺至峻，位離，得天地禮信光亨之氣，而上應乎嚮明之治。是故鍾英炳靈，逢期翊運，後先名碩，固種種也。乃斯文
translation_en: …in their expression, they are balanced and harmonious, expansive and unrestrained, flowing abundantly and continuously; in their ultimate reach, they are profound, steadfast, and luminous, displaying transformations and stirring vigor. Here are gathered abundant and harmonious influences, the radiance of the vast ocean’s waters, and the supreme norm bestowed by the sage ruler: all are attained here. Ah, how flourishing! This can indeed lend distinction to Lingnan! Those who discourse on geography say that its pure and felicitous influences differ from those of the Central Region, and that it abounds in rare, extraordinary, and magnificent products. Yet this concerns only superficial matters. Why? The mountains entering the Central Kingdom originate in Kunlun, pass through Min and Bo, and extend for tens of thousands of li before ending at the sea; thus they coil into the Five Ranges. These ranges are exceedingly lofty and occupy the position of Li, the southern trigram. They receive the vital influences of Heaven and Earth—ritual propriety, trustworthiness, radiance, and flourishing—and correspond above to a government turned toward the light. Thus they concentrate excellence and manifest spiritual potency; those born of these influences meet their appointed time and assist the dynastic fortune. Distinguished men of great learning have indeed appeared in succession in manifold abundance. Now, as for these writings…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
達也冲和浩放而洋洋纚纚
其究也淵邃貞明而變見鼓
奮蓋阜和之委溟浸之光
聖人之錫極均是乎得焉吁盛矣
可爲嶺南重矣彼云職方者
謂清淑不類中州而多乎瑰
奇瑋麗之産蓋末也何也山
===
之入中國昉崑崙經岷嶓數
萬里而窮於海故盤爲五嶺
嶺至峻位離得天地禮信光
亨之氣而上應乎
嚮明之治是故鍾英炳靈逢期
翊
運後先名碩固種種也乃斯文
punctuated: 達也，冲和浩放，而洋洋纚纚；其究也，淵邃貞明，而變見鼓奮。蓋阜和之委，溟浸之光，聖人之錫極，均是乎得焉。吁，盛矣！可爲嶺南重矣！彼云職方者，謂清淑不類中州，而多乎瑰奇瑋麗之産，蓋末也。何也？山之入中國，昉崑崙，經岷嶓，數萬里而窮於海，故盤爲五嶺。嶺至峻，位離，得天地禮信光亨之氣，而上應乎嚮明之治。是故鍾英炳靈，逢期翊運，後先名碩，固種種也。乃斯文
translation_en: …in its expression, harmonious and expansive, flowing forth copiously and continuously; in its ultimate depths, profound, steadfast, and luminous, manifesting transformations and stirring vigorous activity. The accumulated abundance and harmony, the radiance of the vast ocean, and the supreme standard bestowed by the sage—all find their realization here. Ah, how flourishing! This may indeed lend distinction to Lingnan! Those who speak as geographers say that its pure and благicent influences differ from those of the Central Plain, and that it abounds in rare, wondrous, and splendid products; yet these are merely peripheral matters. Why is this? The mountains entering the central lands begin at Kunlun, pass through Min and Bo, and extend for tens of thousands of li before ending at the sea; thus they coil into the Five Ranges. These ranges are exceedingly lofty and occupy the position of Li, the southern trigram. They receive from Heaven and Earth the vital influences of ritual propriety, trustworthiness, radiance, and flourishing, and above respond to the enlightened rule of the sovereign. Thus they concentrate excellence and manifest spiritual potency, meeting the appointed time and assisting the dynastic destiny. Eminent and learned men have indeed appeared in succession in great numbers. And this literary culture…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
又得於磅礴鬱積而非偶然
者與始南國之榛狉也周宣
起而疆理其臣賛之歌金石
矢文德焉我
皇祖受
命宅夏遂臣荒服越裳來王齊哇
秩祀蓋禹平舜肇所未有也
===
列聖熈洽肆我
聖天子中興薄海內外涵濡煦嫗
頃者修文告款雕題允乎敘
戎之
成烈而追琢人文播爲
心法典訓又皆危微精一之旨使
尹召復生不知何如以對揚
punctuated:
又得於磅礴鬱積，而非偶然者與？始南國之榛狉也，周宣起而疆理，其臣賛之，歌金石，矢文德焉。我皇祖受命宅夏，遂臣荒服，越裳來王，齊哇秩祀，蓋禹平舜肇所未有也。
列聖熈洽，肆我聖天子中興，薄海內外，涵濡煦嫗。頃者修文告款，雕題允乎敘戎之成烈；而追琢人文，播爲心法典訓，又皆危微精一之旨。使尹召復生，不知何如以對揚
translation_en:
…does it not also arise from this vast accumulation of vital forces, rather than occur by chance? When the southern lands were still overgrown and wild, King Xuan of Zhou arose and established their boundaries and administration. His ministers praised him, singing to bells and chime stones and setting forth his civil virtue. Our imperial ancestor received Heaven’s mandate and established his rule in the Chinese heartland. He then brought the remotest regions into submission; Yueshang came to acknowledge his kingship, and Qi wa [?] was accorded a place in the prescribed sacrifices. Such achievements had not been seen even when Yu brought the land to order and Shun first established its divisions.
Successive sage emperors brought flourishing harmony. Now our sagely Son of Heaven has brought about a restoration, extending his nourishing warmth throughout the realm and beyond, to the seas. Recently, through the cultivation of civil virtue, the tattooed peoples have declared their allegiance [?]: truly a glorious achievement in bringing the Rong peoples into order. Moreover, he has refined literary culture and disseminated canonical instructions on the methods of cultivating the mind, all embodying the teaching that the human mind is precarious and the mind of the Way subtle, requiring refinement and singleness of purpose. Were Yi Yin and the Duke of Shao to return to life, I do not know how they could fittingly acknowledge and extol …

translation_en:
…and was this, too, attained through a vast accumulation of energies, rather than by chance? When the southern lands were still overgrown and wild, King Xuan of Zhou arose to delimit and order their territories. His ministers assisted him, singing to bells and stone chimes and setting forth his civil virtue. Our imperial progenitor received Heaven’s mandate and established himself in the central lands; he then brought even the remotest regions into submission. Yueshang came to acknowledge his sovereignty. He regulated the sounds [?] and ordered the sacrifices—achievements perhaps unmatched even by Yu’s ordering of the land and Shun’s founding labors.
Successive sage rulers brought flourishing harmony; then our sagely Son of Heaven brought about a restoration, nurturing and warming all within and beyond the seas. Recently, through the cultivation of civil virtue, declarations of allegiance were elicited, and the tattooed peoples proved sincerely trustworthy [?]. His glorious accomplishment in ordering warfare [?] was recounted, while the patterns of human culture were further carved and polished, disseminated as canonical teachings on the method of governing the mind. These all convey the purport of the precarious human mind, the subtle moral mind, and the need for refinement and singleness of purpose. If Yi Yin and the Duke of Shao returned to life, I do not know how they would respond to and extol such beneficence…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也而况衣被雲漢之士優游
厭飫有不煥然而維新者乎
文不惟以地盛矣雖然文也
者爲經緯爲綱維爲軌憲斧
藻龍光均維弘濟布帛菽粟
民用莫先焉是故吾人之文
與天地帝王一也諸士子孕
===
殖於造化之勤而長育於
文治主司又以文進之其千載
一時矣將無毅然而已任者
乎昔者周禮在魯孔氏之徒
相與斟酌乎禮樂而論說乎
仁義故太史公涉汶泗觀鄒
嶧講射而歎焉以其非徒文
punctuated: 也。而况衣被雲漢之士，優游厭飫，有不煥然而維新者乎？文不惟以地盛矣。雖然，文也者，爲經緯，爲綱維，爲軌憲；斧藻龍光，均維弘濟；布帛菽粟，民用莫先焉。是故吾人之文，與天地帝王一也。諸士子孕殖於造化之勤，而長育於文治，主司又以文進之，其千載一時矣！將無毅然而已任者乎？昔者周禮在魯，孔氏之徒相與斟酌乎禮樂，而論說乎仁義。故太史公涉汶泗，觀鄒嶧講射而歎焉，以其非徒文
translation_en:
… And how much more so the scholars clothed in imperial radiance, who dwell at ease and partake of it to the full: could any fail to shine forth renewed? Literary culture flourishes not merely because of its locality. Yet literary culture provides the warp and weft, the guiding cords, and the standards of conduct; it embellishes imperial glory and serves to uphold and broadly benefit the world. Like cloth and grain, nothing takes precedence over it among the necessities of the people. Thus our literary culture is one with that of Heaven and Earth, emperors and kings.

You scholars have been conceived and nurtured through the diligent workings of creation and brought to maturity under civil governance. Now the presiding examiners advance you through your literary accomplishments: surely this is an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years! Will you not resolutely take this as your own responsibility [?]?

Formerly, the rites of Zhou survived in Lu. The disciples of Confucius together deliberated on rites and music and discoursed on benevolence and righteousness. Thus the Grand Astrologer, Sima Qian, crossed the Wen and Si rivers and observed instruction and ceremonial archery in Zou and Yi, sighing in admiration because these were more than mere literary embellishment…

translation_en: …so. How much more, then, must scholars clothed in the radiance of imperial grace, dwelling at ease and fully nourished by it, become resplendently renewed? Literary culture flourishes not merely because of its locality. Yet literary culture provides the warp and weft, the governing framework, and the standards and models; it embellishes imperial glory and brings broad assistance to all [?]. Like cloth, silk, beans, and grain, nothing takes precedence over it in serving the people's needs. Thus our literary culture is one with that of Heaven and Earth and of emperors and kings. These scholars have been nurtured through the tireless workings of creation and brought to maturity under civil governance; the presiding examiners further advance them through their literary accomplishments. This is indeed an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years! Will there not be those who resolutely take this as their own responsibility [?]? In former times, the rites of Zhou survived in Lu, and the followers of Confucius together weighed matters of ritual and music and discussed benevolence and righteousness. Thus the Grand Astrologer, Sima Qian, crossed the Wen and Si rivers, observed instruction in ritual archery in Zou and Yi, and expressed his admiration, because theirs was not merely literary culture…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也夫士之不爲徒文者必也
爲德行爲事業其進也必樹
績流聲必奮庸熈載爲先資
成信而不爲靜言而庸違者
三代之英由此其選也靜深
有徵文之慶矣而又懼夫文
之徒者將無以地重而爲治
===
化累故根極之以鄒魯之文
獻迪焉冀自今所謂豪傑者
必無負於地於時爲
朝家徵實用而主司亦庶乎塞
也維二三子交相成也其懋
圖之
江西撫州府儒學敎授潘靜
punctuated:
也。夫士之不爲徒文者，必也爲德行，爲事業。其進也，必樹績流聲，必奮庸熈載爲先，資成信，而不爲靜言而庸違者。三代之英，由此其選也。靜深有徵文之慶矣，而又懼夫文之徒者，將無以地重，而爲治化累。故根極之，以鄒魯之文獻迪焉，冀自今所謂豪傑者，必無負於地於時，爲朝家徵實用，而主司亦庶乎塞也。維二三子交相成也，其懋圖之！
江西撫州府儒學敎授潘靜。
translation_en:
…mere literary accomplishment. Scholars who do not confine themselves to literary accomplishment must cultivate virtuous conduct and undertake substantive work. When they advance into office, they must establish achievements and leave a lasting reputation, giving priority to exerting themselves in service and bringing their duties to fruition, providing support and establishing trust [?], rather than speaking fine words while acting contrary to them. It was on this basis that the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties were selected.
I, Jing, deeply rejoice in this gathering of literary talent, yet I also fear that those devoted merely to literary accomplishment will fail to bring distinction to their region and instead burden its governance and moral transformation. Thus I have explored the matter to its roots and guided them by the writings and worthies of Zou and Lu. I hope that henceforth those called outstanding men will fail neither their region nor their times, and will demonstrate practical usefulness to the imperial court; then those presiding over the examination may also come close to fulfilling their responsibility. You gentlemen must help one another achieve this. Strive earnestly toward it!
Pan Jing, Professor of the Confucian School of Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

江西撫州府儒學敎授潘靜

…Indeed, scholars who do not engage merely in literary ornament must devote themselves to virtuous conduct and practical achievement. When they advance into office, they must establish accomplishments and leave a lasting reputation; they must give priority to exerting their abilities and making public affairs flourish, drawing upon resources to establish trustworthiness [?], rather than speaking fine words while acting contrary to them. Pan Jing…， Instructor in the Confucian School of Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

text:
嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史楊以誠〔明夫江西宜春縣人戊戌進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使朱紈〔子純直隸長洲縣人辛巳進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政張鏊〔濟甫江西南昌縣人丙戌進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使屠大山〔國望浙江鄞縣人癸未進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事何元述〔元孝福建晉江縣人壬辰進士〕
===

江西撫州府儒學教授潘靜深〔時見貴州普安衛籍浙江桐鄉縣人丁酉貢士〕

河南汝寧府信陽州羅山縣儒學教諭陳英選〔資仕福建長樂縣人丁酉貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試。

translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, twenty-fifth year of Jiajing (1546).

Supervising Official:
Yang Yicheng, Investigating Censor on patrol in Guangdong, had the courtesy name Mingfu and was a native of Yichun County, Jiangxi. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuxu year.

Proctors:

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
曾子曰士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于天優優大哉禮
儀三百威儀三千
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
易
六二直方大不習无不利
凡益之道與時偕行
===

translation_en:
…are illustrious in carrying out their duties and possess a state.
Yue bowed and touched his forehead to the ground, saying: “I venture to acknowledge and extol the Son of Heaven’s gracious command.”
Some stars favor wind; some stars favor rain.
Formerly, the Duke of Zhou instructed and protected the myriad people, and the people cherished his virtue. Go, attend carefully to your office, follow its constant principles, and diligently make manifest the Duke of Zhou’s teachings; then the people will be well governed.

Book of Odes
In the south are trees with downward-curving branches; kudzu and other vines entwine them. Joyful is the noble lord; may blessings bring him peace. In the south are trees with downward-curving branches; kudzu and other vines cover them. Joyful is the noble lord; may blessings sustain him. In the south are trees with downward-curving branches; kudzu and other vines wind around them. Joyful is the noble lord; may blessings bring him fulfillment.
Tall grows that wormwood; the fallen dew glistens upon it. Having seen the noble lord, my heart is relieved. We feast, laugh, and converse; thus there is joy and repose.
Jade and precious jade adorn the lower and upper scabbard fittings of the ceremonial knife.
They reap with a swishing sound and pile the harvest in great heaps. These rise as high as walls and stand as closely together as the teeth of a comb.

異齊五味異和器械異制衣服異宜脩
===
其教不易其俗齊其政不易其宜
善教者使人繼其志
禮義立則貴賤等矣樂文同則上下和矣
好惡著則賢不肖別矣刑禁暴爵舉賢
則政均矣
故明乎其節之志以不失其事則功成而
德行立
第貳場
論
punctuated:
侯燬滅邢。〔僖公二十有五年〕
春，齊人執鄭詹。〔莊公十有七年〕
楚屈完來盟于師。〔僖公四年〕十有一月壬戌，晉侯及秦伯戰于韓。〔僖公十有五年〕
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。〔定公十年〕
禮記
凡居民材，必因天地寒煖燥濕，廣谷大川異制；民生其間者異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。脩其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。
善教者使人繼其志。
禮義立，則貴賤等矣；樂文同，則上下和矣；好惡著，則賢不肖別矣；刑禁暴，爵舉賢，則政均矣。
故明乎其節之志，以不失其事，則功成而德行立。
第貳場
論
translation_en:
…Marquis Hui of Wei destroyed Xing. 〔Twenty-fifth year of Duke Xi.〕
In spring, men of Qi seized Zhan of Zheng. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant at the army’s encampment. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 In the eleventh month, on the renxu day, the Marquis of Jin and the Earl of Qin fought at Han. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xi.〕
In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕

Book of Rites
Whenever settling people and assessing their capacities, one must take account of the cold and warmth, dryness and dampness of their environment, and the differing configurations of broad valleys and great rivers. People born among these have different customs. Their dispositions differ in firmness and gentleness, gravity and lightness, slowness and quickness; they blend the five flavors differently, fashion their implements differently, and find different clothing suitable. Refine their instruction without changing their customs; bring order to their government without changing what suits them.
Those skilled in teaching cause others to carry on their aspirations.
When ritual and righteousness are established, the noble and the lowly have their proper ranks. When the patterns of music are shared, superiors and inferiors are harmonious. When approval and disapproval are made clear, the worthy are distinguished from the unworthy. When punishments restrain violence and ranks elevate the worthy, government is equitable.
Thus, when the intent of the ritual’s successive stages is understood and its observances are not neglected, the undertaking is accomplished and virtuous conduct established.

Second Session
Discourse

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖高皇帝甫定天下留意帝王之學因宋濂
之請
令左右大書衍義揭之兩廡以代圖畫朝夕
諦觀當時指司馬遷所論而
令大臣條析觀鼂錯所言而與侍臣講論
聖謨洋洋具在典冊不識諸士子亦有聞歟我
皇上即位之後嘗
令侍從繙閱經書通鑑以資所聞維時輔臣
以經書微奧通鑑浩繁請以大學衍義
===
進講
皇上欣然嘉納因感賦五言古詩十韻
命二三輔臣先後賡和總而輯之名曰
翊學詩傳播中外久矣亦可得而揚其盛歟
聖子
神孫萬世相繼乃祇遹紹聞固有在也願詳述
之以為
聖學之助
問諸士讀經雖各占其一然諸經大要則
punctuated:
聖祖高皇帝甫定天下，留意帝王之學，因宋濂之請，令左右大書衍義，揭之兩廡，以代圖畫，朝夕諦觀。當時指司馬遷所論而令大臣條析，觀鼂錯所言而與侍臣講論。聖謨洋洋，具在典冊，不識諸士子亦有聞歟？我皇上即位之後，嘗令侍從繙閱經書、通鑑，以資所聞。維時輔臣以經書微奧、通鑑浩繁，請以大學衍義進講。皇上欣然嘉納，因感賦五言古詩十韻，命二三輔臣先後賡和，總而輯之，名曰《翊學詩》，傳播中外久矣，亦可得而揚其盛歟？聖子神孫，萬世相繼，乃祇遹紹聞，固有在也。願詳述之，以為聖學之助。

問：諸士讀經，雖各占其一，然諸經大要則
translation_en:
…our sagely progenitor, Emperor Gao, had only just pacified the realm when he turned his attention to the learning of emperors and kings. At Song Lian’s request, he ordered his attendants to write out the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) in large characters and display it in the two side galleries in place of paintings, so that he could study it attentively morning and evening. At that time, he would point to Sima Qian’s arguments and order his high ministers to analyze them point by point; he would read Chao Cuo’s statements and discuss them with his attendant officials. His abundant sagely counsels are fully preserved in the records. Have you candidates also heard of them?

After our emperor ascended the throne, he once ordered his attendant officials to consult the Classics and the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian) to supplement his knowledge. At that time, his assisting ministers, considering the Classics subtle and profound and the Comprehensive Mirror vast and voluminous, requested permission to lecture instead on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning. The emperor gladly accepted their proposal. Moved by the occasion, he composed an ancient-style poem in five-character lines with ten rhymes, and ordered several assisting ministers to compose matching poems in succession. These were gathered into a collection entitled Poems in Aid of Learning (Yixue shi), which has long circulated both within the court and beyond. Can you also expound upon this flourishing achievement? As sagely sons and divine grandsons succeed one another for ten thousand generations, there is assuredly a foundation here for reverently following and carrying forward the teachings they have received. Please explain this in detail, to assist imperial learning.

Question: Although each of you candidates specializes in one Classic in your studies, as for the essential purport of all the Classics…

translation_en:

At Song Lian’s request, he ordered his attendants to write out the Extended Meaning in large characters and display it in the two side galleries in place of paintings, so that he could study it attentively morning and evening. title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所當與聞者試舉一二商之易之分上
下經也先儒多求其故矣乃朱子則以
其簡帙重大故分之果爾則宜上下經
各三十二卦矣而多下經以四何哉元
儒豫章蕭氏乃爲讀易攷原謂上經一
卦不可增下經一卦不可减其說然歟
否歟可得而言歟書之分古今也今文
多艱深古文多平易古文果孔壁之舊
歟朱子則疑其序吳澄氏幷疑其書是
===
歟否歟或謂張霸僞爲或謂梅賾擬作
其然歟詩之有大小序自毛公以來未
之有議也而朱傳獨去之不知果能盡
得詩人之旨歟東萊吕氏畏服朱子者
也而讀詩記不從朱子而從毛氏亦何
歟春王正月春秋第一義也安國胡氏
則謂孔子以夏時冠周月不知周月其
可以夏時冠否也或謂周改月不改時
或謂時月皆改其說孰是歟周禮冬官
punctuated: 所當與聞者。試舉一二商之：《易》之分上下經也，先儒多求其故矣，乃朱子則以其簡帙重大，故分之。果爾，則宜上下經各三十二卦矣，而多下經以四，何哉？元儒豫章蕭氏乃爲《讀易攷原》，謂上經一卦不可增，下經一卦不可减，其說然歟，否歟？可得而言歟？《書》之分古今也，今文多艱深，古文多平易，古文果孔壁之舊歟？朱子則疑其序，吳澄氏幷疑其書，是歟，否歟？或謂張霸僞爲，或謂梅賾擬作，其然歟？《詩》之有大小序，自毛公以來未之有議也，而朱傳獨去之，不知果能盡得詩人之旨歟？東萊吕氏，畏服朱子者也，而《讀詩記》不從朱子而從毛氏，亦何歟？「春王正月」，《春秋》第一義也。安國胡氏則謂孔子以夏時冠周月，不知周月其可以夏時冠否也？或謂周改月不改時，或謂時月皆改，其說孰是歟？《周禮》冬官
translation_en:
…are matters of which you ought to have knowledge. Let us raise one or two for discussion. Earlier scholars have often sought the reason why the Book of Changes is divided into upper and lower sections. Master Zhu, however, held that it was divided because its bundles of writing slips were bulky and heavy. If that is so, each section should contain thirty-two hexagrams. Why, then, does the lower section contain four more than the upper? The Yuan scholar Xiao of Yuzhang wrote Investigating the Origins of the Book of Changes (Du Yi kaoyuan), arguing that not a single hexagram could be added to the upper section or removed from the lower. Is his explanation correct or not? Can you explain it?

As for the division of the Book of Documents into Old Text and New Text versions, the New Text is often difficult and obscure, while the Old Text is often plain and accessible. Is the Old Text truly the ancient text recovered from the wall of Confucius’s house? Master Zhu doubted its preface, while Wu Cheng doubted the text itself as well. Were they right or wrong? Some say that Zhang Ba forged it; others say that Mei Ze composed it in imitation of an ancient text. Is this so?

The Book of Odes has had its Greater and Lesser Prefaces, unchallenged, since the time of Master Mao. Yet Zhu’s commentary alone discarded them. Could it truly have fully grasped the poets’ intentions? Master Lü of Donglai revered and deferred to Master Zhu, yet his Notes on Reading the Book of Odes (Du Shi ji) followed Master Mao rather than Master Zhu. Why was this?

“Spring, the king’s first month” expresses the foremost principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Hu Anguo held that Confucius prefixed a season according to the Xia calendar to a month according to the Zhou calendar. But can a Zhou month be prefixed with a Xia season? Some say that the Zhou changed the numbering of the months but not the seasons; others say that they changed both seasons and months. Which explanation is correct? The Offices of Winter in the Rites of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之缺久矣吳澄氏謂冬官實在五官之
中而未嘗缺也儀禮之逸多矣取小戴
投壺奔喪等篇又取大戴明堂公符而
補之其說然歟否歟或謂三禮考註非
澄作亦有所據歟此皆千古不決之疑
其陳之尊經之學亮有定見也
問易曰聖人觀乎天文以察時變又曰君
子以治曆明時而箕子傳治法九章則
曰恊用五紀易書之旨果同揆歟說者
===
謂聖人恊用五紀其義有三可得聞歟
成周立馮相氏掌歲月日辰星之位辨
其敘事以會天位保章氏掌五物以詔
救政訪序事不知所謂歲月日辰星之
位當何所辨日月星辰之變當何所觀
歟星土九州當何所別十二歲之相五
雲之物十有二風當何所占歟堯謹曆
象舜察璣衡後世遂有宣夜周髀蓋天
渾天之術歷代增飾其法益精又有所
punctuated:
之缺久矣。吳澄氏謂冬官實在五官之中，而未嘗缺也。儀禮之逸多矣，取小戴投壺、奔喪等篇，又取大戴明堂、公符而補之，其說然歟，否歟？或謂三禮考註非澄作，亦有所據歟？此皆千古不決之疑，其陳之。尊經之學，亮有定見也。
問：易曰：「聖人觀乎天文，以察時變。」又曰：「君子以治曆明時。」而箕子傳治法九章，則曰：「恊用五紀。」易、書之旨，果同揆歟？說者謂聖人恊用五紀，其義有三，可得聞歟？成周立馮相氏，掌歲月日辰星之位，辨其敘事，以會天位；保章氏掌五物，以詔救政，訪序事。不知所謂歲月日辰星之位，當何所辨？日月星辰之變，當何所觀歟？星土九州，當何所別？十二歲之相、五雲之物、十有二風，當何所占歟？堯謹曆象，舜察璣衡，後世遂有宣夜、周髀、蓋天、渾天之術，歷代增飾，其法益精，又有所
translation_en:
…has long been missing. Wu Cheng maintained that the Offices of Winter were actually contained within the other five offices and had never been missing. Much of the Ceremonies and Rites has been lost. Is the proposal to supplement it with such chapters as “Pitch-pot” and “Hastening to the Funeral” from the Younger Dai’s Record of Rites, together with “Hall of Light” and “Gongfu” [?] from the Elder Dai’s Record of Rites, correct or not? Some say that the Examination and Annotations on the Three Ritual Classics was not written by Wu Cheng. Is there evidence for this claim as well? These are all doubts that have remained unresolved through the ages. Set forth your views on them. In your study devoted to honoring the classics, you surely have reached considered conclusions.
Question: The Book of Changes says, “The sage observes the patterns of Heaven to discern the changes of the seasons.” It also says, “The gentleman regulates the calendar and makes the seasons clear.” Yet when Jizi transmitted the nine divisions of the methods of government, he said, “Harmoniously employ the five measures of time.” Do the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents indeed share the same underlying principle? Commentators say that the sage’s harmonious employment of the five measures of time has three meanings. May we hear what these are? The Zhou established the office of Fengxiang, charged with the positions of the year, month, day, celestial stations, and stars, distinguishing their sequence in order to coordinate the celestial positions. The Baozhang officials were charged with five phenomena, using them to advise on remedial government measures and to investigate the ordering of affairs. Regarding these positions of the year, month, day, celestial stations, and stars, what distinctions should be made? What should be observed in the changes of the sun, moon, stars, and celestial stations? What distinctions should be drawn in assigning the Nine Provinces to celestial regions? What should be divined from the configurations of the twelve-year cycle, the appearances of the five kinds of clouds, and the twelve winds? Yao attended carefully to calendrical calculations and celestial phenomena; Shun examined the jeweled astronomical instrument and its transverse sighting tube. In later ages there consequently arose the astronomical methods of Xuanye, Zhoubi, Gaitian, and Huntian. Successive dynasties elaborated these, and their methods grew increasingly refined; there were also…

===

成周立馮相氏掌歲月日辰星之位辨
其叙事以會天位保章氏掌五物以詔
救政訪序事不知所謂歲月日辰星之
位當何所辨日月星辰之變當何所觀
歟星土九州當何所別十二歲之相五
雲之物十有二風當何所占歟堯謹曆
象舜察璣衡後世遂有宣夜周髀蓋天
渾天之術歷代增飾其法益精又有所
punctuated:
之缺久矣。吳澄氏謂冬官實在五官之中，而未甞缺也。儀禮之逸多矣，取小戴投壺、奔喪等篇，又取大戴明堂、公符而補之，其說然歟否歟？或謂三禮考註非澄作，亦有所據歟？此皆千古不决之疑，其陳之。尊經之學，亮有定見也。
問：易曰：「聖人觀乎天文，以察時變。」又曰：「君子以治曆明時。」而箕子傳治法九章，則曰：「恊用五紀。」易、書之旨，果同揆歟？說者謂聖人恊用五紀，其義有三，可得聞歟？成周立馮相氏，掌歲月日辰星之位，辨其叙事，以會天位；保章氏掌五物，以詔救政，訪序事。不知所謂歲月日辰星之位，當何所辨？日月星辰之變，當何所觀歟？星土九州，當何所別？十二歲之相、五雲之物、十有二風，當何所占歟？堯謹曆象，舜察璣衡，後世遂有宣夜、周髀、蓋天、渾天之術，歷代增飾，其法益精，又有所
translation_en:
…has long been missing. Wu Cheng maintained that the Offices of Winter were actually contained within the other five offices and had never been missing. Much of the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) has been lost. He took such chapters as “Pitch-Pot” and “Hastening to the Mourning Rites” from the Younger Dai’s collection, and also “Hall of Light” and “Gongfu” [?] from the Elder Dai’s collection, to supplement it. Is his account correct or not? Some say that Examination and Annotations of the Three Ritual Classics (Sanli kaozhu) was not written by Wu Cheng. Is there evidence for this too? These are all doubts that have remained unresolved through the ages. Set forth your views on them. In your study devoted to the classics, you surely have settled opinions.
Question: The Book of Changes says, “The sage observes the patterns of heaven to discern changes in the seasons.” It also says, “The gentleman regulates the calendar and clarifies the seasons.” Yet when Jizi transmitted the nine divisions of the methods of government, he spoke of “harmoniously employing the five reckonings.” Do the purposes of the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents indeed accord with the same principle? Commentators say that the sage’s harmonious employment of the five reckonings has three meanings. May we hear what these are? The Zhou established Astronomical Observers (Fengxiang shi), who were responsible for the positions of the year, month, day, celestial stations, and stars, distinguishing the sequence of their occurrences so as to correlate the positions in heaven. Astrologers (Baozhang shi) were responsible for the five phenomena, advising on remedial government measures and investigating the sequence of events. Regarding what are called the positions of the year, month, day, celestial stations, and stars, what should be distinguished? What should be observed in the changes of the sun, moon, and stars? What distinctions should be made in the correspondence between stellar regions and the territories of the Nine Provinces? What should be divined from the configurations of the twelve-year cycle, the appearances of clouds of the five colors, and the twelve winds? Yao attended carefully to calendrical calculations and celestial observations; Shun examined the armillary instruments. In later ages there arose the methods of Infinite Space (Xuanye), the Zhou Gnomon (Zhoubi), Canopy Heaven (Gaitian), and Spherical Heaven (Huntian). Successive dynasties elaborated these, and their methods became increasingly refined. There were also what were called…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
謂簡儀仰儀者不知孰有合於唐虞之
制歟三代之曆不可考自漢以來作曆
不同而最著者曰太初曰大衍然太初
法本於律大衍數起於易其義可得而
言歟元人郭守敬所制授時曆法或謂
其度越千古然歟否歟我
朝更制大統曆而積分猶授時之數何
聖人憲天立法不為殊術以改觀而猶仍勝國
之舊歟朱子謂古人曆法疎闊而差少
===
今曆法愈密而愈差以洪武中元統之
論攷之則今日之差愈甚矣玆欲考元
定法隨時協天平秩敬授以度民庸觀
象玩占以裨王政固帝王參贊化育之
首務也諸士抱負有年豈無有達象緯
之秘而通星曆之微者耶願究言之以
觀所蘊
問嶺南山川深鬱故其靈淑所鍾多瓌奇
豪雋之士自漢以下代不乏人有累徴
punctuated:
謂簡儀、仰儀者，不知孰有合於唐虞之制歟？三代之曆不可考，自漢以來作曆不同，而最著者曰太初、曰大衍。然太初法本於律，大衍數起於易，其義可得而言歟？元人郭守敬所制授時曆法，或謂其度越千古，然歟否歟？我朝更制大統曆，而積分猶授時之數，何聖人憲天立法，不為殊術以改觀，而猶仍勝國之舊歟？朱子謂古人曆法疎闊而差少，今曆法愈密而愈差。以洪武中元統之論攷之，則今日之差愈甚矣。玆欲考元定法，隨時協天，平秩敬授，以度民庸，觀象玩占，以裨王政，固帝王參贊化育之首務也。諸士抱負有年，豈無有達象緯之秘而通星曆之微者耶？願究言之，以觀所蘊。

問：嶺南山川深鬱，故其靈淑所鍾，多瓌奇豪雋之士。自漢以下，代不乏人，有累徴
translation_en:
…called the simplified instrument and the upward-facing instrument. Which of these accords with the institutions of Tang and Yu—the ages of Yao and Shun? The calendars of the Three Dynasties cannot be ascertained. Since the Han, calendars have been constructed in different ways, the most celebrated being the Grand Inception (Taichu) and Great Expansion (Dayan) calendars. Yet the methods of the Grand Inception calendar were based on the pitch standards, while the numbers of the Great Expansion calendar originated in the Book of Changes. Can the principles behind them be explained? Some say that the Season-Granting (Shoushi) calendrical system devised by Guo Shoujing of the Yuan surpassed all those of antiquity. Is this so or not? Our dynasty instituted the Grand Unification (Datong) calendar, yet its accumulated fractional values still follow the numbers of the Season-Granting calendar. Why did the sage ruler, in modeling himself on Heaven and establishing calendrical methods, retain the practices of the preceding dynasty instead of devising a different technique to give them a new appearance? Master Zhu said that ancient calendrical methods were rough but had few errors, whereas modern methods became ever more precise yet ever more erroneous. Judging by Yuan Tong’s discussion during the Hongwu reign, the discrepancies today are still greater. Now we wish to investigate the calendrical epoch and establish methods, adjusting them as time passes to accord with Heaven, properly ordering the seasons and reverently communicating them to the people so as to regulate their labors, and observing celestial phenomena and studying their portents to aid royal government. This is indeed the foremost duty of emperors and kings in assisting the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth. You scholars have cultivated your learning and aspirations for years: can there be none among you who comprehends the secrets of celestial configurations and understands the subtleties of astronomy and calendrical calculation? Please discuss these matters fully, so that we may see the learning you possess.

Question: Lingnan’s mountains and rivers are deep and luxuriant; thus, those in whom their numinous and beneficent influences gather are often men of extraordinary talent and outstanding ability. From the Han onward, no age has lacked such men. There were those who were repeatedly summoned…

…those called the simplified armillary instrument and the upward-looking instrument: which of them, one wonders, accords with the institutions of Tang and Yu? The calendars of the Three Dynasties cannot be ascertained. From the Han onward, methods of constructing calendars have differed, but the most celebrated are the Grand Inception Calendar (Taichu) and the Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan). Please discuss these matters fully, so that we may see the learning you possess.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不起太守奏旌其門者有教授於家寇
盜戒勿相犯者有獻金鑑錄著白羽扇
賦文章風度號爲賢相者有著中興自
治萬全策獻愚忠錄文章議論切中時
病者有莊宗出獵而叩馬諫者有真宗
東巡而獻賦頌者有排羣言宗孔子爲
韓愈所尊禮者有知品式通易學爲仁
宗所見知者有屢言邊情三使契丹者
有投匭論事南歸讀易者有進右丞相
===
不就而謚清獻者有爲時讒沮而謚忠
簡者有論王安石爲其鄉所推者有從
蘇軾爲其弟所稱者之數君子出處固
異制行亦殊其功業有崇卑文章有高
下不識可悉數而究言之歟迨至我
朝風氣日淳文物日盛衣冠禮樂之士蓋彬
彬倍昔而瓊海瓊崖黃雲紫水獨當元
氣之會今即其人而論之亦竊有可疑
者律已之嚴而不預名臣之數著述之
punctuated: 不起，太守奏旌其門者；有教授於家，寇盜戒勿相犯者；有獻《金鑑錄》、著《白羽扇賦》，文章風度號爲賢相者；有著《中興自治萬全策》、獻《愚忠錄》，文章議論切中時病者；有莊宗出獵而叩馬諫者；有真宗東巡而獻賦頌者；有排羣言、宗孔子，爲韓愈所尊禮者；有知品式、通易學，爲仁宗所見知者；有屢言邊情、三使契丹者；有投匭論事、南歸讀《易》者；有進右丞相不就而謚清獻者；有爲時讒沮而謚忠簡者；有論王安石，爲其鄉所推者；有從蘇軾，爲其弟所稱者。之數君子，出處固異，制行亦殊，其功業有崇卑，文章有高下，不識可悉數而究言之歟？迨至我朝，風氣日淳，文物日盛，衣冠禮樂之士蓋彬彬倍昔，而瓊海、瓊崖、黃雲、紫水獨當元氣之會。今即其人而論之，亦竊有可疑者：律已之嚴而不預名臣之數，著述之
translation_en:
… would not take office, and whose prefect memorialized the throne to have his gate honored; one who taught at home, whom bandits warned one another not to molest; one who presented the Record of the Golden Mirror and composed the Rhapsody on the White Feather Fan, whose literary accomplishments and bearing earned him renown as a worthy chief minister; one who wrote the Comprehensive Plan for Restoration and Self-Governance [?] and presented the Record of My Humble Loyalty, whose writings and arguments addressed precisely the maladies of his age; one who stopped Zhuangzong’s horse to remonstrate when the emperor went hunting; one who presented rhapsodies and eulogies when Zhenzong toured the east; one who rejected competing doctrines and took Confucius as his master, whom Han Yu respected and treated with courtesy; one who understood official grades and regulations and mastered the study of the Changes, whose worth Renzong recognized; one who repeatedly reported on frontier conditions and served three times as an envoy to the Khitan; one who submitted discussions of public affairs through the petition box and returned south to study the Changes; one who declined promotion to Grand Councilor of the Right and received the posthumous name Qingxian; one who was obstructed by contemporary slander and received the posthumous name Zhongjian; one who criticized Wang Anshi and was esteemed by his fellow countrymen; and one who followed Su Shi and was praised by Su Shi’s younger brother. These several gentlemen differed both in their decisions to serve or retire and in the ways they regulated their conduct. Their achievements were greater or lesser, and their writings higher or lower in quality. Might you enumerate them all and discuss them thoroughly?

By the time of our dynasty, prevailing customs grew daily more wholesome and cultural accomplishments daily more flourishing. Cultivated gentlemen versed in rites and music were perhaps twice as numerous as before, yet Qionghai, Qiongya, Huangyun, and Zishui were uniquely favored by the convergence of primordial vitality. Now, when considering these men individually, I venture to find points that invite questioning: strict as one was in disciplining himself, he was not included among the renowned ministers; as for the writings …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
富而不居理學之科其故何歟受皆一
之學而出處不同膺
優召之隆而受官不仕其意何歟其所謂功
業文章者又孰爲之軒輊歟諸士子居
其鄕論其世起思齊之念懷景行之心
則其講究必精而品評必當矣幸詳言
之觀所以尚友者
問廣東爲揚州要服限隔山海未易綏寧
趙佗自王即延祚滿百觀莊參之料韓
===
公之敗良不易歟伏波樓船雖幸成功
然動天下之力矣古謂用兵斯地者鮮
能大得志豈其然歟厥後有議罷徵發
而專任牧守者有議選經略使而可無
侵叛者有議雜用南北之兵而可永無
事者其說可復採而行之否歟我
國初永忠諸將略地至嶺表不勞餘力而悉
平豈
聖祖之烈將士之良自非尋常可比數歟迄今
punctuated:
富而不居理學之科，其故何歟？受皆一之學而出處不同，膺優召之隆而受官不仕，其意何歟？其所謂功業文章者，又孰爲之軒輊歟？諸士子居其鄕，論其世，起思齊之念，懷景行之心，則其講究必精，而品評必當矣。幸詳言之，觀所以尚友者。
問：廣東爲揚州要服，限隔山海，未易綏寧。趙佗自王，即延祚滿百。觀莊參之料、韓公之敗，良不易歟？伏波、樓船雖幸成功，然動天下之力矣。古謂用兵斯地者鮮能大得志，豈其然歟？厥後有議罷徵發而專任牧守者，有議選經略使而可無侵叛者，有議雜用南北之兵而可永無事者，其說可復採而行之否歟？我國初，永忠諸將略地至嶺表，不勞餘力而悉平，豈聖祖之烈、將士之良，自非尋常可比數歟？迄今
translation_en:
…prolific in writings, yet not ranked among scholars of the Learning of Principle: why was this? They received the teachings of Jieyi [?], yet differed in their decisions to serve or withdraw; they enjoyed the distinction of gracious imperial summonses, yet accepted office without serving. What were their intentions? As for their achievements and literary writings, how should their relative merits be assessed? You candidates dwell in their native region and discuss the age in which they lived. Inspired to equal their worth and cherishing admiration for their lofty conduct, you must have investigated them closely and judged them appropriately. Please explain in detail, so that we may see how you take the ancients as your friends.
Question: Guangdong lay within the outer tributary zone of Yangzhou, separated by mountains and seas, and was not easily pacified. Zhao Tuo proclaimed himself king, and his dynasty thereupon endured a full century. Considering Zhuang Can’s assessment and Lord Han’s defeat [?], was this not indeed a difficult undertaking? Although the General Who Subdues the Waves and the Towered-Ship General fortunately succeeded, they mobilized the resources of the entire realm. It was said in antiquity that those who campaigned in this region seldom fully achieved their aims. Was this indeed so? Subsequently, some proposed ending military levies and requisitions and entrusting responsibility entirely to local governors; some proposed selecting a Military Commissioner, thereby preventing incursions and rebellions; and some proposed employing troops from both north and south together, thereby securing lasting peace. Could these proposals be adopted and put into practice again? At the founding of our dynasty, Yongzhong and the other generals extended their conquests to Lingbiao and pacified the whole region without further exertion. Was this because the glorious might of our sagely founder and the excellence of his officers and soldiers were inherently beyond ordinary comparison? Down to the present…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
富而不居理學之科其故何歟受白沙
之學而出處不同膺
優召之隆而受官不仕其意何歟其所謂功
業文章者又孰爲之軒輊歟諸士子居
其鄕論其世起思齊之念懷景行之心
則其講究必精而品評必當矣幸詳言
之觀所以尚友者
問廣東爲揚州要服限隔山海未易綏寧
趙佗自王卽延祚滿百觀莊參之料韓
===
公之敗良不易歟伏波樓船雖幸成功
然動天下之力矣古謂用兵斯地者鮮
能大得志豈其然歟厥後有議罷徵發
而專任牧守者有議選經略使而可無
侵叛者有議雜用南北之兵而可永無
事者其說可復採而行之否歟我
國初永忠諸將略地至嶺表不勞餘力而悉
平豈
聖祖之烈將士之良自非尋常可比數歟迄今
punctuated:
富而不居理學之科，其故何歟？受白沙之學而出處不同，膺優召之隆而受官不仕，其意何歟？其所謂功業文章者，又孰爲之軒輊歟？諸士子居其鄕，論其世，起思齊之念，懷景行之心，則其講究必精而品評必當矣。幸詳言之，觀所以尚友者。

問：廣東爲揚州要服，限隔山海，未易綏寧。趙佗自王，卽延祚滿百，觀莊參之料、韓公之敗，良不易歟？伏波、樓船雖幸成功，然動天下之力矣。古謂用兵斯地者鮮能大得志，豈其然歟？厥後有議罷徵發而專任牧守者，有議選經略使而可無侵叛者，有議雜用南北之兵而可永無事者，其說可復採而行之否歟？我國初，永忠諸將略地至嶺表，不勞餘力而悉平，豈聖祖之烈、將士之良，自非尋常可比數歟？迄今
translation_en:
…abundant, yet not classified under the Learning of Principle: why was this? Having received Baisha’s teachings, why did he differ in his choice between entering service and remaining in retirement? Honored with a gracious imperial summons, he accepted an office but did not serve: what was his intention? As for what are called his achievements and writings, who could judge their relative merits? You examination candidates dwell in his native region and discuss the age in which he lived. Inspired to equal his virtue and cherishing admiration for his lofty conduct, you must surely have studied these matters closely and judged them fittingly. Please explain in detail, so that we may see how you seek friendship with the worthy men of the past.

Question: Guangdong belonged to the distant submission zone of Yangzhou, cut off by mountains and seas, and was not easily pacified. Zhao Tuo proclaimed himself king, and his dynasty then endured a full hundred years. Considering Zhuang Can’s assessment [?] and Lord Han’s defeat [?], was this indeed no easy task? Although the General Who Calms the Waves and the General of Towered Ships fortunately succeeded, they mobilized the resources of the entire realm. It was said in antiquity that those who campaigned in this region seldom fully achieved their aims. Was this indeed so? Subsequently, some proposed ending military levies and requisitions and entrusting affairs exclusively to the regional governors; some proposed selecting a Military Commissioner, arguing that incursions and rebellions could thereby be prevented; and some proposed combining troops from the north and south, arguing that lasting peace could thereby be secured. Could these proposals be adopted again and put into practice? At the founding of our dynasty, Yongzhong and the other generals extended their conquests to Lingbiao and pacified the whole region without expending further effort. Was this because the glorious achievements of our sagely founder and the excellence of his officers and soldiers were inherently beyond ordinary comparison? Down to the present…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
黠酋遺孽叛服不常近征討雖大克捷
然數年之後又未可知其他負險而幸
未逞者猶不少也豈果無經久之道一
勞而可永逸者歟又濱海諸郡番寇為
梗邇議轉募舟兵以為戰備方覺未便
亦豈無簡要之規可靖盜而安民者歟
是誠嶺表之積患也願聞所以經畫胥
圖一方久安之計
punctuated: 黠酋遺孽叛服不常，近征討雖大克捷，然數年之後又未可知。其他負險而幸未逞者，猶不少也。豈果無經久之道，一勞而可永逸者歟？又濱海諸郡，番寇為梗，邇議轉募舟兵以為戰備，方覺未便，亦豈無簡要之規，可靖盜而安民者歟？是誠嶺表之積患也，願聞所以經畫，胥圖一方久安之計。
translation_en: …the surviving remnants of the crafty chieftains alternate unpredictably between rebellion and submission. Although recent punitive expeditions have achieved great victories, what may happen after a few years remains uncertain. There are still many others who rely on difficult terrain and who, fortunately, have not yet succeeded in their designs. Is there truly no enduring course by which a single exertion could secure lasting peace? Furthermore, foreign raiders cause trouble in the coastal prefectures. A recent proposal to turn to recruiting naval troops for military preparedness is now proving impracticable. Is there likewise no simple and effective plan that could suppress the raiders and bring peace to the people? These are indeed longstanding afflictions of Lingbiao. We wish to hear how you would plan and manage these matters, devising together a strategy for lasting peace throughout the region.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
黠酋遺孽叛服不常近征討雖大克捷
然數年之後又未可知其他負險而幸
未逞者猶不少也豈果無經久之道一
勞而可永逸者歟又濱海諸郡番寇爲
梗邇議轉募舟兵以爲戰備方覺未便
亦豈無簡要之規可靖盜而安民者歟
是誠嶺表之積患也願聞所以經畫胥
圖一方久安之計
punctuated: 黠酋遺孽，叛服不常。近征討雖大克捷，然數年之後，又未可知。其他負險而幸未逞者，猶不少也。豈果無經久之道，一勞而可永逸者歟？又濱海諸郡，番寇爲梗，邇議轉募舟兵以爲戰備，方覺未便。亦豈無簡要之規，可靖盜而安民者歟？是誠嶺表之積患也。願聞所以經畫，胥圖一方久安之計。
translation_en: The surviving remnants of the crafty chieftains are inconstant in rebellion and submission. Although recent campaigns have achieved great victories, what may happen a few years hence remains uncertain. There are still quite a few others who rely on difficult terrain and whose designs have fortunately not yet been realized [?]. Is there truly no enduring method by which a single exertion could secure lasting peace? Moreover, foreign raiders trouble the coastal prefectures. Recently it was proposed to recruit naval troops instead as a preparation for war, but this is now proving impracticable. Is there likewise no simple and effective plan that could quell the raiders and bring peace to the people? These are indeed longstanding afflictions of Lingbiao, the region south of the mountain passes. We wish to hear how arrangements should be made, so that together we may devise a plan for the lasting peace of this region.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
曾子曰士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
謝頤
同考試官教諭陳批弘毅二字正指充養而
言此作精密渾融是能用心於內者
同考試官教諭吳批體認發揮深有醞藉
考試官教諭蕭批知學修辭無愧於士矣
考試官教授潘批理明辭純當是作者
===
大賢言士當入有所養以其大有所受也蓋任
重道遠則所受大矣然必弘毅爲之地焉此養
心之學不可以不大也曾子之意以爲天下之
情其示人以不廣者其居之必不寬而其謂已
爲不能者其爲之必不力而况士志於道而可
以易言哉弘毅其具矣弘也者以言乎其有容
也吾心本然之量其何有於不容而自私者每
狹之士則何可以狹也毅也者以言乎其有執
也吾心自然之能其何有於無執而自棄者恒
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
曾子曰：「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。」
謝頤

同考試官教諭陳批：「弘毅二字，正指充養而言。此作精密渾融，是能用心於內者。」
同考試官教諭吳批：「體認發揮，深有醞藉。」
考試官教諭蕭批：「知學修辭，無愧於士矣。」
考試官教授潘批：「理明辭純，當是作者。」

大賢言士當入有所養，以其大有所受也。蓋任重道遠，則所受大矣；然必弘毅爲之地焉。此養心之學，不可以不大也。曾子之意以爲：天下之情，其示人以不廣者，其居之必不寬；而其謂已爲不能者，其爲之必不力。而况士志於道，而可以易言哉？弘毅其具矣。弘也者，以言乎其有容也。吾心本然之量，其何有於不容？而自私者每狹之，士則何可以狹也？毅也者，以言乎其有執也。吾心自然之能，其何有於無執？而自棄者恒
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

Master Zeng said: “A scholar must be broad-minded and resolute: his burden is heavy, and his road is long.”
Xie Yi

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The two words ‘broad-minded’ and ‘resolute’ refer precisely to developing and nourishing oneself. This composition is meticulous and thoroughly integrated; its author knows how to direct his efforts inward.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Its understanding and exposition possess considerable depth and reserve.”

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “He understands learning and the cultivation of expression, and is worthy of being called a scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “The principles are clear and the language pure. Surely this is an accomplished writer.”

The great worthy says that a scholar must cultivate himself inwardly [?], because what he is entrusted with is great. For if the burden is heavy and the road long, then what he has undertaken is indeed great. Yet broad-mindedness and resolution must provide its foundation. This learning devoted to nourishing the mind must therefore be expansive. Master Zeng’s meaning is this: such is human nature that one who presents himself to others as lacking breadth will inevitably be confined in his outlook; and one who declares himself incapable [?] will inevitably exert little effort in what he does. How much more, then, does this apply to a scholar whose purpose is set upon the Way! Can he speak lightly of it? Broad-mindedness and resolution are the qualities he must possess.

Broad-mindedness refers to having the capacity to accommodate. Given the original breadth of our minds, what could there be that they cannot accommodate? Yet selfish people continually narrow that breadth. How, then, could a scholar allow himself to be narrow? Resolution refers to having steadfastness. Given the natural capacity of our minds, how could they lack steadfastness? Yet those who give up on themselves constantly…

第壹場
四書
曾子曰士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
謝頤
同考試官敎諭陳批弘毅二字正指充養而
言此作精鬯渾融是能用心於內者
同考試官敎諭吳批體認發揮深有醞籍
考試官敎諭蕭批知學修辭無愧於士矣
考試官敎授潘批理鬯辭純當是作者
===
大賢言士當大有所養以其大有所受也蓋任
重道遠則所受大矣然必弘毅爲之地焉此養
心之學不可以不大也曾子之意以爲天下之
情其示人以不廣者其居之必不寬而其謂已
爲不能者其爲之必不力而況士志於道而可
以易言哉弘毅其具矣弘也者以言乎其有容
也吾心本然之量其何有於不容而自私者每

第壹場

四書

曾子曰：「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。」

謝頤

同考試官敎諭陳批：「弘毅二字，正指充養而言。此作精鬯渾融，是能用心於內者。」

同考試官敎諭吳批：「體認發揮，深有醞籍。」

考試官敎諭蕭批：「知學修辭，無愧於士矣。」

考試官敎授潘批：「理鬯辭純，當是作者。」

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zengzi said: “A scholar must be broad-minded and resolute: his burden is heavy, and his road is long.”

Xie Yi

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The two words ‘broad-minded’ and ‘resolute’ refer precisely to developing and nurturing oneself. This composition is refined, lucid, and thoroughly integrated. Its author is someone capable of directing his efforts inward.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “His personal apprehension and exposition possess considerable depth and reserve.”

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “He understands learning and the refinement of expression; he is worthy of being called a scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “The reasoning is lucid and the language pure. Surely this is an accomplished writer.”

The great worthy says that a scholar must cultivate himself on a grand scale because what he takes upon himself is great. For when the burden is heavy and the road long, what one undertakes is indeed great; yet broad-mindedness and resolve must provide its foundation. Thus the learning through which one nurtures the mind must itself be great in scope. Zengzi’s meaning is this: in human affairs, those who present themselves as lacking breadth will surely lack spaciousness in how they conduct themselves; those who declare themselves incapable will surely fail to exert themselves fully in what they do. How much more does this apply to a scholar whose purpose is set upon the Way! Can he speak lightly of it? Broad-mindedness and resolve are the requisite capacities.

Broad-mindedness refers to one’s capacity to accommodate. Given the original measure of my mind, what could it fail to accommodate? Yet selfish people repeatedly narrow it. How, then, could a scholar allow himself to be narrow? Resolve refers to one’s capacity to hold firm. Given my mind’s natural ability, how could it lack the capacity to hold firm? Yet those who abandon themselves constantly…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
怠之士則何可以怠也是必尊德性也而廓然
存虛受之咸不使物欲得以隘吾度其斯以爲
弘也矣道問學也而奮然勵必爲之志不使安
肆得以勝吾强其斯以爲毅也矣夫士之所以
不可不弘毅者何哉爲其有體道之責焉耳是
故爲器重者舉之而莫能勝士則將舉其重器
而勝之者也非弘則物大而吾小負荷之非其
任故大心則能體天下之物而重可勝矣爲道
遠者行之而莫能致士則將行其遠道而致之
===
者也非毅則力竭而氣匱要約之無所歸故貞
固則能幹天下之事而遠可致矣毅而本之以
弘則近利非狃而耻於一善之安弘而出之以
毅則全體不息而自無半塗之廢此爲士者所
當自勉也知此則知所以爲學知所以爲學則
知所以爲士矣抑曾子非徒爲是言也蓋舉所
自得以詔人也曾子之學專用心於內弘毅蓋
其任道之本也故能唯一貫而得統於夫子可
謂勝重任而遠到矣樊遲之鄙何足語弘冉求
punctuated: 怠之，士則何可以怠也？是必尊德性也，而廓然存虛受之咸，不使物欲得以隘吾度，其斯以爲弘也矣；道問學也，而奮然勵必爲之志，不使安肆得以勝吾强，其斯以爲毅也矣。夫士之所以不可不弘毅者何哉？爲其有體道之責焉耳。是故爲器重者，舉之而莫能勝；士則將舉其重器而勝之者也。非弘則物大而吾小，負荷之非其任，故大心則能體天下之物，而重可勝矣。爲道遠者，行之而莫能致；士則將行其遠道而致之者也。非毅則力竭而氣匱，要約之無所歸，故貞固則能幹天下之事，而遠可致矣。毅而本之以弘，則近利非狃，而耻於一善之安；弘而出之以毅，則全體不息，而自無半塗之廢。此爲士者所當自勉也。知此則知所以爲學，知所以爲學則知所以爲士矣。抑曾子非徒爲是言也，蓋舉所自得以詔人也。曾子之學，專用心於內，弘毅蓋其任道之本也，故能唯一貫而得統於夫子，可謂勝重任而遠到矣。樊遲之鄙，何足語弘？冉求
translation_en: …make it indolent. How, then, can a scholar permit himself to be indolent? He must honor his moral nature, expansively preserving the open receptivity expressed by Xian (Influence), and not allowing material desires to narrow his capacity: this is how he becomes broad-minded. He must pursue inquiry and learning, vigorously strengthening his resolve to act, and not allowing ease and indulgence to overcome his strength: this is how he becomes resolute. Why must a scholar be broad-minded and resolute? Because he bears responsibility for embodying the Way. A heavy vessel may be lifted yet prove beyond one's strength to bear; the scholar, however, must lift that heavy vessel and bear it. Without breadth of mind, the object is great while the self is small, and one is unequal to carrying it. Thus, by enlarging the mind, one can embody all things under Heaven and bear the heavy burden. A distant road may be traveled yet its destination remain beyond reach; the scholar, however, must travel that distant road and reach its end. Without resolution, strength is exhausted and vital energy depleted, and efforts to gather things into a coherent whole find no ultimate grounding [?]. Thus, through steadfastness, one can manage the affairs of the world and reach the distant destination. When resolution is rooted in breadth of mind, one is not beguiled by immediate advantage and feels ashamed to rest content with a single good deed. When breadth of mind finds expression through resolution, the whole operates without ceasing, and one naturally avoids abandoning the journey halfway. This is what scholars must encourage themselves to achieve. Understanding this, one understands how to learn; understanding how to learn, one understands how to be a scholar. Moreover, Zengzi did not merely utter these words: he drew upon what he had personally grasped to instruct others. In his learning, Zengzi concentrated his attention on the inner self; breadth of mind and resolution were the foundation of his undertaking to uphold the Way. Thus he could assent to the teaching of the single unifying thread and receive its unifying principle from the Master. He may indeed be said to have borne a heavy charge and reached a distant destination. How could Fan Chi's narrowness qualify him to speak of breadth of mind? Ran Qiu…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
怠之士則何可以怠也是必尊德性也而廓然
存虛受之咸不使物欲得以隘吾度其斯以為
弘也矣道問學也而奮然勵必為之志不使安
肆得以勝吾强其斯以為毅也矣夫士之所以
不可不弘毅者何哉為其有體道之責焉耳是
故為器重者舉之而莫能勝士則將舉其重器
而勝之者也非弘則物大而吾小員荷之非其
任故大心則能體天下之物而重可勝矣為道
遠者行之而莫能致士則將行其遠道而致之
===
者也非毅則力竭而氣匱要約之無所歸故貞
固則能幹天下之事而遠可致矣毅而本之以
弘則近利非狃而耻於一善之安弘而出之以
毅則全體不息而自無半塗之廢此為士者所
當自勉也知此則知所以為學知所以為學則
知所以為士矣抑曾子非徒為是言也蓋舉所
自得以詔人也曾子之學專用心於內弘毅蓋
其任道之本也故能唯一貫而得統於夫子可
謂勝重任而遠到矣樊遲之鄙何足語弘冉求
punctuated: 怠之士，則何可以怠也？是必尊德性也，而廓然存虛受之咸，不使物欲得以隘吾度，其斯以為弘也矣；道問學也，而奮然勵必為之志，不使安肆得以勝吾强，其斯以為毅也矣。夫士之所以不可不弘毅者何哉？為其有體道之責焉耳。是故為器重者，舉之而莫能勝；士則將舉其重器而勝之者也。非弘，則物大而吾小，員荷之非其任。故大心則能體天下之物，而重可勝矣。為道遠者，行之而莫能致；士則將行其遠道而致之者也。非毅，則力竭而氣匱，要約之無所歸。故貞固則能幹天下之事，而遠可致矣。毅而本之以弘，則近利非狃，而耻於一善之安；弘而出之以毅，則全體不息，而自無半塗之廢。此為士者所當自勉也。知此則知所以為學，知所以為學則知所以為士矣。抑曾子非徒為是言也，蓋舉所自得以詔人也。曾子之學，專用心於內，弘毅蓋其任道之本也。故能唯一貫而得統於夫子，可謂勝重任而遠到矣。樊遲之鄙，何足語弘？冉求
translation_en: …a remiss scholar—how, then, could he permit himself to be remiss? He must honor his moral nature, broadly preserving an openness to receive [?], and not allowing material desires to narrow his capacity: this is how he becomes broad-minded. He must pursue inquiry and learning, resolutely strengthening his determination to act, and not allowing ease and self-indulgence to overcome his strength: this is how he becomes steadfast. Why must a scholar be both broad-minded and steadfast? Simply because he bears responsibility for embodying the Way. Thus, when a vessel is heavy, people lift it but cannot bear its weight; the scholar, however, is one who will lift that heavy vessel and bear it. Without breadth of mind, the thing is great while he himself is small, and bearing it [?] exceeds his capacity. Hence, by enlarging his mind, he can embrace the things of the world, and the heavy burden can be borne. When a road is long, people travel it but cannot reach its end; the scholar, however, is one who will travel that long road and reach its end. Without steadfastness, his strength is exhausted and his vital energy depleted, and his efforts at restraint [?] lead nowhere. Hence, through firm constancy he can carry out the affairs of the world, and the distant goal can be reached. When steadfastness is rooted in breadth of mind, he is not beguiled by immediate gain and is ashamed to rest content with a single good deed. When breadth of mind is expressed through steadfastness, his whole being works unceasingly, and he naturally avoids abandoning his undertaking halfway. This is what scholars should urge themselves to achieve. Understanding this, one understands how to pursue learning; understanding how to pursue learning, one understands how to be a scholar. Moreover, Zengzi did not merely utter these words: he offered what he had himself attained in order to instruct others. In his learning, Zengzi concentrated his efforts within; breadth of mind and steadfastness were the foundation of his undertaking to uphold the Way. Thus he could apprehend the single thread running through it all and receive the unified teaching from the Master. He may indeed be said to have borne a heavy responsibility and reached a distant goal. With Fan Chi’s narrowness, how could one speak of breadth of mind? Ran Qiu…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之盡何足語教無怪乎傳道者之不多見也矣
洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于天優優大哉禮
儀三百威儀三千
巖文輔
同考試官學正呂批道為天地人物之紀洋
洋優優正言道之所以大處子思之意為學者立
本此篇發揮真切而歸重于凝道之功錄之
考試官教諭蕭批詞意明鬯不襲塵語
考試官教授潘批清雅可誦
===
中庸論聖人之道至大而至精也夫與天而為
一可謂至大矣體物而不遺可謂至精矣不有
以見聖人之道之大乎中庸二十七章先言聖
人之道以發君子之學也蓋謂道必有所寄體
於人而盡於聖人者也故以其道之極於至大
者言之夫道流動充滿洋洋焉耳矣生長收藏
天之用本如是也而高明覆物道與之同其用
故知化而天焉昭焉陰陽和而萬物皆得性命
正而百昌咸遂則聖人之道歸焉耳穹窿覆幬
punctuated:
之盡，何足語教？無怪乎傳道者之不多見也矣。

洋洋乎！發育萬物，峻極于天。優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千。

巖文輔

同考試官學正呂批：「道為天地人物之紀，洋洋優優，正言道之所以大處。子思之意，為學者立本。此篇發揮真切，而歸重于凝道之功，錄之。」

考試官教諭蕭批：「詞意明鬯，不襲塵語。」

考試官教授潘批：「清雅可誦。」

中庸論聖人之道至大而至精也。夫與天而為一，可謂至大矣；體物而不遺，可謂至精矣。不有以見聖人之道之大乎？中庸二十七章，先言聖人之道，以發君子之學也。蓋謂道必有所寄，體於人而盡於聖人者也。故以其道之極於至大者言之，夫道流動充滿，洋洋焉耳矣。生長收藏，天之用本如是也；而高明覆物，道與之同其用。故知化而天焉昭焉，陰陽和而萬物皆得，性命正而百昌咸遂，則聖人之道歸焉耳。穹窿覆幬
translation_en:
…his exhaustion [?]—how could it suffice to speak of teaching? No wonder transmitters of the Way are so seldom seen.

“How vast and abundant! It nurtures the myriad things and reaches to the height of Heaven. How ample and great! Three hundred rules of ceremony and three thousand rules of deportment.”

Yan Wenfu 巖文輔

Comment by Associate Examiner Lü, School Instructor: “The Way is the ordering principle of Heaven, Earth, human beings, and things. ‘Vast and abundant’ and ‘ample’ describe precisely wherein the Way is great. Zisi’s intention is to establish a foundation for learners. This essay develops that meaning with sincerity and precision, placing the principal emphasis on the work of firmly embodying the Way. Selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Xiao, School Instructor: “The wording and meaning are lucid and fluent, without borrowing stale expressions.”

Comment by Examiner Pan, Prefectural School Instructor: “Refined and elegant, worthy of recitation.”

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way of the sage as supremely great and supremely subtle. To be one with Heaven may indeed be called supremely great; to embody all things without leaving anything out may indeed be called supremely subtle. Does this not reveal the greatness of the sage’s Way? Chapter twenty-seven of the Doctrine of the Mean first speaks of the sage’s Way in order to elucidate the learning of the gentleman. Its meaning is that the Way must have something in which to reside: it is embodied in human beings and finds its fullest realization in the sage. These are attributable to the sage’s Way. The arching vault that overspreads and shelters…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之畫何足語敎無怪乎傳道者之不多見也矣
洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于天優優大哉禮
儀三百威儀三千
嚴文輔
同考試官學正呂批道為天地人物之紀洋
洋優優正言道之所以大處子思之意為學者立
本此篇發揮真切而歸重于凝道之功錄之
考試官敎諭蕭批詞意明鬯不襲塵語
考試官敎授潘批清雅可誦
===
中庸論聖人之道至大而至精也夫與天而為
一可謂至大矣體物而不遺可謂至精矣不有
以見聖人之道之大乎中庸二十七章先言聖
人之道以發君子之學也蓋謂道必有所寄體
於人而盡於聖人者也故以其道之極於至大
者言之夫道流動充滿洋洋焉耳矣生長收藏
天之用本如是也而高明覆物道與之同其用
故知化而天焉昭焉陰陽和而萬物皆得性命
正而百昌咸遂則聖人之道歸焉耳穹窿覆幬
punctuated:
之畫，何足語敎？無怪乎傳道者之不多見也矣。

「洋洋乎！發育萬物，峻極于天。優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千。」
嚴文輔

同考試官學正呂批：「道為天地人物之紀，洋洋優優，正言道之所以大處。子思之意，為學者立本。此篇發揮真切，而歸重于凝道之功，錄之。」
考試官敎諭蕭批：「詞意明鬯，不襲塵語。」
考試官敎授潘批：「清雅可誦。」

中庸論聖人之道，至大而至精也。夫與天而為一，可謂至大矣；體物而不遺，可謂至精矣。不有以見聖人之道之大乎？中庸二十七章先言聖人之道，以發君子之學也。蓋謂道必有所寄，體於人而盡於聖人者也。故以其道之極於至大者言之，夫道流動充滿，洋洋焉耳矣。生長收藏，天之用本如是也；而高明覆物，道與之同其用。故知化而天焉昭焉，陰陽和而萬物皆得，性命正而百昌咸遂，則聖人之道歸焉耳。穹窿覆幬
translation_en:
…such delineation [?]—how could it suffice to speak of teaching? No wonder those who transmit the Way are so seldom seen.

“How vast! It brings forth and nurtures the myriad things and rises loftily to Heaven. How ample and great! There are three hundred rules of ceremony and three thousand rules of deportment.”

Associate Examiner Lü, School Rector, comments: “The Way is the ordering principle of Heaven, Earth, human beings, and all things. ‘Vast’ and ‘ample’ speak precisely of what makes the Way great. Zisi’s intention is to establish a foundation for learners. This essay expounds the meaning with authenticity and precision, placing the emphasis on the effort to bring the Way to full realization. Selected for inclusion.”

Examiner Pan, School Professor, comments: “Clear and elegant, worthy of recitation.”

This, then, is where the sage’s Way finds its consummation. The vaulted expanse, overarching and sheltering…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天之體本如是也而高明配天道與之同其體
故盡性而天為參焉神無聲臭而一理為之貫
通道無際涯而兩間為之充塞則聖人之道極
焉耳若然則斯道也其大無外所謂天下莫能
載焉者此矣又以其道之入於至小者言之夫
道充足有餘優優焉耳矣立經制而總綱維之
要是禮儀也舉其凡則三百而道無乎不在用
之朝廷邦國而人道羣達之閨門鄉黨而彝倫
敘有本有文而禮不為虛器也致委曲而盡節
===
目之詳是威儀也極其數則三千而道無乎不
該周旋裼襲節文之而不忒升降上下範圍之
而不過至精至密而禮不為粗迹也若然則斯
道也其小無內所謂天下莫能破焉者此矣夫
語大遺小語小遺大則道有不備矣兼小大而
一之非聖道之大而能若是乎嘗論之聖人者
道之管也乃君子則與道為二必有希聖之功
而後有凝道之德夫聖人曷可希也吾德性所
賦與聖人一而已故尊吾德性而學之所以希
punctuated:
天之體本如是也，而高明配天，道與之同其體，故盡性而天為參焉。神無聲臭，而一理為之貫通；道無際涯，而兩間為之充塞，則聖人之道極焉耳。若然，則斯道也，其大無外，所謂天下莫能載焉者此矣。又以其道之入於至小者言之，夫道充足有餘，優優焉耳矣。立經制而總綱維之要，是禮儀也；舉其凡則三百，而道無乎不在。用之朝廷邦國而人道羣，達之閨門鄉黨而彝倫敘，有本有文，而禮不為虛器也。致委曲而盡節目之詳，是威儀也；極其數則三千，而道無乎不該。周旋裼襲，節文之而不忒；升降上下，範圍之而不過。至精至密，而禮不為粗迹也。若然，則斯道也，其小無內，所謂天下莫能破焉者此矣。夫語大遺小，語小遺大，則道有不備矣。兼小大而一之，非聖道之大而能若是乎？
嘗論之：聖人者，道之管也；乃君子則與道為二，必有希聖之功，而後有凝道之德。夫聖人曷可希也？吾德性所賦，與聖人一而已。故尊吾德性而學之，所以希
translation_en:
…Such is Heaven’s fundamental form. Lofty and luminous, matching Heaven, the Way shares its form; thus, by fully realizing his nature, the sage becomes a partner of Heaven. Spiritual activity has neither sound nor scent, yet a single principle runs through it; the Way has neither boundary nor limit, yet fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Here the Way of the sage reaches its utmost extent. If this is so, this Way is so great that nothing lies outside it. This is what is meant by saying that nothing under Heaven can contain it.
Consider, in turn, how this Way enters into the smallest things. The Way is abundantly sufficient, ample and inexhaustible. Establishing enduring institutions and gathering together the essentials of their governing framework: these are the rites of ceremony. Their main divisions number three hundred, and the Way is present in every one. Applied in the court and the states, they bring human relations together [?]; extended into households and local communities, they put the constant human relationships in order. Having both substance and patterned expression, ritual is no empty vessel. Attending to every subtle particular and exhausting the detail of every provision: these are the rules of deportment. Their full number is three thousand, and the Way embraces them all. Turning and moving, baring or covering one’s garment, are regulated with fitting distinctions, without error; ascending and descending, moving above and below, are bounded by rules, without excess. Utterly refined and exact, ritual is no mere coarse outward trace. If this is so, this Way is so minute that nothing lies within it. This is what is meant by saying that nothing under Heaven can divide it further. If speaking of the great leaves out the small, or speaking of the small leaves out the great, the account of the Way is incomplete. Could it embrace both small and great and unite them in this fashion without the greatness of the sagely Way?
I have reflected on this: the sage is the conduit [?] of the Way, whereas the gentleman remains distinct from it. Only through the work of aspiring to sagehood can he acquire the virtue that brings the Way to fulfillment. How, then, can one aspire to become a sage? The moral nature with which I am endowed is simply one with that of the sage. Thus, honoring my moral nature and pursuing learning is the means by which to aspire to…

translation_en:
…Heaven’s essential constitution is inherently thus. In loftiness and clarity, the Way matches Heaven and shares its essential constitution. Thus, by fully realizing one’s nature, one becomes like Heaven and participates alongside it. Spiritual efficacy has neither sound nor smell, yet a single principle runs through it; the Way has neither limit nor boundary, yet it fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Here the Way of the sage reaches its utmost extent. If so, this Way is so great that nothing lies outside it. This is what is meant by saying that nothing under Heaven can contain it.

To speak further of how this Way enters into the smallest things: the Way is amply sufficient, with abundance to spare. Establishing enduring institutions and bringing together the essentials of their governing framework—these are the ceremonial rites. Enumerated in their main divisions, they number three hundred, and nowhere among them is the Way absent. Applied at court and in the states, they unite people in the human Way; extended to the inner household and the local community, they bring the constant human relationships into order. Having both a foundation and outward refinement, ritual is no empty vessel. Attending to every subtle particular and exhausting the details of its provisions—these are the rules of dignified deportment. Fully enumerated, they number three thousand, and there is nothing the Way does not embrace. Turning and moving, uncovering and covering one’s garment: ritual regulates and refines these actions so that they do not err. Ascending and descending, moving up and down: ritual sets their bounds so that they do not exceed them. Utterly fine and exact, ritual is no mere crude outward form. If so, this Way is so small that nothing lies within it. This is what is meant by saying that nothing under Heaven can split it.

To speak of the great while omitting the small, or of the small while omitting the great, would leave the Way incomplete. Could it embrace both small and great and unite them in this fashion without the greatness of the sagely Way? I have considered this: the sage is the conduit of the Way, whereas the gentleman remains distinct from it. Only through the effort of aspiring to sagehood can he attain the virtue through which the Way is fully realized. How, then, may one aspire to become a sage? The moral nature with which I am endowed is simply the same as that of the sage. Thus, honoring my moral nature and pursuing learning is the means by which to aspire…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也德修道凝不異於聖人矣若曰聖本生知非
學可至則違道遠矣所以君子貴自勉也
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
郭敬賢
同考試官教諭黃批題本承上起下蓋聲振
二字即含蓄聖智二義作者漫以始終條理牽繞
可厭獨是篇體認傳註發揮明白故錄以式
考試官教諭蕭批純正
考試官教授潘批典實
===
大賢明乎樂之備者而揭其要於二音焉蓋金
聲玉振大成之樂明矣不揭言之何以喻聖之
爲大乎孔子所以異於三子者如此且夫人有
大聖樂有大成不觀其深則擬倫有未至也何
也蓋一樂之奏而眾音以成故成矣必謂之大
也眾音之成而一樂以備故大矣又謂之集焉
若是者豈其萃眾和而遺節奏之妙包羣美而
失綱紀之宜也蓋八音之中有定屬焉惟金以
聲之乎蓋洪以亮者金也而聲則金之職也金
punctuated:
也。德修道凝，不異於聖人矣。若曰聖本生知，非學可至，則違道遠矣。所以君子貴自勉也。

集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。
郭敬賢

同考試官教諭黃批：題本承上起下，蓋聲振二字即含蓄聖智二義。作者漫以始終條理牽繞，可厭。獨是篇體認傳註，發揮明白，故錄以式。
考試官教諭蕭批：純正。
考試官教授潘批：典實。

大賢明乎樂之備者，而揭其要於二音焉。蓋金聲玉振，大成之樂明矣。不揭言之，何以喻聖之爲大乎？孔子所以異於三子者如此。且夫人有大聖，樂有大成，不觀其深，則擬倫有未至也。何也？蓋一樂之奏，而眾音以成，故成矣，必謂之大也；眾音之成，而一樂以備，故大矣，又謂之集焉。若是者，豈其萃眾和而遺節奏之妙，包羣美而失綱紀之宜也？蓋八音之中有定屬焉，惟金以聲之乎？蓋洪以亮者金也，而聲則金之職也。金
translation_en:
…With virtue cultivated and the Way firmly realized, one is no different from a sage. If one says that sages are inherently born with knowledge and that their attainment cannot be reached through learning, one strays far from the Way. This is why the gentleman values exerting himself.

“To bring together the great accomplishment is to sound the bronze bells and conclude with the jade chimes.”
Guo Jingxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: The topic connects what precedes with what follows. The two words “sound” and “conclude” already contain the two meanings of sagehood and wisdom. Writers tediously entangle their arguments in the orderly arrangement of beginnings and endings. This essay alone grasps the commentaries and expounds them clearly; therefore it is recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: Pure and correct.
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: Grounded in the classics and substantial.

The great worthy understood what makes music complete and disclosed its essentials in two sounds. With the sounding of bronze bells and the concluding resonance of jade chimes, music’s great accomplishment becomes clear. Without explicitly bringing this out, how could he illustrate the greatness of the sage? This is how Confucius differs from the three masters.

Now, among men there is the great sage, and in music there is the great accomplishment. Unless one examines their depths, the analogy between them will fall short. Why is this? In the performance of a musical work, the many sounds together accomplish it; thus, although it is an accomplishment, it must be called “great.” Through the accomplishment of the many sounds, a single musical work becomes complete; thus, although it is great, it is further described as “bringing together.” Could such music gather all harmonies yet omit the subtlety of rhythm, or encompass every beauty yet lose the proper ordering of its guiding structure?

Among the eight categories of musical instruments, each has its assigned role. Is it not bronze alone that sounds the opening? For bronze has a sound both full and clear, and sounding the opening is its office. Bronze…

… Thus, with virtue cultivated and the Way firmly established, one is no different from a sage. If one says that sages inherently possess knowledge from birth and that their attainment cannot be reached through learning, one departs far from the Way. This is why the gentleman prizes exerting himself.

“To bring together the great completion is to sound the bronze bells and conclude with the jade chimes.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: The topic carries forward what precedes and introduces what follows. The two words “sound” and “conclude” implicitly contain the two meanings of sagehood and wisdom. Writers tediously entangle themselves in the orderly arrangement of beginnings and endings. Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: Pure and correct.
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: Grounded in the classics and substantial.

The great worthy understood how music achieves completeness and brought out its essentials through two sounds. With the sounding of bronze bells and the concluding jade chimes, the music of great completion becomes clear. Without explicitly bringing this out, how could he illustrate the greatness of the sage? Why is this? When a piece of music is performed, its many sounds achieve completion. Thus, although it is complete, that completion must be called “great.” Through the completion of its many sounds, a whole piece of music becomes fully realized. Thus, although it is great, it is also said to be “brought together.” Could such music gather its many harmonies yet neglect the subtlety of rhythm, or encompass its manifold beauties yet lose the proper ordering of its framework? Among the eight classes of musical instruments, each has its appointed role. Is it not bronze that sounds the opening? Bronze is sonorous and clear, and sounding the opening is its function. title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以聲之則鬱者宣之而使達隱者洩之而使光
蓋一音鏘然而眾音之精華於是乎呈露矣又
惟玉以振之乎蓋清以越者玉也而振則玉之
能也玉以振之則渙者翕之而使專紛者凝之
而使固蓋一音詘然而眾音之美實於是乎斂
藏矣於其聲也若眾音未知而啓以知也其陽
一噓而萬物皆春乎於其振也若眾音未能而
翼以能也其陰一吸而萬物皆秋乎蓋向非金
聲則不能相宰而其失也靡向非玉振則不能
===
相成而其失也流亦何取乎大成也哉吁此金
石所以爲重而聲振又大成之要與可以觀樂
亦可以觀聖人矣雖然又即樂而評焉三子一
音耳不得爲大成猶未爲無成也蓋亞於大成
者矣使季札聽之其在齊陳之間乎乃孔子則
韶矣惜乎位之不舜也故曰韶盡美矣又盡善
也而聽之三月不知肉味其志可知也於乎大
成不可作矣而聖智未爲無所寓也固萬世之
金聲玉振也善學者毋自瞶焉可矣
punctuated: 以聲之，則鬱者宣之而使達，隱者洩之而使光。蓋一音鏘然，而眾音之精華於是乎呈露矣。又惟玉以振之乎？蓋清以越者玉也，而振則玉之能也。玉以振之，則渙者翕之而使專，紛者凝之而使固。蓋一音詘然，而眾音之美實於是乎斂藏矣。於其聲也，若眾音未知而啓以知也，其陽一噓而萬物皆春乎？於其振也，若眾音未能而翼以能也，其陰一吸而萬物皆秋乎？蓋向非金聲，則不能相宰，而其失也靡；向非玉振，則不能相成，而其失也流。亦何取乎大成也哉？吁！此金石所以爲重，而聲振又大成之要與！可以觀樂，亦可以觀聖人矣。雖然，又即樂而評焉，三子一音耳，不得爲大成，猶未爲無成也，蓋亞於大成者矣。使季札聽之，其在齊陳之間乎？乃孔子則韶矣，惜乎位之不舜也。故曰：「韶盡美矣，又盡善也。」而聽之三月不知肉味，其志可知也。於乎！大成不可作矣，而聖智未爲無所寓也，固萬世之金聲玉振也。善學者毋自瞶焉可矣。
translation_en:
…when it sounds them, what is pent up is released and made to flow freely; what is hidden is disclosed and made manifest. With one ringing note, the finest qualities of all the tones are thus revealed. And is it not jade alone that brings them to their conclusion? For jade is pure and far-reaching in sound, and bringing the performance to its conclusion is its capacity. When jade concludes them, it gathers what is dispersed and makes it concentrated; it consolidates what is confused and makes it firm. With one subdued note [?], the beauty and substance of all the tones are thus gathered and stored within. When the bronze sounds, it is as though the tones did not yet know, and it opened them to knowledge. Is this not like a single exhalation of yang bringing spring to all things? When the jade concludes, it is as though the tones were not yet capable, and it aided them in becoming capable. Is this not like a single inhalation of yin bringing autumn to all things? Without the sounding bronze, the tones could not be governed together, and their failing would be laxity; without the concluding jade, they could not complete one another, and their failing would be uncontrolled flow. What claim, then, could there be to great consummation?

Ah! This is why metal and stone instruments carry such weight, and why the sounding commencement and resonant conclusion are essential to great consummation! Through this one may understand music, and also the sage. Nevertheless, to judge once more through music, the three masters each represent only a single tone. Though they cannot constitute great consummation, they are still not without accomplishment: they rank just below great consummation. Had Ji Zha heard them, might he have placed them somewhere between the music of Qi and Chen? Confucius, however, would be the Shao music. Alas that his position was not that of Shun! Thus he said, “The Shao is perfectly beautiful and also perfectly good.” Having heard it, he did not know the taste of meat for three months: from this his aspiration can be understood.

Alas! The master of great consummation cannot be called forth again, yet his sagely wisdom is not without a repository. It is indeed the sounding bronze and concluding jade for all ages. Those who learn well need only refrain from making themselves deaf to it.
