title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則相業顯君子謂律已之嚴著述之富當
時大臣無出其右者明問乃疑其不預名
臣之列居理學之科議者謂相軋而隙也
言者譁然遂指所爲悼亡等作而訾之不
知陶靖節之閒情賦亦不足爲靖節病而
是非得失君子固有辨也邇有輯近代名
臣言行錄者固已指而白之則濬之遺論
已定矣烏足爲病耶獻章家居作詩談道
自樂閉門讀書輟夜不寢始求之博曰雜
===
矣又求之靜曰偏矣其訓人也曰去耳目
支離之用全虛靈不測之神又曰不離日
用之間而見鳶飛魚躍之妙君子謂主靜
之功自得之學近世諸儒無出其右者明
問獨疑其出處不同受官不仕不知與弼
以布衣膺聘而獻章卒業國學需選天曹
况其章疏所陳有始終願仕之說此所以
拜官而不辭卒之乞歸終養歲有徵辟皆
謝病不行則雖曰願仕而未必仕也邇有
punctuated:
則相業顯。君子謂律已之嚴、著述之富，當時大臣無出其右者。明問乃疑其不預名臣之列，居理學之科，議者謂相軋而隙也。言者譁然，遂指所爲悼亡等作而訾之。不知陶靖節之《閒情賦》亦不足爲靖節病，而是非得失，君子固有辨也。邇有輯《近代名臣言行錄》者，固已指而白之，則濬之遺論已定矣，烏足爲病耶？
獻章家居，作詩談道自樂，閉門讀書，輟夜不寢。始求之博，曰：「雜矣。」又求之靜，曰：「偏矣。」其訓人也，曰：「去耳目支離之用，全虛靈不測之神。」又曰：「不離日用之間，而見鳶飛魚躍之妙。」君子謂主靜之功、自得之學，近世諸儒無出其右者。明問獨疑其出處不同，受官不仕。不知與弼以布衣膺聘，而獻章卒業國學，需選天曹。况其章疏所陳，有始終願仕之說，此所以拜官而不辭。卒之乞歸終養，歲有徵辟，皆謝病不行，則雖曰願仕，而未必仕也。邇有
translation_en:
…his achievements as grand secretary were distinguished. Gentlemen maintained that no high minister of his day surpassed Qiu Jun in the rigor of his self-discipline or the abundance of his writings. Your enlightened question nevertheless raises doubts about his exclusion from the ranks of eminent ministers and his placement in the category of scholars of principle; commentators attributed this to mutual antagonism and estrangement. Critics raised an outcry, pointing to his poems mourning his deceased wife and other works to disparage him. They did not understand that even Tao Jingjie’s Rhapsody on Stilling the Passions was insufficient grounds for finding fault with him. Gentlemen certainly distinguish right from wrong, merit from failing. Recently, a compiler of the Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Ministers of Recent Times has already identified and clarified this matter. The judgment passed down concerning Jun is thus settled. How could this suffice to discredit him?
Chen Xianzhang lived at home, finding pleasure in composing poetry and discussing the Way. He shut his door to study, remaining awake through the night [?]. At first he sought understanding through breadth of learning, but said, “It is too miscellaneous.” Then he sought it through stillness, but said, “It is one-sided.” In teaching others, he said, “Discard the fragmented functioning of ears and eyes, and preserve whole the empty, numinous, unfathomable spirit.” He also said, “Without departing from everyday activities, perceive the wonder of kites flying and fish leaping.” Gentlemen maintained that among the Confucian scholars of recent times, none surpassed him in the practice of making stillness central or in learning attained through personal realization. Your enlightened question particularly questions the inconsistency of his taking office and withdrawing: he accepted an appointment but did not serve. Yet Wu Yubi received an invitation to serve while a commoner, whereas Xianzhang had completed his studies at the Directorate of Education and awaited selection by the Ministry of Personnel. Moreover, his memorials declared that he had wished to serve throughout. This explains why he accepted appointment rather than declining it. In the end, however, he requested leave to return home and care for his parent for the remainder of her life. Though summonses to office came year after year, he invariably pleaded illness and did not go. Thus, although he expressed a wish to serve, he would not necessarily do so. Recently there has been…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
輯理學名臣言行錄者亦嘗表而論之則
獻章之志可見矣烏足為疑耶是二君子
其出處亦殊制行亦異文章功業吾又何
敢軒輊之然濬之功業在輔弼著述在天
下莫不家傳而人習之則發揮理學之功
多矣獻章不立功業不為著述然鼓舞天
下之士莫不嚮慕而景從之則講明理學
之功多矣雖然數君子者尚矣未之能行
也乃所願竊有進於是孟子曰以友天下
===
之善士為未足又尚論古之人是故學必
以孔孟為的仕必以伊呂為準則取法髙
立志大趨向正模範端雖未必為孔孟伊
呂也庶幾守洙泗之遺矩竊鄒魯之耿光
而莘野渭濱之風視之嶺海有間矣雖然
竊有志焉而未逮也執事弗以為嘐嘐而
進教之幸甚
第五問
陳玉成
punctuated:
輯理學名臣言行錄者，亦嘗表而論之，則獻章之志可見矣，烏足為疑耶？是二君子，其出處亦殊，制行亦異，文章功業，吾又何敢軒輊之？然濬之功業在輔弼，著述在天下，莫不家傳而人習之，則發揮理學之功多矣。獻章不立功業，不為著述，然鼓舞天下之士，莫不嚮慕而景從之，則講明理學之功多矣。雖然，數君子者尚矣，未之能行也，乃所願竊有進於是。孟子曰：「以友天下之善士為未足，又尚論古之人。」是故學必以孔孟為的，仕必以伊呂為準，則取法髙，立志大，趨向正，模範端。雖未必為孔孟伊呂也，庶幾守洙泗之遺矩，竊鄒魯之耿光，而莘野渭濱之風，視之嶺海有間矣。雖然，竊有志焉，而未逮也。執事弗以為嘐嘐，而進教之，幸甚。

第五問
陳玉成
translation_en:
…those who compiled the Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Ministers of the Learning of Principle also singled this out for discussion. Xianzhang’s intentions are therefore plain to see. How could this warrant doubt? These two gentlemen differed both in their decisions to serve or withdraw and in their conduct. How would I dare rank their literary achievements and public accomplishments? Yet Jun’s public accomplishments lay in assisting the sovereign, and his writings circulated throughout the realm, transmitted in every household and studied by everyone. His contribution to expounding the Learning of Principle was therefore great. Xianzhang established no public achievements and composed no writings, yet he inspired the scholars of the realm, who all admired him and followed his example. His contribution to elucidating the Learning of Principle was therefore great.

Nevertheless, these gentlemen are worthy of esteem, and I have not yet been able to put their example into practice; yet my private aspiration reaches further still. Mengzi said: “Finding it insufficient to befriend the good scholars of the whole realm, one goes further back to consider the men of antiquity.” Thus, in learning one must take Kongzi and Mengzi as one’s target, and in office one must take Yi Yin and Lü Shang as one’s standard. Then one’s chosen examples will be lofty, one’s resolve great, one’s direction correct, and one’s models upright. Although one may not necessarily become a Kongzi, Mengzi, Yi Yin, or Lü Shang, one may hope to preserve the inherited rules of the Zhu and Si rivers and partake of the enduring radiance of Zou and Lu. The exemplary spirit of the fields of Shen and the banks of the Wei stands apart from that of Linghai. Nevertheless, although I privately aspire to this, I have not attained it. If you, honored sir, do not regard these words as boastful, but offer me further instruction, I shall be most fortunate.

Fifth Question
Chen Yucheng

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正吕批廣東民患惟山猺海寇
爲甚子機要之說確乎有見必平日究心於時務
者末復以治人治法爲言深諒子之惓惓矣
考試官教諭蕭批有議論有經制且俱妥
帖可行吾將占子爲有用之才不獨以其文也
考試官教授潘批說經久簡要處讀之如
指諸掌是可見之施爲者錄之
善撫夷者握其機而已矣善禦寇者執其
要而已矣何謂機動之而不得不行驅之
===
而不得不從是也何謂要事舉而不見其
敝民利而不見其害是也機不得則終古
無良圖不有以致之孰從而應之要不得
則目前之近利雖欲以安之適所以擾之
而已矣寧何補耶然此非強之以所不堪
也植其紀不易其俗修其備不貽其害民
夷之從之也易矣兵法曰因其勢而利導
之機與要之謂也撫夷禦寇之略其在茲
乎執事發策重以東粤積患爲念期與經
punctuated:
同考試官學正吕批：廣東民患，惟山猺海寇爲甚。子機要之說，確乎有見，必平日究心於時務者。末復以治人治法爲言，深諒子之惓惓矣。
考試官教諭蕭批：有議論，有經制，且俱妥帖可行。吾將占子爲有用之才，不獨以其文也。
考試官教授潘批：說經久簡要處，讀之如指諸掌，是可見之施爲者，錄之。
善撫夷者，握其機而已矣；善禦寇者，執其要而已矣。何謂機？動之而不得不行，驅之而不得不從，是也。何謂要？事舉而不見其敝，民利而不見其害，是也。機不得，則終古無良圖；不有以致之，孰從而應之？要不得，則目前之近利，雖欲以安之，適所以擾之而已矣，寧何補耶？然此非強之以所不堪也。植其紀，不易其俗；修其備，不貽其害，民夷之從之也易矣。《兵法》曰：「因其勢而利導之。」機與要之謂也。撫夷禦寇之略，其在茲乎？執事發策，重以東粤積患爲念，期與經
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Lü, School Instructor: Of the afflictions suffered by the people of Guangdong, the mountain Yao and maritime raiders are the gravest. Your discussion of the critical means and essential principles shows genuine insight. You must be someone who regularly gives careful thought to current affairs. At the end, you return to the subject of those who govern and the methods of government; I fully appreciate your earnest concern.

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: There is reasoned argument and there are institutional arrangements, all sound and practicable. I would judge you to possess talents useful in service, and not merely on the strength of your writing.

Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: Where you discuss enduring measures concisely and directly, reading it makes the matter as clear as pointing to one’s own palm. These proposals can be put into practice. Select this essay for inclusion.

Those skilled at pacifying non-Han peoples need only grasp the critical means; those skilled at defending against raiders need only hold fast to the essentials. What are the critical means? They are such that, when you move people to act, they cannot but act, and when you direct them, they cannot but comply. What are the essentials? They are such that measures are carried out without attendant abuses, and the people benefit without suffering harm. Without grasping the critical means, there will never be a sound plan. Unless there is a way to bring people over, who will comply and respond? Without grasping the essentials, even immediate advantages, intended to bring people peace, will serve only to trouble them. What benefit could there possibly be?

Yet this does not mean forcing upon them what they cannot bear. Establish order among them without changing their customs; improve defensive preparations without bringing harm upon them. Then it will be easy for the common people and non-Han peoples to comply. The Art of War says: “Follow the circumstances and guide them advantageously.” This refers to the critical means and the essentials. Does not the strategy for pacifying non-Han peoples and defending against raiders lie here? In setting this policy question, you, honored examiners, have given particular thought to the longstanding afflictions of eastern Yue, hoping together to devise [?] …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
畫以圖久安甚盛心也愚鄕人也聞見矜
矣私憂而過計之者亦久矣請敬陳之竊
惟東粤古揚州外徼也自今言之土沃民
阜穀饒賦薄視諸省謂非一樂土哉但嶺
海限隔疆域自分故漢之囂佗嘗有自爲
一州之議佗據之卽啓百年之祚文帝方
且置之度外撫以溫言要惟視彼爲未易
與故也自後徭獞諸種叛服不常每厪征
討伺便則非時虜掠失利則深窟潜藏蒐
===
薙多方莫可蹤跡信乎鮮能大得志矣今
聲敎文明已無愧中土然形勢險阻固自
猶昔是以黠酋遺孽竄伏崇巘每爲中郡
之殃番盜巨憝出沒溟渤時肆濱海之擾
誠如所策執事欲爲經畫之計而參諸往
古之猷就其所言亦皆切中當時之事但
今古異勢事變異宜恐難例論取其善者
而師其意焉可也韓千秋之見挫於吕嘉
果如莊參之料然以二千人而遽欲得志
punctuated: 畫以圖久安，甚盛心也。愚鄕人也，聞見矜矣，私憂而過計之者亦久矣。請敬陳之。竊惟東粤，古揚州外徼也。自今言之，土沃民阜，穀饒賦薄，視諸省，謂非一樂土哉？但嶺海限隔，疆域自分，故漢之囂佗嘗有自爲一州之議。佗據之，卽啓百年之祚。文帝方且置之度外，撫以溫言，要惟視彼爲未易與故也。自後徭獞諸種，叛服不常，每厪征討。伺便則非時虜掠，失利則深窟潜藏，蒐薙多方，莫可蹤跡，信乎鮮能大得志矣。今聲敎文明，已無愧中土，然形勢險阻，固自猶昔。是以黠酋遺孽竄伏崇巘，每爲中郡之殃；番盜巨憝出沒溟渤，時肆濱海之擾。誠如所策。執事欲爲經畫之計，而參諸往古之猷，就其所言，亦皆切中當時之事。但今古異勢，事變異宜，恐難例論。取其善者而師其意焉，可也。韓千秋之見挫於吕嘉，果如莊參之料，然以二千人而遽欲得志
translation_en:
…to devise plans for lasting peace: this is a most noble intention. I am a native of this region, humble and limited in what I have heard and seen [?]. For a long time I have privately worried about it and pondered it, perhaps excessively. Allow me respectfully to set forth my views.

I submit that eastern Yue, Guangdong, was anciently an outer frontier of Yangzhou. Speaking of it today, its soil is fertile, its people prosperous, its grain plentiful, and its taxes light. Compared with the other provinces, could it not be called a land of happiness? Yet mountains and sea form barriers, naturally setting its territory apart. Thus, under the Han, Xiao and Tuo [?] once discussed making it a region unto itself. Tuo occupied it and thereby founded a ruling house that endured a hundred years. Emperor Wen even left it outside his immediate concerns and soothed it with kindly words, essentially because he regarded it as no easy opponent.

Thereafter, the various Yao and Zhuang groups alternated unpredictably between rebellion and submission, repeatedly necessitating punitive expeditions. When opportunities presented themselves, they raided and took captives at unexpected times; when they suffered reverses, they concealed themselves deep in caves. Many methods were used to hunt them down and root them out, yet their tracks could not be found. Truly, few campaigns achieved any substantial success.

Today, the civilizing influence of imperial rule and the region’s cultural refinement need yield nothing to the central lands. Its difficult and defensible terrain, however, remains as it was of old. Hence cunning chieftains and surviving rebel bands hide among lofty peaks, repeatedly bringing calamity upon the inland prefectures; foreign pirates and great malefactors appear and disappear upon the seas, periodically disturbing the coast. Matters are indeed as your policy question describes.

You wish to devise plans and consult the strategies of antiquity. The measures you mention did indeed address the circumstances of their own times precisely. Yet circumstances differ between past and present, and changing affairs require different measures. I fear it is difficult to discuss them as equivalent cases. It is appropriate to select what is good in them and emulate their underlying intent. Han Qianqiu’s defeat at the hands of Lü Jia did indeed accord with Zhuang Can’s prediction; yet to seek immediate success with only two thousand men…

translation_en:
…plans to secure lasting peace: this is a most generous intention. I am a native of this region, and what I have heard and seen is [?]. For a long time I have privately worried about it and pondered it, perhaps excessively. Allow me respectfully to set out my views. I submit that eastern Yue was anciently an outlying frontier of Yangzhou. Speaking of its present condition, its soil is fertile, its people prosperous, its grain abundant, and its taxes light. Compared with the other provinces, could it be called anything but a land of contentment? Yet mountains and sea cut it off, giving it boundaries of its own. Thus, in Han times, Ren Xiao and Zhao Tuo once discussed making it a province unto itself. Once Tuo occupied it, he established a ruling house that lasted a hundred years. Emperor Wen even left it outside his concerns and soothed it with kindly words, chiefly because he considered it no easy opponent to contend with. Thereafter, the various Yao and Zhuang peoples alternated unpredictably between rebellion and submission, repeatedly necessitating punitive expeditions. When opportunities arose, they raided and plundered at irregular times; when they suffered reverses, they hid deep in caves. Despite searches by many means [?], their tracks could not be found. Truly, few could achieve any great success against them.
Today, the civilizing influence of imperial instruction and the flourishing of culture here are already worthy of the central lands. Yet the terrain remains as rugged and inaccessible as before. Thus, the surviving followers of crafty chieftains lurk among lofty peaks, repeatedly bringing calamity upon the interior commanderies; foreign pirates and great malefactors appear and disappear upon the ocean, periodically wreaking havoc along the coast. It is indeed as your policy question states. You wish to devise plans for managing this situation by consulting the strategies of antiquity. The proposals you cite all addressed the circumstances of their own times precisely. But circumstances differ between antiquity and the present, and changing affairs demand different measures. I fear that they cannot readily be judged by the same precedents. It would suffice to select what is good in them and follow their underlying intent. Han Qianqiu’s defeat at the hands of Lü Jia was indeed as Zhuang Can had foreseen. Yet to seek immediate success with only two thousand men…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
良率易矣其取敗宜也博德輩之收功於
南海足洗千秋之辱然以天下全力而從
事一方甚勞瘁矣其取勝無可稱也此皆
無關於勝敗之數者也永和間李固欲阻
四州徵發之役故有專任牧守之議開陳
反覆利害較然荊揚兗豫之徵並從報罷
而祝良張喬卒以成功州郡之可任其效
著矣但今郡縣事權之寄法非漢比直以
責成烏足辦此是固之議未可盡通於今
===
者也然境內之事何者非守令之責力之
可為者任之可也仁宗時宋祁欲止北人
嶺外之戍故有南北雜用之論因時調停
非為定說其謂歲留北兵五千人分屯要
害募土人為鄉軍百人給北兵三十以勁
弩利兵佐之俟其出掠一大斬獲則兵威
自張是亦兵家之略但北人不勝炎瘴多
生疾疫去家太遠人情奚堪是宋祁之論
不必復講於今者也然南人止習戈矛不
punctuated:
良率易矣，其取敗宜也。博德輩之收功於南海，足洗千秋之辱；然以天下全力而從事一方，甚勞瘁矣，其取勝無可稱也。此皆無關於勝敗之數者也。永和間，李固欲阻四州徵發之役，故有專任牧守之議。開陳反覆，利害較然，荊、揚、兗、豫之徵並從報罷，而祝良、張喬卒以成功。州郡之可任，其效著矣。但今郡縣事權之寄，法非漢比，直以責成，烏足辦此？是固之議未可盡通於今者也。然境內之事，何者非守令之責？力之可為者，任之可也。
仁宗時，宋祁欲止北人嶺外之戍，故有南北雜用之論。因時調停，非為定說。其謂歲留北兵五千人，分屯要害，募土人為鄉軍，百人給北兵三十，以勁弩利兵佐之。俟其出掠，一大斬獲，則兵威自張，是亦兵家之略。但北人不勝炎瘴，多生疾疫，去家太遠，人情奚堪？是宋祁之論不必復講於今者也。然南人止習戈矛，不
translation_en:
…was indeed rash; his defeat was only to be expected. The success achieved by Bode and his fellows in Nanhai was sufficient to wipe away Qianqiu’s humiliation. Yet directing the full strength of the empire against a single region entailed immense toil, and their victory merits no praise. None of these cases bears on the principles governing victory and defeat.
During the Yonghe reign period, Li Gu sought to prevent the mobilization of troops from four regions and therefore proposed entrusting responsibility exclusively to regional inspectors and commandery governors. He explained the matter at length, making the advantages and disadvantages clear. The proposed levies from Jing, Yang, Yan, and Yu were all canceled in accordance with his recommendation, and Zhu Liang and Zhang Qiao ultimately achieved success. This clearly demonstrated that regional and commandery authorities could be entrusted with the task. Today, however, the statutory powers entrusted to prefectural and county officials are not comparable to those under the Han. How could merely holding them responsible for results suffice to accomplish this? Thus Li Gu’s proposal cannot be applied in its entirety today. Nevertheless, what affair within their jurisdictions is not the responsibility of prefects and magistrates? They may properly be entrusted with whatever lies within their power.
During Emperor Renzong’s reign, Song Qi sought to end the garrison service of northerners beyond the Ling mountains, and therefore advocated employing northerners and southerners together. This was an accommodation to the circumstances of the time, not a fixed doctrine. He proposed retaining five thousand northern soldiers each year, stationing them at strategic points, and recruiting local men into local militia units. For every hundred local men, thirty northern soldiers would be assigned to support them with powerful crossbows and sharp weapons. Once the enemy came out to plunder, a single substantial success in killing and capturing them would naturally establish the army’s prestige. This, too, was a military strategy. Yet northerners could not endure the heat and miasma and often fell ill from epidemics. So far from home, how could they bear it? Thus Song Qi’s proposal need not be taken up again today. Nevertheless, southerners are trained only in dagger-axes and spears and do not …

…Liang acted rashly [?], so his defeat was to be expected. The success achieved by Bode and his fellows in Nanhai was enough to wash away the disgrace of a thousand years. Yet concentrating the entire strength of the realm on operations in a single region was exceedingly exhausting; their victory merits no praise. Yet southerners are practiced only in handling dagger-axes and spears, and are not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
善弓矢益以此人之長技亦制寇之一策
也此皆所謂師其意焉者也獨韓愈氏有
專責經略使之請蓋一方之重臣也即今
提督之設非其官耶邇幸
聖天子簡命得人平蠻累捷封川柳州相繼寧
輯矣昔
國初之有事於百粵也廖永中則整旅東趨
楊璟則陳師西伐所在破竹兵不血刃兩
廣悉平會兵奏凱此誠所謂大得志者而
===
戡定之績今復著焉則我
聖祖之啓運開基
皇上之中興振武英略神功後先相輝映矣然
執事猶爲未盡之憂更求經久之道以撫
山徭簡要之規以禦海寇此體國之長慮
也敢以所謂機與要者告焉夫今之山徭
寧矣而愚固與執事之憂者何也蓋徭之
寧者暫也而不寧者其常也誅殺之後不
久復集山谷使然奚怪耶封川諸邑雖平
punctuated:
善弓矢，益以此人之長技，亦制寇之一策也。此皆所謂師其意焉者也。獨韓愈氏有專責經略使之請，蓋一方之重臣也。即今提督之設，非其官耶？邇幸聖天子簡命得人，平蠻累捷，封川、柳州相繼寧輯矣。昔國初之有事於百粵也，廖永中則整旅東趨，楊璟則陳師西伐，所在破竹，兵不血刃，兩廣悉平，會兵奏凱。此誠所謂大得志者，而戡定之績今復著焉，則我聖祖之啓運開基、皇上之中興振武，英略神功，後先相輝映矣。
然執事猶爲未盡之憂，更求經久之道以撫山徭、簡要之規以禦海寇，此體國之長慮也。敢以所謂機與要者告焉。夫今之山徭寧矣，而愚固與執事之憂者，何也？蓋徭之寧者暫也，而不寧者其常也。誅殺之後，不久復集，山谷使然，奚怪耶？封川諸邑雖平
translation_en:
…skilled with bows and arrows; supplementing them with these men's particular skills [?] is also one means of subduing the bandits. These are all instances of what is meant by following the underlying intent of earlier proposals. Han Yu alone proposed that sole responsibility be assigned to the Military Commissioner, a high official entrusted with a whole region. Is not the present office of Supreme Commander precisely such an office? Fortunately, the sage Son of Heaven has recently selected and appointed suitable men. They have won repeated victories in pacifying the non-Han peoples, and Fengchuan and Liuzhou have successively been restored to order. Formerly, at the beginning of the dynasty, when military operations were undertaken in the lands of the Hundred Yue, Liao Yongzhong marshaled his troops and advanced eastward, while Yang Jing arrayed his forces and campaigned westward. Wherever they went, resistance broke like split bamboo, and their blades were not bloodied. Both Guang provinces were entirely pacified, and the armies united to celebrate victory. This was truly what is called fully achieving one's aims. Now achievements in conquest and pacification are manifest once again. Thus the heroic strategies and divine accomplishments of our sagely founding ancestor, who inaugurated the dynastic mandate and laid its foundations, and of His Majesty, who has brought about a restoration and reinvigorated military power, illuminate one another across the generations.
Yet you remain concerned about what has not been fully accomplished, and further seek enduring means of pacifying the mountain Yao and concise, essential measures for resisting maritime bandits. This is farsighted concern for the affairs of the state. I venture to set before you what I regard as the critical opportunities and essential points. The mountain Yao are now at peace; why, then, do I in my humble view still share your concern? Because their peace is temporary, while unrest is their usual condition. After punitive killings, they soon gather again: the mountain valleys make this possible, so why be surprised? Although Fengchuan and the other counties have been pacified…

translation_en:
…skilled with bows and arrows, supplemented by the particular skills of northerners: this too is one strategy for subduing the raiders. These are all instances of what is meant by emulating the underlying intent. Han Yu alone proposed placing sole responsibility upon a Military Commissioner, a high official entrusted with the affairs of a whole region. Does the present appointment of a Supreme Commander not correspond to that office? Recently, fortunately, our sagely Son of Heaven has selected the right man for this charge. Repeated victories have been won in pacifying the southern peoples, and Fengchuan and Liuzhou have successively been restored to peace. Wherever they went, resistance broke like split bamboo, and their blades went unstained with blood. Both Guangdong and Guangxi were entirely pacified, and the armies joined to announce their triumph. This is farsighted concern born of devotion to the state. I venture to explain what I mean by the crucial opportunity and the essential measures. The mountain Yao are now at peace; why, then, do I nevertheless share your concern? Because peace among the Yao is temporary, whereas unrest is their usual condition. After punitive killing, they soon gather again: the mountain valleys make this possible, so why should it be surprising? Although Fengchuan and the other counties have been pacified…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或不能保於數年之後況羅傍瀧水諸盜
方眾且强幸其未逞耳征之常不足撫之
則有餘其機惟在設土官以統之而已矣
凡舊設之地不惟猺不爲殃且其精銳每
爲
國家用設官之利彰彰明矣今之爲患於郡
邑者皆散處之猺僅數十人各爲一羣而
叢處耳苟視其地之大小以爲官之崇卑
取眾酋中素所信服者授之而卽使盡有
===
其地慰撫長巡無不可者諸酋若不服從
則天兵助而征之其勢必歸於一也蓋以
朝廷威福臨之如粤西土官之制永無征討
之勞而反獲其用則亦何憚而不爲哉甞
有病此者則曰其酋不應命也殊不知加
以名號而他無可欲者以利之則是虛名
雖榮約束徒擾何爲而願之哉果如所處
則以
國家之力爲之驅廣土眾民必人情之所欲
punctuated: 或不能保於數年之後，況羅傍瀧水諸盜方眾且强，幸其未逞耳。征之常不足，撫之則有餘，其機惟在設土官以統之而已矣。凡舊設之地，不惟猺不爲殃，且其精銳每爲國家用。設官之利，彰彰明矣。今之爲患於郡邑者，皆散處之猺，僅數十人各爲一羣而叢處耳。苟視其地之大小，以爲官之崇卑，取眾酋中素所信服者授之，而卽使盡有其地，慰撫長巡，無不可者。諸酋若不服從，則天兵助而征之，其勢必歸於一也。蓋以朝廷威福臨之，如粤西土官之制，永無征討之勞，而反獲其用，則亦何憚而不爲哉？甞有病此者，則曰其酋不應命也。殊不知加以名號，而他無可欲者以利之，則是虛名雖榮，約束徒擾，何爲而願之哉？果如所處，則以國家之力爲之驅廣土眾民，必人情之所欲
translation_en:
…perhaps their security cannot be assured a few years hence. How much more is this so when the bandits of Luobang and Longshui are now numerous and strong: we are merely fortunate that they have not yet run rampant. Military campaigns against them are always inadequate, whereas pacification would more than suffice. The key lies simply in appointing native officials to govern them. Wherever such offices were established previously, the Yao not only cease to cause harm, but their picked warriors are also frequently employed by the state. The benefits of establishing these offices are abundantly clear. Those now causing trouble in the prefectures and counties are all scattered Yao, clustered in separate bands of only a few dozen people each. If official ranks were graded according to the size of their territories, and those among the chiefs whom the people have long trusted and obeyed were selected for appointment and immediately granted possession of the entire territory, there would be nothing impracticable about comforting, pacifying, and maintaining oversight of them [?]. If other chiefs refused to submit, imperial troops would assist the appointed chiefs in campaigning against them, and the circumstances would inevitably bring them under a single authority. By exercising the court’s power to punish and reward them, following the system of native officials in western Guangxi, we would forever be spared the toil of punitive campaigns and instead obtain their services. What, then, should make us hesitate to do this?

Some have objected to this proposal, saying that the chiefs would not accept appointment. They utterly fail to understand that if we confer titles upon them but offer no other desirable benefits, then, however glorious these empty titles may be, the restrictions imposed would merely trouble them. Why would they want this? If matters were indeed arranged as proposed, the power of the state would be used to secure extensive lands and numerous subjects for them [?], something human nature would surely desire…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或不能保於數年之後况羅傍瀧水諸盜
方衆且強幸其未逞耳征之常不足撫之
則有餘其機惟在設土官以統之而已矣
凡舊設之地不惟猺不爲殃且其精銳每
爲
國家用設官之利彰彰明矣今之爲患於郡
邑者皆散處之猺僅數十人各爲一羣而
叢處耳苟視其地之大小以爲官之崇卑
取衆酋中素所信服者授之而卽使盡有
===
其地慰撫長巡無不可者諸酋若不服從
則天兵助而征之其勢必歸於一也蓋以
朝廷威福臨之如粤西土官之制永無征討
之勞而反獲其用則亦何憚而不爲哉甞
有病此者則曰其酋不應命也殊不知加
以名號而他無可欲者以利之則是虛名
雖榮約束徒擾何爲而願之哉果如所處
則以
國家之力爲之驅廣土衆民必人情之所欲
punctuated: 或不能保於數年之後，况羅傍瀧水諸盜方衆且強，幸其未逞耳。征之常不足，撫之則有餘，其機惟在設土官以統之而已矣。凡舊設之地，不惟猺不爲殃，且其精銳每爲國家用，設官之利彰彰明矣。今之爲患於郡邑者，皆散處之猺，僅數十人各爲一羣而叢處耳。苟視其地之大小，以爲官之崇卑，取衆酋中素所信服者授之，而卽使盡有其地，慰撫長巡，無不可者。諸酋若不服從，則天兵助而征之，其勢必歸於一也。蓋以朝廷威福臨之，如粤西土官之制，永無征討之勞，而反獲其用，則亦何憚而不爲哉？甞有病此者，則曰：「其酋不應命也。」殊不知加以名號，而他無可欲者以利之，則是虛名雖榮，約束徒擾，何爲而願之哉？果如所處，則以國家之力爲之驅，廣土衆民，必人情之所欲
translation_en: …perhaps it cannot be secured for years to come. Moreover, the bandits of Luobang and Longshui are numerous and strong; we are merely fortunate that they have not yet run rampant. Military campaigns against them are always inadequate, whereas pacification would more than suffice. The key lies solely in establishing native officials to govern them. Wherever such offices were established in the past, the Yao have not only refrained from causing harm, but their elite fighters have also frequently served the state. The advantages of establishing these offices are plainly evident. Those now troubling the prefectures and counties are all scattered groups of Yao, each consisting of only a few dozen people living together. If the rank of each office were determined according to the size of its territory, and someone long trusted and obeyed among the chieftains were selected for appointment and immediately granted possession of the entire territory, then comforting, pacifying, and continually patrolling [?] would all be practicable. If any chieftains refused to submit, imperial troops would assist in campaigning against them, and circumstances would inevitably bring them under a single authority. By exercising the court’s power to punish and reward, following the system of native officials in western Guangdong and Guangxi (Yuexi), we would forever avoid the toil of punitive campaigns and instead gain their service. What, then, should make us hesitate to act? Someone once objected to this proposal, saying, “Their chieftains will not obey the command.” Such a person fails to understand that if we merely confer titles without offering any other desirable benefit, then, although the empty title may be glorious, the restraints are simply troublesome. Why should they desire it? If matters were indeed arranged as proposed, the power of the state would be used to drive others out on their behalf [?]; extensive lands and numerous subjects must be what people naturally desire…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也不亦動之而不得不行驅之而不得不
從者乎就其地用其人而鼓其所必趨故
曰因勢而利導之也今之海寇備矣而愚
亦與執事之憂者何也蓋今之議者戰也
而愚之所見者則守也風波迅速盜舟獨
宜追兵雖設何益耶近濱海之郡轉募舟
師皆在他邑雇直旣寡將權復輕利則進
不利則退海洋之戰孰從而稽之耶及以
功報又類非寇也稱戰皆虛事議守則實
===
功其要惟在募土兵以守之而已矣凡言
戰者皆由於武弁之喜功守則民蒙安靜
之福而若輩無以自見故甘心爲之他不
暇計卽如所募之舟直輕價厚而其人率
多悍徒應募而來將圖他利向賊死戰豈
其心耶區區募資知不足以係之者又陵
擾居民莫之能制虜來猶可尹來殺我此
之謂也苟惟專爲守計改募土兵則所守
之地卽其室廬桑梓之區其樂爲守且偵
punctuated: 也。不亦動之而不得不行，驅之而不得不從者乎？就其地，用其人，而鼓其所必趨，故曰因勢而利導之也。今之海寇備矣，而愚亦與執事之憂者，何也？蓋今之議者戰也，而愚之所見者則守也。風波迅速，盜舟獨宜，追兵雖設，何益耶？近濱海之郡，轉募舟師，皆在他邑。雇直旣寡，將權復輕，利則進，不利則退。海洋之戰，孰從而稽之耶？及以功報，又類非寇也。稱戰皆虛事，議守則實功。其要惟在募土兵以守之而已矣。凡言戰者，皆由於武弁之喜功。守則民蒙安靜之福，而若輩無以自見，故甘心爲之，他不暇計。卽如所募之舟，直輕價厚，而其人率多悍徒，應募而來，將圖他利，向賊死戰，豈其心耶？區區募資，知不足以係之者。又陵擾居民，莫之能制。「虜來猶可，尹來殺我」，此之謂也。苟惟專爲守計，改募土兵，則所守之地卽其室廬桑梓之區，其樂爲守且偵
translation_en:
…indeed. Would this not move them so that they could not but act, and impel them so that they could not but comply? Use their own territory and their own people, and encourage them toward what they will inevitably seek. This is what is meant by guiding them advantageously according to the circumstances.

Preparations against maritime raiders have now been made; why, then, do I too share your concern? It is because those offering proposals today advocate fighting, whereas in my humble view we should defend. Amid swift winds and waves, the raiders’ vessels alone are well suited to the conditions. Even if pursuing forces are provided, what use are they? Recently, coastal prefectures have turned to recruiting naval forces, all from other counties. Their pay is meager, and their commanders’ authority is weak. When conditions favor them, they advance; when they do not, they retreat. Who can follow them out to sea and verify their battles? When they report their achievements, those they have attacked generally turn out not to have been raiders at all. Claims of fighting are all empty affairs; a policy of defense brings real results. The essential point is simply to recruit local troops to defend the coast.

All this talk of fighting arises from military officers’ eagerness for merit. With defense, the people enjoy the blessings of peace and quiet, but such men have no means of distinguishing themselves. Thus they willingly pursue fighting, with no time to consider anything else. Take the vessels hired: their value is low, yet their price is high [?]. Their crews are mostly violent fellows who answer the recruitment call intending to seek other profits. Can fighting the raiders to the death be their true intention? We know that the paltry recruitment funds cannot suffice to bind them to their duty. Moreover, they bully and harass the inhabitants, and no one can restrain them. This is precisely what is meant by the saying, “When raiders come, we may yet survive; when Yin comes, he kills us.” If we concentrate exclusively on defense and recruit local troops instead, the land they defend will be the very place of their homes and ancestral villages. They will gladly defend it and keep watch…

text:
也不亦動之而不得不行驅之而不得不
從者乎就其地用其人而鼓其所必趨故

師皆在他邑雇直旣寡將權復輕利則進

…would this not mean that, when stirred to action, they could not but act, and when urged forward, they could not but follow? Employ the people of the locality on their own ground, and encourage them toward what they are bound to pursue. This is what is meant by taking advantage of circumstances to guide them to good effect. Preparations against maritime raiders have now been made; why, then, do I too share your concern? Because those discussing the matter today advocate fighting, whereas my own view favors defense. Winds and waves move swiftly, and the raiders’ vessels alone are suited to them. They will gladly undertake defense and scouting…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
戍未甞出境而日有所給則德我者深雖
半其直亦所願者況臨之者即其本籍之
長吏統屬既定號令易行視他募之樂則
就不樂則去飄忽不可羈者又難同日語
矣防守之眾一呼即集盜賊何虞耶亦甞
有病此者則曰其人不善戰也殊不知濱
海之人地利素熟壯年受募精習矣難顧
所以簡教振作之者何如耳不亦事舉而
不見其敝民利而不見其害者乎投所欲
===
違所惡而責以所不難故亦曰因勢而利
導之也盖大酋既撫則小醜之竊發者不
虞矣邏守既嚴則島嶼之棲泊者無所矣
此盖機與要之說也至其原本則治人治
法之說又所當留意者乎若夫兵食之宜
阨塞之要威信之實練習之方固有槩於
中而未敢盡也惟執事裁其可否
punctuated: 戍未甞出境，而日有所給，則德我者深，雖半其直，亦所願者。況臨之者即其本籍之長吏，統屬既定，號令易行，視他募之樂則就、不樂則去，飄忽不可羈者，又難同日語矣。防守之眾，一呼即集，盜賊何虞耶？亦甞有病此者，則曰其人不善戰也。殊不知濱海之人，地利素熟，壯年受募，精習矣難，顧所以簡教振作之者何如耳。不亦事舉而不見其敝，民利而不見其害者乎？投所欲，違所惡，而責以所不難，故亦曰因勢而利導之也。盖大酋既撫，則小醜之竊發者不虞矣；邏守既嚴，則島嶼之棲泊者無所矣。此盖機與要之說也。至其原本，則治人治法之說，又所當留意者乎？若夫兵食之宜、阨塞之要、威信之實、練習之方，固有槩於中而未敢盡也。惟執事裁其可否。
translation_en:
…on garrison duty, they would never leave their own territory and would receive daily provisions. Their gratitude toward us would therefore be profound; even at half the pay, they would willingly serve. Moreover, those supervising them would be the senior local officials of their own native jurisdictions. With the chain of command established, orders would be easy to enforce. They could hardly be compared with other recruits, who join when it pleases them and leave when it does not, drifting about beyond restraint. The defenders would assemble at a single call: what fear would there be of bandits?

Some have objected to this proposal, saying that these men are poor fighters. They fail to understand that coastal inhabitants are thoroughly familiar with the advantages of the terrain. Recruited in their prime, they would be well trained [?]; it depends only on how they are selected, instructed, and spurred to action. Would this not accomplish the task without its attendant abuses, benefiting the people without harming them? Give them what they desire, avoid what they dislike, and require of them what presents no difficulty. This, too, is what is meant by guiding circumstances to advantage. Once the chief leaders have been pacified, there will be no need to fear sudden outbreaks by lesser miscreants; once patrols and defenses are strict, those who shelter and anchor among the islands will have nowhere to go. This, broadly, is the argument concerning the critical opportunity and the essential measures.

As for the foundations, should attention not also be given to the argument concerning the men who govern and the methods of government? Regarding suitable arrangements for troops and provisions, the strategic importance of narrow passes, the substance of authority and trustworthiness, and methods of training, I do have some general ideas in mind, but have not presumed to set them all forth. I leave it to you, Sir, to judge their merits.

text:

…those serving on garrison duty have never had to leave their own territory and receive daily provisions, so their gratitude to us will be profound. Even at half the pay, they would willingly serve. Moreover, those overseeing them are the senior local officials of their own places of registration. Once the chain of command is established, orders are readily carried out. When the defenders assemble at a single call, what fear need there be of bandits?

I ask only that you judge whether these proposals are acceptable.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
洪惟我
聖天子御極之二十有五年秋八
月廣東鄉試事旣訖萬斛不
佞敢諗於諸士子曰自萬斛
獲與斯役嘗竊自懼以爲
國家取士于文務莫重焉乃今
===
持獨見之是一旦取素所不
知者七十五人於數千之中
其皆賢才矣乎萬有一焉非
賢與才也其何以逃罪苟曰
拔十得五斯已矣此可以恕
人而未宜自諉也夫循言識
實聖哲惟難何則其達之詞
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

洪惟我聖天子御極之二十有五年秋八月，廣東鄉試事旣訖，萬斛不佞，敢諗於諸士子曰：「自萬斛獲與斯役，嘗竊自懼，以爲國家取士于文，務莫重焉。乃今持獨見之是，一旦取素所不知者七十五人於數千之中，其皆賢才矣乎？萬有一焉非賢與才也，其何以逃罪？苟曰拔十得五，斯已矣，此可以恕人，而未宜自諉也。夫循言識實，聖哲惟難。何則？其達之詞
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the autumn, in the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year since our sagely Son of Heaven ascended the throne, the Guangdong Provincial Examination had concluded. I, Wanhu, unworthy though I am, ventured to address the candidates: “Since I was privileged to take part in this undertaking, I have privately felt apprehensive, believing that no duty is weightier than selecting men for state service through their writing. Yet now, relying on what my own judgment alone deems right, I have at one stroke selected seventy-five men previously unknown to me from among several thousand. Are they all men of virtue and talent? If even one among them possesses neither virtue nor talent, how could I escape blame? If one says that selecting ten and finding five worthy is sufficient, this may serve to excuse others, but ought not to serve as a pretext for shirking one’s own responsibility. To discern substance through words is difficult even for sages and wise men. Why is this? The words through which they express themselves …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
洪惟我
聖天子御極之二十有五年秋八
月廣東鄉試事旣訖萬斛不
佞敢諗於諸士子曰自萬斛
獲與斯役嘗竊自懼以爲
國家取士于文務莫重焉乃今
持獨見之是一旦取素所不
知者七十五人於數千之中
其皆賢才矣乎萬有一焉非
賢與才也其何以逃罪苟曰
拔十得五斯已矣此可以恕
人而未宜自諉也夫循言識
實聖哲惟難何則其達之詞
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

洪惟我聖天子御極之二十有五年秋八月，廣東鄉試事旣訖，萬斛不佞，敢諗於諸士子曰：「自萬斛獲與斯役，嘗竊自懼，以爲國家取士于文，務莫重焉。乃今持獨見之是，一旦取素所不知者七十五人於數千之中，其皆賢才矣乎？萬有一焉非賢與才也，其何以逃罪？苟曰拔十得五，斯已矣，此可以恕人，而未宜自諉也。夫循言識實，聖哲惟難。何則？其達之詞
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the autumn, in the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year since our sage Son of Heaven ascended the throne, the Guangdong Provincial Examination had concluded. I, Wan Hu, unworthy though I am, venture to address the candidates: “Ever since I was permitted to take part in this undertaking, I have privately felt apprehensive, believing that no task is weightier than the state’s selection of men through their writing. Yet now, relying on my own judgment of what is right, I have at a stroke selected seventy-five men whom I did not previously know from among several thousand. Are they all worthy and talented? If even one among them should lack worthiness and talent, how could I escape blame? If one says that selecting ten and finding five suitable is enough, this may serve to excuse others, but it ought not serve to absolve oneself. To discern the reality of a man from his words is difficult even for sages and wise men. Why is this? The words in which he expresses himself…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也未必皆若其所存也是故
躁而詞莊貪而詞介暴而詞
溫懦而詞勁冥而詞昭是將
循奚道以決之今惟其文取
耳矣庸知其中無前所云若
人也既又自解曰粤山海阻
奥鍾奇毓秀奮舒景光後先
===
相望矧自
明聖建極垂範彰明好惡登崇茂
實甄陶漸漬益醇以熈薄海
内外罔不泳游
聖澤砥礪于名行粤多才傑苟在
士籍宜無庸違而况七十五
人者尤其庠校之英乎此萬
punctuated: 也，未必皆若其所存也。是故躁而詞莊，貪而詞介，暴而詞溫，懦而詞勁，冥而詞昭，是將循奚道以決之？今惟其文取耳矣，庸知其中無前所云若人也？既又自解曰：「粤山海阻奥，鍾奇毓秀，奮舒景光，後先相望。矧自明聖建極垂範，彰明好惡，登崇茂實，甄陶漸漬，益醇以熈，薄海内外罔不泳游聖澤，砥礪于名行。粤多才傑，苟在士籍，宜無庸違，而况七十五人者，尤其庠校之英乎？此萬
translation_en:
… need not all reflect what they harbor within. Thus, the impetuous may write with solemnity, the greedy with integrity, the violent with gentleness, the cowardly with vigor, and the benighted with clarity. By what method, then, can one reach a judgment? Today we select them solely on the basis of their compositions. How can we know that among them there are none of the people just described?
Then I consoled myself further, saying: “Guangdong, secluded behind mountains and seas, gathers extraordinary gifts and nurtures outstanding talent. Men rise and display their brilliance, appearing in succession, one after another. Moreover, since our enlightened sage sovereign established the supreme standard and set an example, clearly manifested his approval and disapproval, and advanced and honored men of substantial merit, his molding and permeating influence has brought ever greater refinement and prosperity. Throughout the realm, as far as the seas, within and beyond, all bathe in the sage sovereign’s beneficence and apply themselves to refining their reputation and conduct. Guangdong has many outstanding men of talent. Those enrolled as students should be neither mediocre nor wayward; how much more must this be so of these seventy-five, who are the very flower of its schools? This … [The page breaks off at 萬, ‘ten thousand’; its meaning here remains uncertain.]

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也未必皆若其所存也是故
躁而詞莊貪而詞介暴而詞
溫懦而詞勁冥而詞昭是將
循奚道以决之今惟其文取
耳矣庸知其中無前所云若
人也旣又自解曰粤山海阻
奧鍾奇毓秀奮舒景光後先
===
相望矧自
明聖建極垂範彰明好惡登崇茂
實甄陶漸漬益醇以熙薄海
内外罔不泳游
聖澤砥礪于名行粤多才傑茍在
士籍宜無庸違而况七十五
人者尤其庠校之英乎此〔萬〕
punctuated: 也，未必皆若其所存也。是故躁而詞莊，貪而詞介，暴而詞溫，懦而詞勁，冥而詞昭，是將循奚道以决之？今惟其文取耳矣，庸知其中無前所云若人也？旣又自解曰：「粤山海阻奧，鍾奇毓秀，奮舒景光，後先相望。矧自明聖建極垂範，彰明好惡，登崇茂實，甄陶漸漬，益醇以熙，薄海内外，罔不泳游聖澤，砥礪于名行。粤多才傑，茍在士籍，宜無庸違，而况七十五人者，尤其庠校之英乎！此〔萬〕
translation_en:
…yet they do not necessarily all accord with what they harbor within. Thus, an impetuous man may write with gravity; a greedy man, with integrity; a violent man, with gentleness; a timid man, with force; and a benighted man, with clarity. By what means, then, are we to judge them? At present we select them solely on their writing. How can we know that among them there are none like those just described?
Then I reassured myself, saying: “Guangdong, secluded behind mountains and seas, gathers extraordinary energies and nurtures outstanding talent. Its splendid brilliance unfolds, and distinguished men arise in succession. Moreover, since our enlightened sage sovereign established the supreme standard and provided an enduring example, clearly proclaimed what he favors and condemns, and elevated men of substantial worth, his formative influence has gradually steeped the people, making their customs ever purer and more harmonious. Throughout the realm and beyond, to the seas’ utmost bounds, all bathe in the imperial beneficence and strive to refine their reputations and conduct. Guangdong has many talented and outstanding men. Those enrolled as students should surely live up to these expectations; how much more these seventy-five men, the very elite of its schools! This〔ten thousand〕…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
斛心口自語之實非面謾也
夫事之輕重世之榮辱恒繫
乎其人是舉也誠得一人焉
振于德業天下且將視之若
泰山與華袞也又况乎七十
五人者皆能有聞也其弗益
榮以重乎使有一人焉負厥
===
瑕疵天下且將以爲口實矣
又况乎或不幸而有二三其
人也其弗益輕以辱乎夫宴
以鹿鳴導以計偕賓之以盛
禮固將期之以大效也上之
必能黼黻
鴻猷協和
punctuated:
斛心口自語之實，非面謾也。
夫事之輕重，世之榮辱，恒繫乎其人。是舉也，誠得一人焉，振于德業，天下且將視之若泰山與華袞也。又况乎七十五人者皆能有聞也，其弗益榮以重乎？使有一人焉，負厥瑕疵，天下且將以爲口實矣。又况乎或不幸而有二三其人也，其弗益輕以辱乎？夫宴以鹿鳴，導以計偕，賓之以盛禮，固將期之以大效也。上之，必能黼黻鴻猷，協和
translation_en:
…the sincere words that I, Hu [Wan Hu, whose surname appears on the preceding page], utter from my own heart and mouth, not deception offered to your faces.
The importance accorded an undertaking, and the honor or disgrace it receives in the world, always depend upon the people involved. If this examination truly yields even one man distinguished in virtue and accomplishment, the world will regard him as Mount Tai or a splendid ceremonial robe. How much more so if all seventy-five men achieve renown! Would this not bring still greater honor and weight to the undertaking? If even one man bears some moral blemish, the world will seize upon it as grounds for criticism. How much more so if, unfortunately, there are two or three such men! Would this not further diminish the undertaking and bring it disgrace? We feast them at the Deer’s Cry Banquet, send them onward to the capital with the tribute mission, and honor them as guests with sumptuous ceremony precisely because we expect great achievements from them. At the highest level, they must surely be able to embellish the grand imperial designs and bring into harmony…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
斛心口自語之實非面謾也
夫事之輕重世之榮辱恒繫
乎其人是舉也誠得一人焉
振于德業天下且將視之若
泰山與華袞也又况乎七十
五人者皆能有聞也其弗益
榮以重乎使有一人焉負厥
===

又况乎或不幸而有二三其
人也其弗益輕以辱乎夫宴
以鹿鳴導以計偕賓之以盛
禮固將期之以大效也上之
必能黼黻
鴻猷協和
punctuated: 斛心口自語之實，非面謾也。夫事之輕重，世之榮辱，恒繫乎其人。是舉也，誠得一人焉，振于德業，天下且將視之若泰山與華袞也。又况乎七十五人者皆能有聞也，其弗益榮以重乎？使有一人焉，負厥瑕疵，天下且將以爲口實矣。又况乎或不幸而有二三其人也，其弗益輕以辱乎？夫宴以鹿鳴，導以計偕，賓之以盛禮，固將期之以大效也。上之必能黼黻鴻猷，協和
translation_en: …the sincerity of words spoken from the heart [?], rather than deception to one’s face. The weight accorded an undertaking, and the honor or disgrace it receives in the world, always depend upon the people involved. If this examination truly obtains even one man distinguished in virtue and achievement, the world will regard him as Mount Tai or an ornate ceremonial robe. How much more so if all seventy-five men attain distinction! Will this not bring still greater honor and weight? If even one man among them bears moral blemishes, the world will make him grounds for reproach. How much more so if, unfortunately, there are two or three such men! Will this not bring still greater loss of standing and disgrace? To feast them with the singing of “Deer Call,” send them onward together with the tribute mission, and receive them as guests with sumptuous ceremony is assuredly to expect great accomplishments from them. The foremost among them will surely adorn the grand imperial designs and bring into harmony …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
神化次之必能輸誠殫慮輯寧民
社忠功義烈昭昭乎若揭日
月盈天壤斯庶乎仰答
洪造萬分之一乃無負主司遴選
之意苟惟祿與位焉是崇是
圖其究也罔所底止有司者
將持尺寸議其後不但眛眛
===
已也夫施厚而報薄俊延而
鄙卻榮出而辱歸將謂之何
古人有言行萬里者始跬步
鹿鳴之歌固
巖廊之跬步而輕重榮辱之兆
端也夫八音不諧則至樂不
全水火不積則光炎不博蹄
punctuated: 神化。次之，必能輸誠殫慮，輯寧民社，忠功義烈，昭昭乎若揭日月，盈天壤。斯庶乎仰答洪造萬分之一，乃無負主司遴選之意。苟惟祿與位焉是崇是圖，其究也罔所底止，有司者將持尺寸議其後，不但眛眛已也。夫施厚而報薄，俊延而鄙卻，榮出而辱歸，將謂之何？古人有言：「行萬里者始跬步。」鹿鳴之歌，固巖廊之跬步，而輕重榮辱之兆端也。夫八音不諧，則至樂不全；水火不積，則光炎不博。蹄
translation_en:
…the sovereign’s divine transforming influence. At the next level, they must offer their wholehearted loyalty and exhaust their deliberative efforts to bring peace to the people and their communities. Their loyal achievements and righteous deeds must shine as brilliantly as the sun and moon raised aloft, filling heaven and earth. Only thus might they repay one ten-thousandth of the sovereign’s immense beneficence and live up to the chief examiners’ intentions in selecting them. If they esteem and pursue only salaries and rank, their striving will ultimately know no bounds. The responsible officials will then apply exacting standards in judging their subsequent conduct; the matter will not end merely in obscurity [?].

To receive generous favor but repay it meagerly, to be welcomed as a man of talent but rejected as a contemptible fellow, to depart in glory but return in disgrace—what is one to say of this? The ancients said: “A journey of ten thousand li begins with a half-step.” The singing of “Deer Cry” is indeed the first half-step toward service at the imperial court, and the beginning of the signs that foretell esteem or contempt, glory or disgrace. If the eight classes of musical instruments are not in harmony, the finest music cannot be complete; if water and fire are not accumulated, light and flame cannot spread far [?]. Hoof [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
神化次之必能輸誠殫慮輯寧民
社忠功義烈昭昭乎若揭日
月盈天壤斯庶乎仰答
洪造萬分之一乃無負主司遴選
之意苟惟祿與位焉是崇是
圖其究也罔所底止有司者
將持尺寸議其後不但眛眛
已也夫施厚而報薄俊延而
鄙卻榮出而辱歸將謂之何
古人有言行萬里者始跬步
鹿鳴之歌固
巖廊之跬步而輕重榮辱之兆
端也夫八音不諧則至樂不
全水火不積則光炎不博蹄
punctuated: 神化次之，必能輸誠殫慮，輯寧民社，忠功義烈，昭昭乎若揭日月，盈天壤，斯庶乎仰答洪造萬分之一，乃無負主司遴選之意。苟惟祿與位焉是崇是圖，其究也罔所底止，有司者將持尺寸議其後，不但眛眛已也。夫施厚而報薄，俊延而鄙卻，榮出而辱歸，將謂之何？古人有言：「行萬里者始跬步。」鹿鳴之歌，固巖廊之跬步，而輕重榮辱之兆端也。夫八音不諧，則至樂不全；水火不積，則光炎不博。蹄
translation_en:
… divine transformation comes next [?]. You must be able to offer your utmost sincerity and expend all your thought, bringing peace to the people and their communities. Let your loyal achievements and righteous deeds shine as brightly as the sun and moon raised aloft, filling heaven and earth. Only thus might you repay one ten-thousandth of the Emperor’s immense beneficence and fulfill the intention with which the presiding examiners selected you. If you esteem and pursue only emoluments and rank, your desires will ultimately know no bounds. The responsible officials will apply their standards in judging your subsequent conduct; the matter will not simply remain in obscurity [?]. If generous favor receives scant repayment, if those welcomed as men of talent are rejected as base, and if those who depart in honor return in disgrace, what is one to say?

The ancients said, “A journey of ten thousand li begins with a single step.” The singing of “The Deer Call” is indeed the first step toward service at court, and the first indication of esteem or disregard, honor or disgrace. If the eight classes of musical instruments are not in harmony, the finest music cannot be complete; if water and fire do not accumulate, light and flame cannot spread widely [?]. Hooves …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
齧善走未若騏驥之良唐虞
之廷不厭盛德之彙萬斛也
竊有全望於爾諸士子也幸
相與勗之云爾
直隸安慶府望江縣儒學敎
諭蕭萬斛謹序
punctuated:
齧善走，未若騏驥之良。唐虞之廷，不厭盛德之彙。萬斛也，竊有全望於爾諸士子也，幸相與勗之云爾。
直隸安慶府望江縣儒學敎諭蕭萬斛謹序。
translation_en:
…a horse that bites may run well, yet it cannot match the excellence of a thoroughbred. The courts of Tang and Yu never tired of gathering men of abundant virtue. I, Wanhu, place my fullest hopes in you, gentlemen scholars, and trust that you will encourage one another in this endeavor. That is all I wish to say.
Respectfully prefaced by Xiao Wanhu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Wangjiang County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
齧善走未若騏驥之良唐虞
之廷不厭盛德之彙萬斛也
竊有全望於爾諸士子也幸
相與勗之云爾
直隷安慶府望江縣儒學敎
諭蕭萬斛謹序
punctuated:
齧善走，未若騏驥之良；唐虞之廷，不厭盛德之彙。萬斛也，竊有全望於爾諸士子也，幸相與勗之云爾。
直隷安慶府望江縣儒學敎諭蕭萬斛謹序。
translation_en:
…Nie [?] runs well, yet cannot match the excellence of a thoroughbred; the courts of Tang Yao and Yu Shun never tired of gathering men of eminent virtue. I, Wanhu, privately place my fullest hopes in you scholars, and hope that you will encourage one another—that is all.
Respectfully prefaced by Xiao Wanhu, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wangjiang County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
嘉靖丙午秋粤當大比士監
察御史楊以誠奉
命按治寔維監臨申嚴胥飭凡簾
內外百執事咸愼簡以充先
是前巡按御史陳儲秀稽度
規恢表章令甲徵靜深等以
===
===
需校藝至是咸集乃以靜深
暨敎諭蕭萬斛總試而分經
校閱則學正呂天恩敎諭黃
繼宗雷孟冬吳珊陳英選提
調則左布政使朱紈左叅政
張鏊監試則按察使屠大山
僉事何元述規畫維允罔弗
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

嘉靖丙午秋，粤當大比士。監察御史楊以誠奉命按治，寔維監臨，申嚴胥飭。凡簾內外百執事，咸愼簡以充。先是，前巡按御史陳儲秀稽度規恢，表章令甲，徵靜深等以需校藝。至是咸集，乃以靜深暨敎諭蕭萬斛總試，而分經校閱則學正呂天恩、敎諭黃繼宗、雷孟冬、吳珊、陳英選。提調則左布政使朱紈、左叅政張鏊；監試則按察使屠大山、僉事何元述。規畫維允，罔弗
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], Guangdong was due to hold the triennial examination of scholars. Investigating Censor Yang Yicheng, commissioned by imperial command to inspect the province’s administration, served as Supervising Official. He reiterated strict requirements and enjoined all concerned to act diligently. All personnel serving inside and outside the examination curtain were carefully selected for their duties.

Previously, the former Regional Inspector, Chen Chuxiu, had assessed and planned the arrangements, publicized the statutory regulations, and summoned Jingshen and others to await the assessment of examination compositions. By this time they had all assembled. Jingshen and Instructor Xiao Wanhu were therefore placed in overall charge of the examination. Those assigned to evaluate compositions by individual Classic were Instructor Lü Tian’en and Instructors Huang Jizong, Lei Mengdong, Wu Shan, and Chen Yingxuan. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Wan and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Ao; those supervising the examination were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Tu Dashan and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner He Yuanshu. The arrangements were fitting, and none failed to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
寅恭事事維時兵部右侍郎
張岳奠綏南服保釐化誨人
有寧宇士咸思奮都御史顧
遂屏翰方隅燕及士類敦獎
縫掖振雅覘文總兵平江伯
陳圭雅尚儒術恤刑郎中杜
捄樂觀鉅典右參政張烜左
===
參議朱憲章右參議方民悅
副使張瑤袁載僉事陳捷都
指揮王寵則皆協志宣猷率
作于外右布政使龔輝左參
議顧中孚僉事施雨都指揮
夏忠先期次第入
賀若左布政使今陞都御史應
punctuated: 寅恭事事。維時兵部右侍郎張岳奠綏南服，保釐化誨，人有寧宇，士咸思奮。都御史顧遂屏翰方隅，燕及士類，敦獎縫掖，振雅覘文。總兵平江伯陳圭雅尚儒術，恤刑郎中杜捄樂觀鉅典。右參政張烜、左參議朱憲章、右參議方民悅、副使張瑤、袁載、僉事陳捷、都指揮王寵，則皆協志宣猷，率作于外。右布政使龔輝、左參議顧中孚、僉事施雨、都指揮夏忠，先期次第入賀。若左布政使今陞都御史應
translation_en: … respectfully attended to every matter. At this time, Zhang Yue, Right Vice Minister of War, secured and pacified the southern region, maintaining order and providing moral instruction. The people had peaceful homes, and the scholars all aspired to distinguish themselves. Gu Sui, Censor-in-chief, served as a bulwark for the region, extending his beneficence to the scholarly community, generously encouraging men of learning, promoting refined scholarship, and assessing literary accomplishment. Chen Gui, Earl of Pingjiang and Regional Commander, esteemed Confucian learning; Du Jiu, a Bureau Director assigned to review penal cases, gladly witnessed this great ceremony. Zhang Xuan, Right Vice Administration Commissioner; Zhu Xianzhang, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; Fang Minyue, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; Zhang Yao and Yuan Zai, Vice Surveillance Commissioners; Chen Jie, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Wang Chong, Regional Military Commissioner, all worked with a common purpose to carry out the plans, taking the lead in work outside the examination compound. Gong Hui, Right Administration Commissioner; Gu Zhongfu, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; Shi Yu, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Xia Zhong, Regional Military Commissioner, arrived in succession before the appointed date to offer congratulations. As for the Left Administration Commissioner, now promoted to Censor-in-chief, Ying…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大猷按察使今陞山東右布
政使駱顒副使今陞湖廣右
參政游居敬雖先後去粤亦
皆與有聞焉者也旣圍棘鑰
院御史率衆而籲諗曰諸大
夫其有思乎衆唯唯又曰玆
役也事
===
===
君以人也苟弗參以衆見非忠也
其毖諸曰辭尚體要有弗誠
弗衷弗率于
訓者其麾諸曰
上再三俞議矣其祗奉
德音無侵無昵協于大公惟真材
之務得其勗諸衆唯唯内外
punctuated: 大猷、按察使今陞山東右布政使駱顒、副使今陞湖廣右參政游居敬，雖先後去粤，亦皆與有聞焉者也。旣圍棘鑰院，御史率衆而籲諗曰：「諸大夫，其有思乎？」衆唯唯。又曰：「玆役也，事君以人也。苟弗參以衆見，非忠也，其毖諸！」曰：「辭尚體要，有弗誠、弗衷、弗率于訓者，其麾諸！」曰：「上再三俞議矣，其祗奉德音，無侵無昵，協于大公，惟真材之務得，其勗諸！」衆唯唯。内外
translation_en:
…Dayou [Ying Dayou, named across the page boundary]; Surveillance Commissioner Luo Yong, now promoted to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong; and Surveillance Vice Commissioner You Jujing, now promoted to Right Vice Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang—although they had left Guangdong at different times, all had participated in and been informed of these affairs.
Once the thorn enclosure had been erected and the examination compound locked, the censor assembled everyone and addressed them: “Gentlemen, have you given this thought?” All assented respectfully. He continued: “In this undertaking, we serve the ruler by providing men of talent. If we fail to consult everyone’s views, we are not loyal. Be vigilant!” He said: “In writing, what matters is substance and essentials. Reject any whose words are insincere, fail to accord with what is right, or do not follow the authoritative teachings!” He said: “His Majesty has repeatedly approved the proposals. Reverently uphold his gracious pronouncements; allow neither encroachment nor favoritism, and act together in complete impartiality. Make obtaining true talent your sole concern. Exert yourselves!” All assented respectfully. Those inside and outside…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
咸精白事事乃進提學副使
陳愷所簡士二千四百三試
之遵
制額拔其雋七十五人并梓其文
之粹者以
獻而靜深職務猥序首簡竊惟粵
本虞夏要服而祝融遐壤也
===
頃靜深以介聘而來也道彭
蠡泝章貢南度庾嶺煙雲杳
靄之間一翠千里星日之南
際天爲壑蓋奧區也已旣乃
俊髦畢來雲蒸景附縱觀乎
所爲文則深蓄濬發其體類
皆雄渾昌大而莊重秀偉其
punctuated:
咸精白事事。乃進提學副使陳愷所簡士二千四百，三試之，遵制額拔其雋七十五人，并梓其文之粹者以獻。而靜深職務，猥序首簡。竊惟粵本虞夏要服，而祝融遐壤也。
頃靜深以介聘而來也，道彭蠡，泝章貢，南度庾嶺。煙雲杳靄之間，一翠千里；星日之南，際天爲壑，蓋奧區也已。旣乃俊髦畢來，雲蒸景附。縱觀乎所爲文，則深蓄濬發，其體類皆雄渾昌大，而莊重秀偉。其
translation_en:
…all attended to their duties with pure intentions. We then admitted the 2,400 scholars selected by Chen Kai, the Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, and examined them in three sessions. In accordance with the imperially prescribed quota, we selected seventy-five outstanding candidates and had the finest of their writings printed for presentation to the throne. I, Jingshen, in fulfillment of my official duties, venture to supply a preface for the opening pages. I humbly reflect that Yue was originally within the Outer Submission Zone under Yu and Xia, a distant domain of Zhurong, the god of fire.
Recently, when I, Jingshen, came as an assistant envoy, I passed through Pengli, ascended the Zhang and Gong rivers, and crossed the Yu Mountains southward. Amid distant, misty clouds, an unbroken green stretched for a thousand li. South of the stars and sun, a vast hollow reached to the horizon: truly a secluded region. Then the gifted scholars all arrived, gathering like rising clouds and following like shadows. Surveying their writings, I found deeply stored learning expressed with penetrating force. Their styles were uniformly vigorous, full-bodied, expansive, and grand, yet dignified, refined, and imposing. Their…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
達也冲和浩放而洋洋纚纚
其究也淵邃貞明而變見鼓
奮蓋阜和之委溟浸之光
聖人之錫極均是乎得焉吁盛矣
可為嶺南重矣彼云職方者
謂清淑不類中州而多乎瑰
奇瑋麗之產蓋末也何也山
===
之入中國昉崑崙經岷嶓數
萬里而窮於海故盤為五嶺
嶺至峻位離得天地禮信光
亨之氣而上應乎
嚮明之治是故鍾英炳靈逢期
翊
運後先名碩固種種也乃斯文
punctuated: 達也，冲和浩放而洋洋纚纚；其究也，淵邃貞明而變見鼓奮。蓋阜和之委、溟浸之光、聖人之錫極，均是乎得焉。吁，盛矣！可為嶺南重矣！彼云職方者，謂清淑不類中州，而多乎瑰奇瑋麗之產，蓋末也。何也？山之入中國，昉崑崙，經岷嶓數萬里而窮於海，故盤為五嶺。嶺至峻，位離，得天地禮信光亨之氣，而上應乎嚮明之治。是故鍾英炳靈，逢期翊運，後先名碩，固種種也。乃斯文
translation_en:
…in their expression, they are harmonious, expansive, and unrestrained, flowing forth copiously and continuously; in their ultimate import, they are profound, upright, and lucid, displaying transformations and stirring the spirit. The accumulated bounty of harmonious influences, the radiance of the surrounding seas, and the sage’s bestowal of the supreme norm are all realized here. Ah, how splendid! This indeed brings distinction to Lingnan! Those who speak as geographers say that its pure and felicitous influences differ from those of the Central Plain, and that it abounds in rare, extraordinary, and beautiful products. Yet this touches only the surface. Why is that?

The mountains that enter China originate in Kunlun, pass through Min and Bo, and extend for tens of thousands of li before ending at the sea; thus they coil together to form the Five Ranges. These ranges are exceedingly lofty and occupy the position of Li, the south. They receive from Heaven and Earth the vital influences of ritual propriety, trustworthiness, radiance, and flourishing, and correspond above to a government turned toward the light. Thus they concentrate excellence and manifest spiritual potency. Meeting their appointed time and assisting the dynastic destiny, eminent and learned men have certainly appeared here in abundance, generation after generation. And now these writings…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
又得於磅礴鬱積而非偶然
者與始南國之榛狉也周宣
起而疆理其臣賛之歌金石
矢文德焉我
皇祖受
命宅夏遂臣荒服越裳來王齊哇
秩祀蓋禹平舜肇所未有也
===
===
列聖熈洽肆我
聖天子中興薄海内外涵濡煦嫗
頃者修文告款雕題允乎叙
戎之
成烈而追琢人文播爲
心法典訓又皆危微精一之旨使
尹召復生不知何如以對揚
punctuated:
又得於磅礴鬱積，而非偶然者與？始南國之榛狉也，周宣起而疆理，其臣賛之，歌金石，矢文德焉。我皇祖受命宅夏，遂臣荒服，越裳來王，齊哇秩祀，蓋禹平舜肇所未有也。
列聖熈洽，肆我聖天子中興，薄海内外，涵濡煦嫗。頃者修文，告款雕題，允乎叙戎之成烈！而追琢人文，播爲心法典訓，又皆危微精一之旨。使尹召復生，不知何如以對揚
translation_en:
…must not this literary flourishing likewise derive from the vast, accumulated forces of the region, rather than have arisen by chance? When the southern lands were still overgrown and wild, King Xuan of Zhou arose and established their boundaries and administration. His ministers celebrated him in songs accompanied by bells and chime stones, setting forth his civil virtue. Our imperial ancestor received Heaven’s mandate and established his seat in the central lands, then brought even the remotest territories into submission. Yuechang came to acknowledge his kingship; “Qi wa” and the ordering of sacrifices [?]—achievements beyond even Yu’s pacification and Shun’s establishment of order.
Successive sage emperors brought prosperity and concord. Now our sage Son of Heaven has brought about a restoration, nurturing and warming all within and beyond the seas. Recently, through his cultivation of civil virtue, the tattooed peoples have declared their allegiance: truly a magnificent achievement in bringing the Rong peoples into order! Moreover, he has refined human culture and disseminated it as canonical instructions on the method of cultivating the mind, all embodying the teaching that the human mind is precarious and the moral mind subtle, requiring refinement and singleness of purpose. Were Yin and Shao to return to life, I do not know how they could adequately respond to and extol…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也而况衣被雲漢之士優游
厭飫有不煥然而維新者乎
文不惟以地盛矣雖然文也
者爲經緯爲綱維爲軌憲斧
藻龍光均維弘濟布帛菽粟
民用莫先焉是故吾人之文
與天地帝王一也諸士子孕
===
殖於造化之勤而長育於
文治主司又以文進之其千載
一時矣將無毅然而已任者
乎昔者周禮在魯孔氏之徒
相與斟酌乎禮樂而論說乎
仁義故太史公涉汶泗觀鄒
嶧講射而歎焉以其非徒文
punctuated: 也。而况衣被雲漢之士，優游厭飫，有不煥然而維新者乎？文不惟以地盛矣。雖然，文也者，爲經緯，爲綱維，爲軌憲，斧藻龍光，均維弘濟，布帛菽粟，民用莫先焉。是故吾人之文，與天地帝王一也。諸士子孕殖於造化之勤，而長育於文治，主司又以文進之，其千載一時矣！將無毅然而已任者乎？昔者周禮在魯，孔氏之徒相與斟酌乎禮樂，而論說乎仁義。故太史公涉汶泗，觀鄒嶧講射而歎焉，以其非徒文
translation_en:
…And how much more so for scholars clothed in the sovereign’s heavenly radiance! Dwelling at ease and thoroughly nourished by it, could any fail to be brilliantly renewed? Literary culture flourishes through more than its locality alone. Yet culture supplies the warp and weft, the guiding cords, and the standards; it embellishes imperial glory, sustains order, and broadly aids the world. Like cloth and silk, beans and grain, nothing takes precedence over it in the people’s daily use. Thus our literary culture is one with that of Heaven and Earth and of emperors and kings. You scholars have been conceived and nurtured through the tireless workings of creation and brought to maturity under civil governance. The presiding examiners now advance you through your writing: surely this is an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years! Will there not be those who resolutely take this responsibility upon themselves [?]?

In former times, the rites of Zhou survived in Lu. The followers of Confucius together weighed rites and music and discussed benevolence and righteousness. Thus, when the Grand Astrologer Sima Qian traveled through the Wen and Si river region and observed instruction in ritual archery in Zou and Yi, he sighed in admiration, because theirs was no mere outward refinement…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也夫士之不爲徒文者必也
爲德行爲事業其進也必樹
績流聲必奮庸熈載爲先資
成信而不爲靜言而庸違者
三代之英由此其選也靜深
有徵文之慶矣而又懼夫文
之徒者將無以地重而爲治
===
化累故根極之以鄒魯之文
獻迪焉冀自今所謂豪傑者
必無負於地於時爲
朝家徵實用而主司亦庶乎塞
也維二三子交相成也其懋
圖之
江西撫州府儒學敎授潘靜
punctuated:
也。夫士之不爲徒文者，必也爲德行，爲事業。其進也，必樹績流聲，必奮庸熈載爲先，資成信而不爲靜言而庸違者。三代之英，由此其選也。靜深有徵文之慶矣，而又懼夫文之徒者，將無以地重而爲治化累，故根極之以鄒魯之文獻迪焉。冀自今所謂豪傑者，必無負於地於時，爲朝家徵實用，而主司亦庶乎塞也。維二三子交相成也，其懋圖之！
江西撫州府儒學敎授潘靜
translation_en:
…indeed. A scholar whose learning is more than mere literary display must cultivate virtuous conduct and accomplish practical deeds. Upon advancing into office, he must establish achievements and leave a lasting reputation; he must give priority to exerting his abilities and bringing his duties to fruition, providing assistance and fulfilling good faith [?], rather than speaking fine words while acting contrary to them. It was on this basis that the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties were selected.
I, Jingshen, have had the pleasure of evaluating literary accomplishment, yet I also fear that those devoted merely to literary display may fail to enhance the standing of this region and instead burden its governance and moral transformation. Thus I have traced matters to their roots, guiding them through the writings and worthy traditions of Zou and Lu. I hope that henceforth those called outstanding men will disappoint neither their region nor their age, demonstrating their practical usefulness to the imperial court, so that the officials presiding over the examination may also come close to fulfilling their responsibilities. You gentlemen must help one another achieve this. Strive earnestly toward it!
Pan Jing…, Professor of the Confucian School of Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text: 深謹序
punctuated: 深謹序。
translation_en: …shen (completing the name Pan Jingshen) respectfully composed this preface.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史楊以誠〔明夫江西宜春縣人戊戌進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使朱紈〔子純直隸長洲縣人辛巳進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政張鏊〔濟甫江西南昌縣人丙戌進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使屠大山〔國望浙江鄞縣人癸未進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事何元述〔元孝福建晉江縣人壬辰進士〕
===
考試官
江西撫州府儒學教授潘靜深〔時見貴州普安衛籍浙江桐鄉縣人丁酉貢士〕
直隸安慶府望江縣儒學教諭蕭萬斛〔時應江西泰和縣人庚子貢士〕
同考試官
湖廣武昌府興國州儒學學正吕天恩〔仁甫廣西灌陽縣人丁酉貢士〕
江西撫州府樂安縣儒學教諭黃繼宗〔允肖福建莆田縣人丁酉貢士〕
江西廣信府貴溪縣儒學教諭雷孟冬〔貞卿湖廣長沙縣人癸卯貢士〕
浙江嚴州府壽昌縣儒學教諭吳珊〔佩之廣西宜山縣人癸卯貢士〕
河南汝寧府信陽州羅山縣儒學教諭陳英選〔資仕福建長樂縣人丁酉貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試

監臨官：巡按廣東監察御史楊以誠〔明夫，江西宜春縣人，戊戌進士〕。

提調官：廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使朱紈〔子純，直隸長洲縣人，辛巳進士〕。廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政張鏊〔濟甫，江西南昌縣人，丙戌進士〕。

監試官：廣東等處提刑按察司按察使屠大山〔國望，浙江鄞縣人，癸未進士〕。廣東等處提刑按察司僉事何元述〔元孝，福建晉江縣人，壬辰進士〕。

考試官：江西撫州府儒學教授潘靜深〔時見，貴州普安衛籍，浙江桐鄉縣人，丁酉貢士〕。直隸安慶府望江縣儒學教諭蕭萬斛〔時應，江西泰和縣人，庚子貢士〕。

同考試官：湖廣武昌府興國州儒學學正吕天恩〔仁甫，廣西灌陽縣人，丁酉貢士〕。江西撫州府樂安縣儒學教諭黃繼宗〔允肖，福建莆田縣人，丁酉貢士〕。江西廣信府貴溪縣儒學教諭雷孟冬〔貞卿，湖廣長沙縣人，癸卯貢士〕。浙江嚴州府壽昌縣儒學教諭吳珊〔佩之，廣西宜山縣人，癸卯貢士〕。河南汝寧府信陽州羅山縣儒學教諭陳英選〔資仕，福建長樂縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, twenty-fifth year of Jiajing (1546)

Supervising Official
Yang Yicheng, Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Mingfu and was a native of Yichun County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuxu year.

Proctors
Zhu Wan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Zichun and was a native of Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.
Zhang Ao, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Jifu and was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Tu Dashan, Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Guowang and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.
He Yuanshu, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Yuanxiao and was a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Examiners
Pan Jingshen, Professor of the Confucian School of Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Shijian. He was registered in Pu’an Guard, Guizhou, and was a native of Tongxiang County, Zhejiang; he became a tribute student (gongshi) in the dingyou year.
Xiao Wanhu, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wangjiang County, Anqing Prefecture, in Zhili, had the courtesy name Shiying and was a native of Taihe County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute student in the gengzi year.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
曾子曰士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于天優優大哉禮
儀三百威儀三千
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
易
六二直方大不習无不利
凡益之道與時偕行
===
易則易知簡則易從易知則有親易從則
有功有親則可久有功則可大可久則
賢人之德可大則賢人之業易簡而天
下之理得矣天下之理得而成位乎其
中矣
易之為書也原始要終以為質也六爻相
雜唯其時物也
書
日宣三德夙夜浚明有家日嚴祇敬六德
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

曾子曰：「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。」
洋洋乎！發育萬物，峻極于天。優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千。
集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。

易

六二：直方大，不習无不利。
凡益之道，與時偕行。
易則易知，簡則易從；易知則有親，易從則有功；有親則可久，有功則可大；可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡而天下之理得矣；天下之理得，而成位乎其中矣。
易之為書也，原始要終，以為質也。六爻相雜，唯其時物也。

書

日宣三德，夙夜浚明有家；日嚴祇敬六德，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zengzi said: “A scholar must be broad-minded and resolute, for his burden is heavy and his road is long.”
How vast! It nurtures all things and towers to Heaven. How ample and great! There are three hundred rules of ceremony and three thousand rules of deportment.
To bring together the complete achievement is to begin with the sound of bronze bells and conclude with the resonance of jade chimes.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

Six in the second place: Straight, square, and great; without practice, nothing is unfavorable.
Every way of bringing increase proceeds in accord with the times.
What is easy is readily understood; what is simple is readily followed. What is readily understood wins affinity; what is readily followed achieves results. With affinity, one can endure; with results, one can become great. Endurance is the virtue of the worthy; greatness is the achievement of the worthy. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. When those principles are grasped, one establishes one’s place in their midst.
As a book, the Changes takes tracing beginnings and comprehending endings as its substance. The intermingling of the six lines depends upon the circumstances and things appropriate to their times.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

Those who daily display three virtues, profoundly manifesting them morning and night, may govern a noble house; those who daily attend solemnly and reverently to six virtues …

===

蓼彼蕭斯零露湑兮既見君子我心寫兮
燕笑語兮是以有譽處兮
維玉及瑶鞞琫容刀
穫之挃挃積之栗栗其崇如墉其比如櫛
春秋
三月公及邾儀父盟于蔑〔隱公元年〕春公
會戎于潛〔隱公二年〕冬十月齊師滅譚
譚子奔莒〔莊公十年〕春王正月丙午衛
punctuated:
亮采有邦。
說拜稽首，曰：「敢對揚天子之休命。」
星有好風，星有好雨。
昔周公師保萬民，民懷其德。往慎乃司，茲率厥常，懋昭周公之訓，惟民其乂。

詩
南有樛木，葛藟纍之。樂只君子，福履綏之。南有樛木，葛藟荒之。樂只君子，福履將之。南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。
蓼彼蕭斯，零露湑兮。既見君子，我心寫兮。燕笑語兮，是以有譽處兮。
維玉及瑶，鞞琫容刀。

translation_en:
…conduct affairs faithfully and possess a state.
Yue bowed and touched his forehead to the ground, saying: “I venture to acknowledge and extol the Son of Heaven’s gracious command.”
Some stars favor wind; some stars favor rain.
In former times, the Duke of Zhou taught and protected the myriad people, and the people cherished his virtue. Go, attend carefully to your office, follow its constant principles, and strive to make manifest the Duke of Zhou’s teachings; then the people will be well governed.

Book of Odes
In the south are trees with drooping branches; kudzu and creeping vines entwine them. Joyful is the noble gentleman; blessings bring him peace. In the south are trees with drooping branches; kudzu and creeping vines cover them. Joyful is the noble gentleman; blessings sustain him. In the south are trees with drooping branches; kudzu and creeping vines wind around them. Joyful is the noble gentleman; blessings bring him fulfillment.
Tall grows that mugwort; the falling dew glistens. Having seen the noble gentleman, my heart is relieved. We feast, laugh, and converse, and thus enjoy happiness and repose.
Jade and precious jade adorn the lower and upper scabbard fittings of the ceremonial knife.
They reap with a swishing sound and pile the harvest high. Its height is like a wall; its close-set rows are like the teeth of a comb.

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
侯燬滅邢〔僖公二十有五年〕
春齊人執鄭詹〔莊公十有七年〕
楚屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕十有一月壬
戌晉侯及秦伯戰于韓〔僖公十有五年〕
夏公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕
禮記
凡居民材必因天地寒煖燥濕廣谷大川
異制民生其間者異俗剛柔輕重遲速
異齊五味異和器械異制衣服異宜脩
===
其教不易其俗齊其政不易其宜
善教者使人繼其志
禮義立則貴賤等矣樂文同則上下和矣
好惡著則賢不肖別矣刑禁暴爵舉賢
則政均矣
故明乎其節之志以不失其事則功成而
德行立
第貳場
論
punctuated:
侯燬滅邢〔僖公二十有五年〕。
春，齊人執鄭詹〔莊公十有七年〕。
楚屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕。十有一月壬戌，晉侯及秦伯戰于韓〔僖公十有五年〕。
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕。
禮記
凡居民材，必因天地寒煖燥濕，廣谷大川異制，民生其間者異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。脩其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。
善教者，使人繼其志。
禮義立，則貴賤等矣；樂文同，則上下和矣；好惡著，則賢不肖別矣；刑禁暴，爵舉賢，則政均矣。
故明乎其節之志，以不失其事，則功成而德行立。
第貳場
論
translation_en:
…Marquis Hui of Wei destroyed Xing. 〔Twenty-fifth year of Duke Xi.〕
In spring, men of Qi seized Zhan of Zheng. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant at the army’s camp. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 In the eleventh month, on the renxu day, the Marquis of Jin and the Earl of Qin fought at Han. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xi.〕
In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Book of Rites
Whenever settling people according to their capacities, one must take account of the conditions of heaven and earth: cold and warmth, dryness and dampness. Broad valleys and great rivers differ in configuration; the people born among them differ in customs. Their dispositions differ in firmness and gentleness, lightness and gravity, slowness and speed. They blend the five flavors differently, make implements differently, and find different clothing suitable. Cultivate their instruction without changing their customs; bring their government into order without changing what suits them.
One who teaches well enables others to carry on his aspirations.
When ritual and righteousness are established, the noble and the lowly have their proper ranks. When musical forms are shared, superiors and inferiors are harmonious. When approval and disapproval are made manifest, the worthy and unworthy are distinguished. When punishments restrain violence and ranks elevate the worthy, government is equitable.
Thus, if one understands the intent of the ritual regulations and does not fail in carrying them out, achievement is completed and virtuous conduct established.
Second Session
Discourse

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君子無所不用其極
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石興廉舉孝詔〔元朔元年〕
擬唐以開府儀同三司長孫無忌為司空
誥〔貞觀七年〕
擬宋曹彬平江南羣臣賀表〔開寶八年〕
判語〔五條〕
擅離職役
得遺失物
===
上書陳言
關津留難
斷罪不當
第參場
策〔五道〕
問大學之書帝王修齊治平之道具載於
此而宋儒真德秀所著衍義又所以羽
翼聖經發揮理道治天下者不可以不
講也我
punctuated:
君子無所不用其極。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石興廉舉孝詔〔元朔元年〕。
擬唐以開府儀同三司長孫無忌為司空誥〔貞觀七年〕。
擬宋曹彬平江南羣臣賀表〔開寶八年〕。
