得遺失物。
上書陳言。
關津留難。
斷罪不當。

第參場
策〔五道〕
問：大學之書，帝王修齊治平之道具載於此，而宋儒真德秀所著《衍義》，又所以羽翼聖經，發揮理道，治天下者不可以不講也。我
translation_en:
“There is nothing in which the gentleman does not strive for the highest excellence.”

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One question from within this category [?].〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty ordering officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank to promote men of integrity and recommend men of filial conduct. 〔First year of Yuanshuo.〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Zhangsun Wuji, Palace Attendant with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies, as Minister of Works. 〔Seventh year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose a congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials in the manner of the Song dynasty on Cao Bin’s pacification of Jiangnan. 〔Eighth year of Kaibao.〕

Legal judgments 〔Five items.〕
Leaving one’s official post or assigned service without authorization.
Finding lost property.
Submitting a written statement to the throne.
Obstructing passage at checkpoints and ferries.
Improper adjudication of crimes.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔Five questions.〕
Question: The Great Learning fully sets forth the way by which emperors and kings cultivate themselves, regulate their families, govern the state, and bring peace to all under Heaven. The Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Yanyi), written by the Song Confucian scholar Zhen Dexiu, further supports the sages’ classic and elucidates its principles and way. Those who govern all under Heaven cannot neglect its study. Our…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖高皇帝甫定天下留意帝王之學因宋濂
之請
令左右大書衍義揭之兩廡以代圖畫朝夕
諦觀當時指司馬遷所論而
令大臣條析觀鼂錯所言而與侍臣講論
聖謨洋洋具在典冊不識諸士子亦有聞歟我
皇上卽位之後嘗
令侍從繙閱經書通鑑以資所聞維時輔臣
以經書微奧通鑑浩繁請以大學衍義
===
進講
皇上欣然嘉納因感賦五言古詩十韻
命二三輔臣先後賡和總而輯之名曰
翊學詩傳播中外久矣亦可得而揚其盛歟
聖子
神孫萬世相繼乃衹遹紹聞固有在也願詳述
之以爲
聖學之助
問諸子讀經雖各占其一然諸經大要則
punctuated:
聖祖高皇帝甫定天下，留意帝王之學，因宋濂之請，令左右大書衍義，揭之兩廡，以代圖畫，朝夕諦觀。當時指司馬遷所論，而令大臣條析；觀鼂錯所言，而與侍臣講論。聖謨洋洋，具在典冊，不識諸士子亦有聞歟？我皇上卽位之後，嘗令侍從繙閱經書、通鑑，以資所聞。維時輔臣以經書微奧、通鑑浩繁，請以大學衍義進講。皇上欣然嘉納，因感賦五言古詩十韻，命二三輔臣先後賡和，總而輯之，名曰《翊學詩》，傳播中外久矣，亦可得而揚其盛歟？聖子神孫，萬世相繼，乃衹遹紹聞，固有在也。願詳述之，以爲聖學之助。
問：諸子讀經，雖各占其一，然諸經大要則
translation_en:
…Our sagely progenitor, Emperor Gao, had only just pacified the realm when he turned his attention to the learning proper to emperors and kings. At Song Lian’s request, he ordered his attendants to write out the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning in large characters and display it along the two side galleries in place of paintings, so that he could examine it attentively morning and evening. On one occasion he pointed to Sima Qian’s arguments and ordered his high ministers to analyze them point by point; on another, he read Chao Cuo’s statements and discussed them with his attendant ministers. His abundant sagely counsels are fully preserved in the records. Have you candidates also heard of them?
After Our Emperor ascended the throne, he once ordered his attendants to consult the canonical books and the Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government to enrich his knowledge. At that time, his grand secretaries, considering the canonical books subtle and profound and the Comprehensive Mirror vast and voluminous, requested that they lecture to him on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning. The Emperor gladly approved their proposal. Moved by the occasion, he composed an ancient-style poem in five-character lines with ten rhymes, and ordered several grand secretaries to compose matching poems in succession. These were collected under the title Poems in Aid of Learning (Yixue shi) and have long circulated both within and beyond the court. Can you also expound upon this splendid achievement? Sagely sons and divine grandsons will succeed one another for ten thousand generations; their reverent continuation of the teachings handed down surely has its foundation here. Please discuss this in detail, to assist imperial learning.
Question: Although each of you specializes in one classic in your studies, as for the essential purport of the various classics…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所當與聞者試舉一二商之易之分上
下經也先儒多求其故矣乃朱子則以
其簡帙重大故分之果爾則宜上下經
各三十二卦矣而多下經以四何哉元
儒豫章蕭氏乃為讀易攷原謂上經一
卦不可增下經一卦不可減其說然歟
否歟可得而言歟書之分古今也今文
多艱深古文多平易古文果孔壁之舊
歟朱子則疑其序吳澄氏并疑其書是
===
歟否歟或謂張霸偽為或謂梅賾擬作
其然歟詩之有大小序自毛公以來未
之有議也而朱傳獨去之不知果能盡
得詩人之旨歟東萊呂氏畏服朱子者
也而讀詩記不從朱子而從毛氏亦何
歟春王正月春秋第一義也安國胡氏
則謂孔子以夏時冠周月不知周月其
可以夏時冠否也或謂周改月不改時
或謂時月皆改其說孰是歟周禮冬官
punctuated: 所當與聞者，試舉一二商之。《易》之分上下經也，先儒多求其故矣，乃朱子則以其簡帙重大故分之。果爾，則宜上下經各三十二卦矣，而多下經以四，何哉？元儒豫章蕭氏乃為《讀易攷原》，謂上經一卦不可增，下經一卦不可減，其說然歟否歟？可得而言歟？《書》之分古今也，今文多艱深，古文多平易，古文果孔壁之舊歟？朱子則疑其序，吳澄氏并疑其書，是歟否歟？或謂張霸偽為，或謂梅賾擬作，其然歟？《詩》之有大小序，自毛公以來未之有議也，而朱傳獨去之，不知果能盡得詩人之旨歟？東萊呂氏，畏服朱子者也，而《讀詩記》不從朱子而從毛氏，亦何歟？「春，王正月」，《春秋》第一義也。安國胡氏則謂孔子以夏時冠周月，不知周月其可以夏時冠否也？或謂周改月不改時，或謂時月皆改，其說孰是歟？《周禮》冬官
translation_en:
…are matters you ought also to know. Let us raise one or two for discussion. Earlier scholars often sought the reason why the Book of Changes was divided into upper and lower sections. Master Zhu, however, held that it was divided because its bundles of writing slips were bulky and heavy. If so, each section ought to contain thirty-two hexagrams. Why, then, does the lower section contain four more than the upper? The Yuan scholar Xiao of Yuzhang composed Investigating the Origins of the Book of Changes (Du Yi Kaoyuan), arguing that not a single hexagram could be added to the upper section or removed from the lower. Is his explanation correct or not? Can you explain it?

As for the division of the Book of Documents into Old Text and New Text, the New Text is often difficult and obscure, while the Old Text is often plain and accessible. Is the Old Text truly the ancient text recovered from the wall of Confucius’s house? Master Zhu questioned its preface, and Wu Cheng questioned the text itself as well. Were they right or wrong? Some say Zhang Ba forged it; others say Mei Ze composed it in imitation of the ancient text. Is this so?

The Greater and Lesser Prefaces to the Book of Odes had gone unchallenged since Master Mao, yet Master Zhu’s commentary alone discarded them. Could it truly have grasped the poets’ intentions in full? Master Lü of Donglai revered and deferred to Master Zhu, yet his Notes on Reading the Odes (Du Shi Ji) followed Master Mao rather than Master Zhu. Why was this?

“Spring, the first month of the king’s calendar” is the first cardinal principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Hu Anguo held that Confucius placed the Xia designation of the season before the Zhou designation of the month. But can a Zhou month properly be prefaced with a Xia season? Some say that the Zhou changed the numbering of the months but not the seasons; others say that both seasons and months were changed. Which explanation is correct? As for the Office of Winter in the Rites of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之缺久矣吳澄氏謂冬官實在五官之
中而未嘗缺也儀禮之逸多矣取小戴
投壺奔喪等篇又取大戴明堂公符而
補之其說然歟否歟或謂三禮考註非
澄作亦有所據歟此皆千古不決之疑
其陳之尊經之學亮有定見也
問易曰聖人觀乎天文以察時變又曰君
子以治曆明時而箕子傳治法九章則
曰協用五紀易書之旨果同揆歟說者
===
謂聖人協用五紀其義有三可得聞歟
成周立馮相氏掌歲月日辰星之位辨
其敘事以會天位保章氏掌五物以詔
救政訪序事不知所謂歲月日辰星之
位當何所辨日月星辰之變當何所觀
歟星土九州當何所別十二歲之相五
雲之物十有二風當何所占歟堯謹曆
象舜察璣衡後世遂有宣夜周髀蓋天
渾天之術歷代增飾其法益精又有所
punctuated:
之缺久矣。吳澄氏謂冬官實在五官之中，而未嘗缺也。儀禮之逸多矣，取小戴投壺、奔喪等篇，又取大戴明堂、公符而補之，其說然歟否歟？或謂《三禮考註》非澄作，亦有所據歟？此皆千古不決之疑，其陳之。尊經之學，亮有定見也。
問：易曰：「聖人觀乎天文，以察時變。」又曰：「君子以治曆明時。」而箕子傳治法九章，則曰：「協用五紀。」易、書之旨，果同揆歟？說者謂聖人協用五紀，其義有三，可得聞歟？成周立馮相氏，掌歲月日辰星之位，辨其敘事，以會天位；保章氏掌五物，以詔救政，訪序事。不知所謂歲月日辰星之位，當何所辨？日月星辰之變，當何所觀歟？星土九州，當何所別？十二歲之相、五雲之物、十有二風，當何所占歟？堯謹曆象，舜察璣衡，後世遂有宣夜、周髀、蓋天、渾天之術，歷代增飾，其法益精，又有所
translation_en:
…has long been missing. Wu Cheng maintained that the Office of Winter was actually contained within the other five offices and had never been missing. Much of the Ceremonies and Rites has been lost. He took such chapters as “Pitch-Pot” and “Hastening to the Funeral” from the Younger Dai’s Record of Rites, and also “Hall of Light” and “Ducal Tallies” [?] from the Elder Dai’s Record of Rites, to supplement it. Is his contention correct or not? Some say that the Examination and Annotation of the Three Ritual Classics was not written by Wu Cheng. Is there evidence for this claim as well? These are all doubts that have remained unresolved through the ages. Set forth your views on them. Through your study in reverence for the classics, you surely have reached considered judgments.
Question: The Book of Changes says, “The sage observes the patterns of heaven to discern changes in the seasons.” It also says, “The gentleman regulates the calendar and clarifies the seasons.” Yet when Jizi transmitted the nine divisions of the methods of government, he said, “Harmoniously employ the five regulators of time.” Do the purports of the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents indeed accord? Commentators say that the sage’s harmonious employment of the five regulators has three meanings. May we hear what they are? The Zhou established the office of Calendrical Astrologer (Fengxiang shi), who supervised the positions relating to the years, months, days, celestial divisions, and stars, distinguished the proper sequence of their operations, and thereby coordinated the celestial positions. The Astrologer (Baozhang shi) supervised five kinds of phenomena, advising on remedial governmental measures and investigating the ordering of affairs. Regarding these positions relating to the years, months, days, celestial divisions, and stars, what distinctions should be made? What should be observed in the changes of the sun, moon, stars, and constellations? How should the terrestrial regions corresponding to the stars and the Nine Provinces be distinguished? What should be divined from the configurations of the twelve-year cycle, the appearances of clouds of five colors, and the twelve winds? Yao attended carefully to calendrical calculations and celestial phenomena; Shun examined the jade astronomical instrument and its sighting tube. In later ages there consequently arose the methods of Infinite Empty Space (Xuanye), the Zhou Gnomon (Zhoubi), the Canopy Heaven (Gaitian), and the Spherical Heaven (Huntian). Successive dynasties elaborated them, and their methods became increasingly refined. There were also what are…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
謂簡儀仰儀者不知孰有合於唐虞之
制歟三代之曆不可考自漢以來作曆
不同而最著者曰太初曰大衍然太初
法本於律大衍數起於易其義可得而
言歟元人郭守敬所制授時曆法或謂
其度越千古然歟否歟我
朝更制大統曆而積分猶授時之數何
聖人憲天立法不為殊術以改觀而猶仍勝國
之舊歟朱子謂古人曆法疎闊而差少
===
今曆法愈密而愈差以洪武中元統之
論攷之則今日之差愈甚矣玆欲考元
定法隨時協天平秩敬授以度民庸觀
象玩占以裨王政固帝王參贊化育之
首務也諸士抱負有年豈無有達象緯
之秘而通星曆之微者耶願究言之以
觀所蘊
問嶺南山川深鬱故其靈淑所鍾多瑰奇
豪雋之士自漢以下代不乏人有累徴
punctuated:
謂簡儀、仰儀者，不知孰有合於唐虞之制歟？三代之曆不可考，自漢以來作曆不同，而最著者曰太初，曰大衍。然太初法本於律，大衍數起於易，其義可得而言歟？元人郭守敬所制授時曆法，或謂其度越千古，然歟否歟？我朝更制大統曆，而積分猶授時之數，何聖人憲天立法，不為殊術以改觀，而猶仍勝國之舊歟？朱子謂古人曆法疎闊而差少，今曆法愈密而愈差。以洪武中元統之論攷之，則今日之差愈甚矣。玆欲考元定法，隨時協天，平秩敬授，以度民庸；觀象玩占，以裨王政，固帝王參贊化育之首務也。諸士抱負有年，豈無有達象緯之秘而通星曆之微者耶？願究言之，以觀所蘊。
問：嶺南山川深鬱，故其靈淑所鍾，多瑰奇豪雋之士。自漢以下，代不乏人。有累徴
translation_en:
…called the simplified instrument and the upward-looking instrument: which of these accords with the institutions of Tang and Yu, the ages of Yao and Shun? The calendars of the Three Dynasties cannot be investigated with certainty. Since the Han, calendars have been constructed in different ways; the most celebrated are the Grand Inception Calendar (Taichu) and the Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan). Yet the methods of the Grand Inception Calendar were based on the pitch standards, while the numbers of the Great Expansion Calendar originated in the Book of Changes. Can the principles underlying these be explained? Some say that the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi), devised by Guo Shoujing of the Yuan, surpassed all those of antiquity. Is this true or not? Our dynasty newly established the Grand Unification Calendar (Datong), yet its accumulated fractions still follow the numbers of the Season-Granting Calendar. Why did the sage ruler, in modeling himself on Heaven and establishing methods, retain the practices of the preceding dynasty rather than devise a different technique to give them a new appearance?

Master Zhu said that the calendrical methods of the ancients were coarse but produced few errors, whereas those of his own day became ever more precise yet increasingly erroneous. Judged against Yuan Tong’s discussion during the Hongwu reign, the errors of the present day are even greater. We now wish to investigate the calendrical epoch and establish methods, keeping in accord with Heaven as time passes, duly ordering the seasons and reverently communicating them to the people so as to regulate their labors; and to observe celestial phenomena and ponder their prognostications in order to assist royal government. These are indeed foremost among the duties through which emperors and kings participate in and assist the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth. You gentlemen have nurtured your learning and aspirations for years: surely some among you have penetrated the secrets of celestial configurations and understood the subtleties of astronomy and calendrical calculation? Please discuss these matters fully, so that we may see the learning you possess.

Question: The mountains and rivers of Lingnan are secluded and luxuriant; thus their numinous and beneficent influences have often concentrated in men of extraordinary gifts and outstanding talent. From the Han onward, no age has lacked such men. There was one who, repeatedly summoned to office…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不起太守奏旌其門者有教授於家寇
盜戒勿相犯者有獻金鑑錄著白羽扇
賦文章風度號爲賢相者有著中興自
治萬全策獻愚忠錄文章議論切中時
病者有莊宗出獵而叩馬諫者有眞宗
東巡而獻賦頌者有排羣言宗孔子爲
韓愈所尊禮者有知品式通易學爲仁
宗所見知者有屢言邊情三使契丹者
有投匭論事南歸讀易者有進右丞相
===
不就而謚清獻者有爲時讒沮而謚忠
簡者有論王安石爲其鄉所推者有從
蘇軾爲其弟所稱者之數君子出處固
異制行亦殊其功業有崇卑文章有高
下不識可悉數而究言之歟迨至我
朝風氣日淳文物日盛衣冠禮樂之士蓋彬
彬倍昔而碧海瓊崖黃雲紫水獨當元
氣之會今卽其人而論之亦竊有可疑
者律已之嚴而不預名臣之數著述之
punctuated: 不起，太守奏旌其門者；有教授於家，寇盜戒勿相犯者；有獻金鑑錄、著白羽扇賦，文章風度號爲賢相者；有著中興自治萬全策、獻愚忠錄，文章議論切中時病者；有莊宗出獵而叩馬諫者；有眞宗東巡而獻賦頌者；有排羣言、宗孔子，爲韓愈所尊禮者；有知品式、通易學，爲仁宗所見知者；有屢言邊情、三使契丹者；有投匭論事、南歸讀易者；有進右丞相不就，而謚清獻者；有爲時讒沮，而謚忠簡者；有論王安石，爲其鄉所推者；有從蘇軾，爲其弟所稱者。之數君子，出處固異，制行亦殊，其功業有崇卑，文章有高下，不識可悉數而究言之歟？迨至我朝，風氣日淳，文物日盛，衣冠禮樂之士蓋彬彬倍昔，而碧海瓊崖、黃雲紫水獨當元氣之會。今卽其人而論之，亦竊有可疑者：律已之嚴而不預名臣之數，著述之
translation_en:
…yet would not take office, and whose gate the governor petitioned to have honored; one who taught at home, whom bandits admonished one another not to molest; one who presented the Record of the Golden Mirror and composed the Rhapsody on the White Feather Fan, and whose literary accomplishments and bearing earned him the reputation of a worthy chief councilor; one who wrote the Infallible Policies for Restoration and Self-Governance [?] and presented the Record of My Humble Loyalty, whose writings and arguments struck directly at the maladies of his time; one who stopped Zhuangzong’s horse to remonstrate when the emperor went hunting; one who presented rhapsodies and eulogies when Zhenzong toured the east; one who rejected competing teachings and honored Confucius as his master, and whom Han Yu treated with respect; one who understood regulations and procedures and was versed in the study of the Book of Changes, and whose abilities Renzong recognized; one who repeatedly reported on frontier conditions and went three times as envoy to the Khitan; one who submitted a discussion of public affairs through the petition box and returned south to study the Book of Changes; one who declined appointment as Chief Councilor of the Right and received the posthumous name Qingxian; one who was thwarted by contemporary slander and received the posthumous name Zhongjian; one whose discussions of Wang Anshi won the esteem of his native community; and one who followed Su Shi and was praised by Su Shi’s younger brother. These gentlemen differed in their decisions to serve or withdraw, and also in the conduct they prescribed for themselves. Their achievements were of greater or lesser distinction, and their writings of higher or lower quality. Might you enumerate them all and discuss them thoroughly?

Under our dynasty, prevailing customs have grown daily more upright, and cultural accomplishments daily more flourishing. Cultivated gentlemen versed in ritual and music have surely multiplied beyond those of former times. Yet the azure sea and Qiongya, the yellow clouds and purple waters [?], have especially enjoyed a convergence of primordial vitality. Now, when discussing these men individually, I venture to find certain points puzzling: one so rigorous in disciplining himself was nevertheless excluded from the ranks of celebrated ministers; one whose writings were so…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
富而不居理學之科其故何歟受崔□
之學而出處不同膺
優召之隆而受官不仕其意何歟其所謂功
業文章者又孰爲之軒輊歟諸士子居
其鄕論其世起思齊之念懷景行之心
則其講究必精而品評必當矣幸詳言
之觀所以尚友者
問廣東爲揚州要服限隔山海未易綏寧
趙佗自王即延祚滿百觀莊參之料韓
===
公之敗良不易歟伏波樓船雖幸成功
然動天下之力矣古謂用兵斯地者鮮
能大得志豈其然歟厥後有議罷徵發
而專任牧守者有議選經略使而可無
侵叛者有議雜用南北之兵而可永無
事者其說可復採而行之否歟我
國初永忠諸將略地至嶺表不勞餘力而悉
平豈
聖祖之烈將士之良自非尋常可比數歟迄今
punctuated:
富而不居理學之科，其故何歟？受崔□之學而出處不同，膺優召之隆而受官不仕，其意何歟？其所謂功業文章者，又孰爲之軒輊歟？諸士子居其鄕，論其世，起思齊之念，懷景行之心，則其講究必精，而品評必當矣。幸詳言之，觀所以尚友者。
問：廣東爲揚州要服，限隔山海，未易綏寧。趙佗自王，即延祚滿百。觀莊參之料、韓公之敗，良不易歟？伏波、樓船雖幸成功，然動天下之力矣。古謂用兵斯地者鮮能大得志，豈其然歟？厥後有議罷徵發而專任牧守者，有議選經略使而可無侵叛者，有議雜用南北之兵而可永無事者，其說可復採而行之否歟？我國初，永忠諸將略地至嶺表，不勞餘力而悉平，豈聖祖之烈、將士之良，自非尋常可比數歟？迄今
translation_en:
…so abundant in his writings, yet not placed in the category of scholars of the Learning of Principle: why was this? One received the teachings of Cui □, yet differed from him in entering office or withdrawing; another received the great honor of an imperial summons, yet accepted an appointment without taking up service. What were their intentions? As for their achievements and literary writings, who should be ranked higher or lower? You examination candidates live in their native region and consider the times in which they lived. Inspired to equal their worth and cherishing admiration for their lofty conduct, you must have investigated them closely and judged them appropriately. Please explain in detail, so that we may see how you take the ancients as your friends.
Question: Guangdong lay in the outer, or yao, zone of Yangzhou. Cut off by mountains and seas, it was not easily pacified. Zhao Tuo proclaimed himself king, and his dynasty endured a full hundred years. Considering Zhuang Can’s assessment [?] and Lord Han’s defeat [?], was this indeed no easy undertaking? Although the General Who Subdues the Waves and the General of the Towered Ships fortunately succeeded, they mobilized the strength of the whole realm. It was said in antiquity that those who campaigned in this region seldom fully attained their aims. Was this really so? Subsequently, some proposed ending military levies and requisitions and entrusting affairs entirely to the local governors; others proposed selecting a Military Commissioner, believing that incursions and rebellions could thereby be prevented; still others proposed employing northern and southern troops together, believing that lasting peace could thereby be secured. Can these proposals be adopted and implemented again? At the founding of our dynasty, Yongzhong and the other generals conquered territory as far as Lingbiao and pacified it all without exhausting their strength. Was this because the exploits of our Sagely Progenitor and the excellence of his officers and soldiers were inherently beyond ordinary comparison? Down to the present…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
黠酋遺孽叛服不常近征討雖大克捷
然數年之後又未可知其他負險而幸
未逞者猶不少也豈果無經久之道一
勞而可永逸者歟又濱海諸郡番寇為
梗邇議轉募舟兵以為戰備方覺未便
亦豈無簡要之規可靖盜而安民者歟
是誠嶺表之積患也願聞所以經畫胥
圖一方久安之計
punctuated: 黠酋遺孽，叛服不常。近征討雖大克捷，然數年之後又未可知。其他負險而幸未逞者，猶不少也。豈果無經久之道，一勞而可永逸者歟？又濱海諸郡，番寇為梗，邇議轉募舟兵以為戰備，方覺未便。亦豈無簡要之規，可靖盜而安民者歟？是誠嶺表之積患也。願聞所以經畫，胥圖一方久安之計。
translation_en: …The surviving followers of cunning chieftains alternate unpredictably between rebellion and submission. Although recent punitive campaigns have won great victories, what may happen a few years hence remains uncertain. There are still many others who rely on rugged terrain and who, fortunately, have not yet succeeded in their designs. Is there truly no enduring method by which a single exertion could secure lasting peace? Furthermore, foreign raiders trouble the coastal prefectures. A recent proposal calls for turning to the recruitment of naval troops to prepare for combat, but this is now proving impracticable. Is there likewise no simple and effective plan to quell the raiders and bring peace to the people? These are indeed longstanding afflictions of Lingbiao. We wish to hear how arrangements should be made, so that together we may devise a plan for the lasting peace of this region.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
曾子曰士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
謝頤
同考試官教諭陳批弘毅二字正指充養而
言此作精密渾融是能用心於內者
同考試官教諭吳批體認發揮深有醞藉
考試官教諭蕭批知學修辭無愧於士矣
考試官教授潘批理密辭純當是作者
===
大賢言士當大有所養以其大有所受也蓋任
重道遠則所受大矣然必弘毅爲之地焉此養
心之學不可以不大也曾子之意以爲天下之
情其示人以不廣者其居之必不寬而其謂已
爲不能者其爲之必不力而況士志於道而可
以易言哉弘毅其具矣弘也者以言乎其有容
也吾心本然之量其何有於不容而自私者每
狹之士則何可以狹也毅也者以言乎其有執
也吾心自然之能其何有於無執而自棄者恒
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
曾子曰：「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。」
謝頤
同考試官教諭陳批：「弘毅二字，正指充養而言。此作精密渾融，是能用心於內者。」
同考試官教諭吳批：「體認發揮，深有醞藉。」
考試官教諭蕭批：「知學修辭，無愧於士矣。」
考試官教授潘批：「理密辭純，當是作者。」

大賢言士當大有所養，以其大有所受也。蓋任重道遠，則所受大矣。然必弘毅爲之地焉，此養心之學不可以不大也。曾子之意，以爲天下之情，其示人以不廣者，其居之必不寬；而其謂已爲不能者，其爲之必不力。而況士志於道，而可以易言哉？弘毅其具矣。弘也者，以言乎其有容也。吾心本然之量，其何有於不容？而自私者每狹之，士則何可以狹也？毅也者，以言乎其有執也。吾心自然之能，其何有於無執？而自棄者恒
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
Master Zeng said: “A scholar must be broad-minded and resolute: his burden is heavy and his way is long.”
Xie Yi

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The two words ‘broad-minded’ and ‘resolute’ refer precisely to developing and nourishing oneself. This composition is meticulous and seamlessly integrated; its author knows how to direct his efforts inward.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “His personal understanding and exposition possess great depth and reserve.”
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “He understands learning and the cultivation of expression; he is worthy of being called a scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “The reasoning is closely wrought and the language pure. He surely deserves recognition as an accomplished writer.”

The great worthy says that a scholar must cultivate himself greatly because what he takes upon himself is great. For when the burden is heavy and the way long, what one undertakes is indeed great. Yet broad-mindedness and resolution must provide its foundation. Thus this learning devoted to nourishing the mind must be expansive. Master Zeng’s meaning is that, as human dispositions generally operate, those who display narrowness to others will necessarily lack breadth in how they conduct themselves; those who say that they themselves are incapable [?] will necessarily fail to exert themselves in their actions. How much more does this apply to a scholar whose aspirations are set upon the Way! Can one speak lightly of this? Broad-mindedness and resolution are the requisite qualities.

Broad-mindedness means having the capacity to embrace things. How could the mind’s original capacity be unable to embrace anything? Yet selfish people continually constrict it. How, then, could a scholar allow himself to be narrow? Resolution means having the capacity to hold firm. How could the mind’s natural ability lack the capacity to hold firm? Yet those who abandon themselves constantly …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
怠之士則何可以怠也是必尊德性也而廓然
存虛受之咸不使物欲得以隘吾度其斯以為
弘也矣道問學也而奮然勵必為之志不使安
肆得以勝吾强其斯以為毅也矣夫士之所以
不可不弘毅者何哉為其有體道之責焉耳是
故為器重者舉之而莫能勝士則將舉其重器
而勝之者也非弘則物大而吾小負荷之非其
任故大心則能體天下之物而重可勝矣為道
遠者行之而莫能致士則將行其遠道而致之
===
者也非毅則力竭而氣匱要約之無所歸故貞
固則能幹天下之事而遠可致矣毅而本之以
弘則近利非狃而耻於一善之安弘而出之以
毅則全體不息而自無半塗之廢此為士者所
當自勉也知此則知所以為學知所以為學則
知所以為士矣抑曾子非徒為是言也蓋舉所
自得以詔人也曾子之學專用心於內弘毅蓋
其任道之本也故能唯一貫而得統於夫子可
謂勝重任而遠到矣樊遲之鄙何足語弘冉求
punctuated:
怠之，士則何可以怠也？是必尊德性也，而廓然存虛受之咸，不使物欲得以隘吾度，其斯以為弘也矣；道問學也，而奮然勵必為之志，不使安肆得以勝吾强，其斯以為毅也矣。夫士之所以不可不弘毅者何哉？為其有體道之責焉耳。是故為器重者，舉之而莫能勝，士則將舉其重器而勝之者也。非弘則物大而吾小，負荷之非其任，故大心則能體天下之物，而重可勝矣。為道遠者，行之而莫能致，士則將行其遠道而致之者也。非毅則力竭而氣匱，要約之無所歸，故貞固則能幹天下之事，而遠可致矣。毅而本之以弘，則近利非狃，而耻於一善之安；弘而出之以毅，則全體不息，而自無半塗之廢。此為士者所當自勉也。知此則知所以為學，知所以為學則知所以為士矣。

抑曾子非徒為是言也，蓋舉所自得以詔人也。曾子之學專用心於內，弘毅蓋其任道之本也。故能唯一貫而得統於夫子，可謂勝重任而遠到矣。樊遲之鄙何足語弘？冉求
translation_en:
…allow it to grow idle. How, then, could a scholar allow himself to be idle? He must honor his moral nature, preserving an expansive openness to receive all things [?], and not allowing material desires to constrict his capacity: this is how he becomes broad-minded. He must pursue inquiry and learning, vigorously strengthening his resolve to act, and not allowing ease and indulgence to overcome his strength: this is how he becomes resolute. Why must a scholar possess both breadth of mind and resolution? Simply because he bears responsibility for embodying the Way. Thus, when a vessel is heavy, people lift it but cannot sustain its weight; the scholar is one who will lift that heavy vessel and sustain it. Without breadth of mind, things are great while he himself is small, and he is unequal to bearing them. Hence, by enlarging his mind he can embody all things under Heaven, and the heavy burden can be borne. When a road is long, people travel it but cannot reach its end; the scholar is one who will travel that long road and reach its end. Without resolution, his strength is exhausted and his vital energy depleted, and his efforts to draw things together have no final resting place [?]. Hence, through steadfast firmness he can manage the affairs of all under Heaven, and the distant destination can be reached. When resolution is rooted in breadth of mind, he is not drawn into the pursuit of immediate gain and is ashamed to rest content with a single good deed. When breadth of mind finds expression through resolution, his whole being remains unceasingly active, and he naturally never abandons his course halfway. This is what a scholar ought to urge himself to achieve. Knowing this, he knows how to pursue learning; knowing how to pursue learning, he knows how to be a scholar.

Moreover, Zengzi was not merely uttering these words: he was drawing on what he had personally attained to instruct others. In his learning, Zengzi devoted his attention wholly to the inner self; breadth of mind and resolution were the foundation on which he undertook responsibility for the Way. Thus he could assent to the teaching of the single thread running through all things and receive its unifying principle from the Master. He may indeed be said to have borne a heavy responsibility and reached a distant goal. How could Fan Chi, with his narrowness, merit discussion in terms of breadth of mind? Ran Qiu…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之畫何足語教無怪乎傳道者之不多見也矣
洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于天優優大哉禮
儀三百威儀三千
嚴文輔
同考試官學正呂批道為天地人物之紀洋
洋優優正言道之所以大處子思之意為學者立
本此篇發揮真切而歸重于凝道之功錄之
考試官教諭蕭批詞意明鬯不襲塵語
考試官教授潘批清雅可誦
===
中庸論聖人之道至大而至精也夫與天而為
一可謂至大矣體物而不遺可謂至精矣不有
以見聖人之道之大乎中庸二十七章先言聖
人之道以發君子之學也蓋謂道必有所寄體
於人而盡於聖人者也故以其道之極於至大
者言之夫道流動充滿洋洋焉耳矣生長收藏
天之用本如是也而高明覆物道與之同其用
故知化而天焉昭焉陰陽和而萬物皆得性命
正而百昌咸遂則聖人之道歸焉耳穹窿覆幬
punctuated:
之畫，何足語教？無怪乎傳道者之不多見也矣。

洋洋乎！發育萬物，峻極于天。優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千。
嚴文輔

同考試官學正呂批：道為天地人物之紀，洋洋優優，正言道之所以大處。子思之意，為學者立本。此篇發揮真切，而歸重于凝道之功，錄之。
考試官教諭蕭批：詞意明鬯，不襲塵語。
考試官教授潘批：清雅可誦。

中庸論聖人之道，至大而至精也。夫與天而為一，可謂至大矣；體物而不遺，可謂至精矣。不有以見聖人之道之大乎？中庸二十七章，先言聖人之道，以發君子之學也。蓋謂道必有所寄，體於人而盡於聖人者也。故以其道之極於至大者言之，夫道流動充滿，洋洋焉耳矣。生長收藏，天之用本如是也；而高明覆物，道與之同其用，故知化而天焉昭焉。陰陽和而萬物皆得，性命正而百昌咸遂，則聖人之道歸焉耳。穹窿覆幬，
translation_en:
…how could his drawing a limit to his efforts qualify as instruction [?]? No wonder transmitters of the Way are so seldom seen.

“How vast and overflowing! It brings forth and nourishes the myriad things and reaches up to Heaven. How abundant and great! The rules of ceremony number three hundred, and the rules of deportment three thousand.”
By Yan Wenfu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lü, School Director: “The Way is the ordering principle of Heaven, Earth, human beings, and things. ‘Vast and overflowing’ and ‘abundant’ describe precisely what makes the Way great. Zisi’s intention was to establish a foundation for learners. This essay develops that meaning truly and precisely, placing ultimate emphasis on the work of giving the Way firm embodiment. Selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “The language and meaning are clear and fluent, without borrowing stale expressions.”
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “Pure and elegant, worthy of recitation.”

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way of the sage as supremely great and supremely subtle. To be one with Heaven may indeed be called supremely great; to embody all things, leaving none out, may indeed be called supremely subtle. Does this not enable us to perceive the greatness of the sage’s Way? Chapter twenty-seven of the Doctrine of the Mean first speaks of the sage’s Way in order to elucidate the learning of the noble person. Its point is that the Way must have something in which to reside: it is embodied in human beings and reaches its fullness in the sage.

Thus, speaking of this Way as it reaches the utmost greatness, the Way flows and fills all things—vast and overflowing, that is all. Bringing forth, nurturing, gathering in, and storing away: such are inherently the operations of Heaven. Lofty and luminous, covering all things, the Way shares those operations. Thus, through understanding transformation, Heaven is made manifest [?]. When yin and yang are harmonious and the myriad things each obtain their due, when their natures and allotted lives are set right and all living things flourish, this is where the sage’s Way finds its fulfillment. The vault arching overhead and sheltering all…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天之體本如是也而高明配天道與之同其體
故盡性而天爲參焉神無聲臭而一理爲之貫
通道無際涯而兩間爲之充塞則聖人之道極
焉耳若然則斯道也其大無外所謂天下莫能
載焉者此矣又以其道之入於至小者言之夫
道充足有餘優優焉耳矣立經制而總綱維之
要是禮儀也舉其凡則三百而道無乎不在用
之朝廷邦國而人道羣達之閨門鄉黨而彜倫
敘有本有文而禮不爲虛器也致委曲而盡節
===
目之詳是威儀也極其數則三千而道無乎不
該周旋裼襲節文之而不忒升降上下範圍之
而不過至精至密而禮不爲粗迹也若然則斯
道也其小無內所謂天下莫能破焉者此矣夫
語大遺小語小遺大則道有不備矣兼小大而
一之非聖道之大而能若是乎嘗論之聖人者
道之管也乃君子則與道爲二必有希聖之功
而後有凝道之德夫聖人曷可希也吾德性所
賦與聖人一而已故尊吾德性而學之所以希
punctuated: 天之體本如是也，而高明配天，道與之同其體，故盡性而天爲參焉。神無聲臭，而一理爲之貫通；道無際涯，而兩間爲之充塞，則聖人之道極焉耳。若然，則斯道也，其大無外，所謂天下莫能載焉者，此矣。又以其道之入於至小者言之，夫道充足有餘，優優焉耳矣。立經制而總綱維之要，是禮儀也。舉其凡則三百，而道無乎不在。用之朝廷邦國而人道羣，達之閨門鄉黨而彜倫敘，有本有文，而禮不爲虛器也。致委曲而盡節目之詳，是威儀也。極其數則三千，而道無乎不該。周旋裼襲，節文之而不忒；升降上下，範圍之而不過。至精至密，而禮不爲粗迹也。若然，則斯道也，其小無內，所謂天下莫能破焉者，此矣。夫語大遺小，語小遺大，則道有不備矣。兼小大而一之，非聖道之大而能若是乎？嘗論之：聖人者，道之管也。乃君子則與道爲二，必有希聖之功，而後有凝道之德。夫聖人曷可希也？吾德性所賦，與聖人一而已。故尊吾德性而學之，所以希
translation_en:
…Such is Heaven’s inherent form. Lofty and luminous, matching Heaven, the Way shares its form; thus, by fully realizing one’s nature, one forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. The numinous has neither sound nor scent, yet a single principle runs throughout it; the Way has neither limit nor boundary, yet fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Here the Way of the sage reaches its utmost extent. If this is so, this Way is so great that nothing lies outside it. This is what is meant by saying that nothing under Heaven can contain it.

Consider also how this Way enters into the very smallest things. The Way is abundant beyond sufficiency, ample indeed. Establishing enduring institutions and encompassing the essentials of their governing framework: these are the ritual observances. Enumerated in their broad divisions, they number three hundred, and the Way is present in every one. Applied at court and in the states, they bring people together in the human Way [?]; extended to households and local communities, they set the enduring human relationships in order. Having both foundation and outward refinement, ritual is no empty vessel. Attending to every subtlety and exhausting the details of every particular: these are the rules of ceremonial deportment. Counted in full, they number three thousand, and the Way encompasses them all. In turning and moving, in exposing or covering the garment, they provide measured forms that admit no error; in ascending and descending, moving up and down, they establish bounds that admit no excess. Utterly fine and exact, ritual is no mere crude outward trace. If this is so, this Way is so small that nothing lies within it. This is what is meant by saying that nothing under Heaven can divide it further.

To speak of the great while omitting the small, or of the small while omitting the great, would leave the Way incomplete. Could it thus embrace the small and the great and unite them, were it not for the greatness of the sagely Way? I have considered this: the sage is the conduit of the Way. The gentleman, however, remains distinct from the Way. Only through the effort of aspiring to sagehood can he acquire the virtue that brings the Way to full realization. How, then, can one aspire to become a sage? The moral nature with which I am endowed is simply the same as the sage’s. Thus, honoring my moral nature and pursuing learning is the means by which I aspire…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也德修道凝不異於聖人矣若曰聖本生知非
學可至則違道遠矣所以君子貴自勉也
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
郭敬賢
同考試官教諭黃批題本承上起下蓋聲振
二字即含蓄聖智二義作者漫以始終條理牽繞
可厭獨是篇體認傳註發揮明白故錄以式
考試官教諭蕭批純正
考試官教授潘批典實
===
大賢明乎樂之備者而揭其要於二音焉蓋金
聲玉振大成之樂明矣不揭言之何以喻聖之
為大乎孔子所以異於三子者如此且夫人有
大聖樂有大成不觀其深則擬倫有未至也何
也蓋一樂之奏而眾音以成故成矣必謂之大
也眾音之成而一樂以備故大矣又謂之集焉
若是者豈其萃眾和而遺節奏之妙包羣美而
失綱紀之宜也蓋八音之中有定屬焉惟金以
聲之乎蓋洪以亮者金也而聲則金之職也金
punctuated:
也。德修道凝，不異於聖人矣。若曰聖本生知，非學可至，則違道遠矣。所以君子貴自勉也。

集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。
郭敬賢

同考試官教諭黃批：題本承上起下，蓋聲振二字，即含蓄聖智二義。作者漫以始終條理牽繞，可厭。獨是篇體認傳註，發揮明白，故錄以式。
考試官教諭蕭批：純正。
考試官教授潘批：典實。

大賢明乎樂之備者，而揭其要於二音焉。蓋金聲玉振，大成之樂明矣。不揭言之，何以喻聖之為大乎？孔子所以異於三子者如此。且夫人有大聖，樂有大成，不觀其深，則擬倫有未至也。何也？蓋一樂之奏，而眾音以成，故成矣，必謂之大也；眾音之成，而一樂以備，故大矣，又謂之集焉。若是者，豈其萃眾和而遺節奏之妙，包羣美而失綱紀之宜也？蓋八音之中，有定屬焉。惟金以聲之乎？蓋洪以亮者，金也，而聲則金之職也。金
translation_en:
…to aspire to sagehood. Once virtue is cultivated and the Way firmly established, one is no different from a sage. To say that sages inherently possess knowledge from birth and that their attainment cannot be reached through learning is to depart far from the Way. This is why the gentleman prizes exerting himself.

“To bring together the great completion is to sound the metal bells and conclude with the jade chimes.”
Guo Jingxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: The topic carries forward the preceding passage and introduces what follows. The two words “sound” and “conclude” implicitly contain the two meanings of sagehood and wisdom. Writers tiresomely entangle themselves in loose discussions of ordering the beginning and the end. This essay alone grasps the commentaries and develops their meaning clearly; it is therefore included as a model.
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: Pure and orthodox.
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: Grounded in the classics and substantial.

The great worthy [Mencius] understood what makes music complete and disclosed its essentials through two sounds. With the sounding of metal bells and the concluding jade chimes, music’s great completion becomes clear. Without explicitly setting this forth, how could he illustrate the greatness of the sage? Such is what distinguishes Confucius from the three masters.

Among men there is the great sage; in music there is the great completion. Unless one examines their profundity, the comparison will fall short. Why? When a piece of music is performed, its many sounds achieve completion together. Thus, though it is a “completion,” it must be called “great.” When the many sounds reach completion, the whole piece of music is fully realized. Thus, though it is “great,” it is further described as “brought together.” Could such music gather all harmonies yet omit the subtlety of rhythm, or encompass every beauty yet lose the proper ordering of its structure?

Among the eight classes of musical instruments, each has its assigned function. Is it not metal alone that sounds the opening? For metal is resonant and clear, and sounding the opening is its office. Metal …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以聲之則鬱者宣之而使達隱者洩之而使光
蓋一音鏘然而眾音之精華於是乎呈露矣又
惟玉以振之乎蓋清以越者玉也而振則玉之
能也玉以振之則渙者翕之而使專紛者凝之
而使固蓋一音詘然而眾音之美實於是乎斂
藏矣於其聲也若眾音未知而啓以知也其陽
一噓而萬物皆春乎於其振也若眾音未能而
翼以能也其陰一吸而萬物皆秋乎蓋向非金
聲則不能相率而其失也靡向非玉振則不能
===
===
相成而其失也流亦何取乎大成也哉吁此金
石所以為重而聲振又大成之要與可以觀樂
亦可以觀聖人矣雖然又即樂而評焉三子一
音耳不得為大成猶未為無成也蓋亞於大成
者矣使季札聽之其在齊陳之間乎乃孔子則
韶矣惜乎位之不舜也故曰韶盡美矣又盡善
也而聽之三月不知肉味其志可知也於乎大
成不可作矣而聖智未為無所寓也固萬世之
金聲玉振也善學者毋自瞶焉可矣
punctuated: 以聲之，則鬱者宣之而使達，隱者洩之而使光。蓋一音鏘然，而眾音之精華於是乎呈露矣。又惟玉以振之乎？蓋清以越者玉也，而振則玉之能也。玉以振之，則渙者翕之而使專，紛者凝之而使固。蓋一音詘然，而眾音之美實於是乎斂藏矣。於其聲也，若眾音未知而啓以知也，其陽一噓而萬物皆春乎？於其振也，若眾音未能而翼以能也，其陰一吸而萬物皆秋乎？蓋向非金聲，則不能相率，而其失也靡；向非玉振，則不能相成，而其失也流。亦何取乎大成也哉？吁！此金石所以為重，而聲振又大成之要與！可以觀樂，亦可以觀聖人矣。雖然，又即樂而評焉：三子一音耳，不得為大成，猶未為無成也，蓋亞於大成者矣。使季札聽之，其在齊陳之間乎？乃孔子則韶矣，惜乎位之不舜也！故曰：「韶盡美矣，又盡善也。」而聽之三月不知肉味，其志可知也。於乎！大成不可作矣，而聖智未為無所寓也，固萬世之金聲玉振也。善學者毋自瞶焉可矣。
translation_en:
…by sounding them, it releases what is pent up and lets it flow freely, discloses what is hidden and makes it shine. One ringing note thus reveals the finest qualities of all the sounds. And is it not jade alone that brings them to completion? For jade is clear and far-reaching in tone, and bringing the music to completion is its capacity. When jade brings them to completion, it gathers what is dispersed into concentration and consolidates what is confused into stability. With one subsiding note [?], the beauty and substance of all the sounds are thus gathered and stored within. When the metal sounds, it is as though the other sounds did not yet know, and it enlightened them with knowledge: is this not like a single outward breath of yang bringing spring to all things? When the jade brings the music to completion, it is as though the other sounds were not yet capable, and it aided them with ability: is this not like a single inward breath of yin bringing autumn to all things? Without the sounding of metal at the outset, the sounds could not lead one another onward, and their failing would be weakness; without the concluding resonance of jade, they could not bring one another to completion, and their failing would be diffusion. What claim, then, could there be to a great consummation?

Ah! This is why metal and stone instruments are so important, and why the opening sound and concluding resonance are essential to the great consummation! Through them one may understand music, and also the sage. Nevertheless, let us assess the three masters again in terms of music. Each is but a single sound. Though they cannot constitute a great consummation, they are not without accomplishment; they stand just below that great consummation. If Ji Zha heard them, would he place them somewhere between the music of Qi and Chen? Confucius, however, is the Shao music itself. Alas, he did not occupy Shun’s position! Thus he said, “The Shao is perfectly beautiful, and also perfectly good.” And when he heard it, for three months he did not know the taste of meat: from this we can understand his aspirations. Alas! The great consummation can no longer be performed, yet sagely wisdom is not without a place in which to reside. It is indeed the sounding of metal and the concluding resonance of jade for all ages. Those who learn well need only refrain from making themselves deaf to it.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
易
六二直方大不習无不利
嚴文輔
同考試官學正吕批直方二字類能言之至
大與不習无不利處輒纏繞可厭此作得肯宜錄
爲式
考試官敎諭蕭批體用之學發明殆盡

矣盛德不容於强爲也六二有直方大之德而
利於行也夫焉有所倚哉且坤之道以柔順正
固爲直以賦形有定爲方以德合無疆爲大而
六二則得夫坤道之純者故周公繫其辭曰天
下之道盡於性矣君子之學率其性焉止矣坤
之六二其有得於率性之學者乎蓋其天性融
而本體不虧涵養純而人爲不鑿語乎其内則
無反也無側也渾然而存天下之正矣語乎其
外則無適也無莫也秩然而通天下之故矣然
punctuated:
易
六二，直方大，不習无不利。
嚴文輔

translation_en:
Book of Changes
Six in the second place: Straight, square, great; without practice, nothing is unfavorable.
Yan Wenfu 嚴文輔
Associate Examiner Lü, School Instructor, comments: “Most candidates can discuss the two words ‘straight’ and ‘square’; when they reach ‘great’ and ‘without practice, nothing is unfavorable,’ they invariably become tiresomely tangled. This composition gets to the heart of the matter and should be recorded as a model.”
Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates the learning of substance and function almost exhaustively.”
Examiner Pan, Professor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”
When the sage appended the line statements to Kun, he necessarily made manifest the fullness of its virtue and the ease of its activity. How utterly full virtue excludes forced effort! Six in the second place possesses the virtues of straightness, squareness, and greatness, and acts advantageously. What could it need to depend upon? The Way of Kun takes yielding compliance and upright firmness as straightness, the definite forms it bestows as squareness, and virtue that accords with the boundless as greatness. Six in the second place embodies the purity of the Way of Kun. Thus the Duke of Zhou appended its statement, saying: “The Way of all under Heaven is fully contained in our nature. The learning of the gentleman consists solely in following that nature. Might six in the second place of Kun have attained something of this learning of following one’s nature? Its Heaven-endowed nature is harmonious, and its original substance unimpaired; its nurturing is pure, and human contrivance does not chip away at it. Speaking of its inward aspect, there is neither contrariness nor deviation: in undivided wholeness it preserves the rectitude of all under Heaven. Speaking of its outward aspect, there is neither predisposition for nor predisposition against: in orderly fashion it comprehends the affairs of all under Heaven. Yet…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
且精微徹性命之原而易簡合以成德上下極
同流之妙而久大渾乎無疆則天地之高深聖
人之神化一以貫之矣其直方大也何如夫天
下無不可能之事人每外求而不足耳六二誠
有是德則焉往而不利哉但見埋本諸素而幾
無不通誠妙於為而施無不裕其靜也藏諸用
也先事而具夫通變之權其動也顯諸仁也因
感而彰吾順應之妙心即體而欲即用以時措
之誠有不思不勉而從容中道者矣豈待學之
===
而後利哉體即道而用即義推而行之誠有從
心所欲而不踰矩者矣豈必慮焉而後能哉夫
是以知有盛德者必有大業而所養不純者亦
無惑乎臨事而困也占坤六二者尚知其所以
不習之故乎愚甞因而求之率性以為行者其
行自利因性以為學者其學易成六二之德固
其所性之純不可誣而近性之學實居多也蓋
天地之性不專一則不能直遂不翕聚則不能
發散而夫人之性得之於靜者未始不失之於
punctuated: 且精微徹性命之原，而易簡合以成德；上下極同流之妙，而久大渾乎無疆，則天地之高深、聖人之神化，一以貫之矣。其直方大也何如？夫天下無不可能之事，人每外求而不足耳。六二誠有是德，則焉往而不利哉？但見埋本諸素而幾無不通，誠妙於為而施無不裕。其靜也，藏諸用也，先事而具夫通變之權；其動也，顯諸仁也，因感而彰吾順應之妙。心即體而欲即用，以時措之，誠有不思不勉而從容中道者矣，豈待學之而後利哉？體即道而用即義，推而行之，誠有從心所欲而不踰矩者矣，豈必慮焉而後能哉？夫是以知有盛德者必有大業，而所養不純者，亦無惑乎臨事而困也。占坤六二者，尚知其所以不習之故乎？愚甞因而求之：率性以為行者，其行自利；因性以為學者，其學易成。六二之德，固其所性之純不可誣，而近性之學實居多也。蓋天地之性，不專一則不能直遂，不翕聚則不能發散，而夫人之性，得之於靜者，未始不失之於
translation_en:
… Moreover, its subtle refinement penetrates to the source of human nature and destiny, while ease and simplicity unite to perfect its virtue. Above and below, it fully realizes the marvel of flowing together with Heaven and Earth, while its endurance and greatness merge into boundlessness. Thus the height and depth of Heaven and Earth and the sage’s wondrous transformations are threaded together by a single principle. How straight, square, and great it is! There is nothing in the world that cannot be accomplished; people merely seek outside themselves and so fall short. If the six in the second place truly possesses this virtue, where could it go without benefit? We see only that its grounding lies in the unadorned [?], and no incipient impulse fails to find passage; sincerity works wondrously in action, and its application is everywhere abundant. In stillness, it is stored within its functioning: before affairs arise, it already possesses the capacity to respond to change. In movement, it is manifest in benevolence: in response to stimuli, it reveals the marvel of our responsive accord. The mind is substance, and desire is function. Put into practice at the appropriate time, this truly yields an effortless accordance with the Way, without deliberation or striving. How could benefit depend on first learning it? Substance is the Way, and function is righteousness. Extended into practice, this truly enables one to follow the heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds. How could ability depend on first deliberating?

From this we know that those of abundant virtue necessarily accomplish great works; nor should we be puzzled when those whose self-cultivation is impure find themselves at a loss when confronted with affairs. Do those who divine by the six in the second place of Kun understand why it requires no practice? I have ventured to pursue this further: those who follow their nature in their conduct find that their conduct proceeds smoothly of itself; those who base their learning on their nature readily bring that learning to completion. As for the virtue of the six in the second place, the purity of its inherent nature certainly cannot be denied, yet learning that draws one close to that nature accounts for a great deal. For the nature of Heaven and Earth cannot proceed straight ahead unless it is concentrated and unified, and cannot spread outward unless it first gathers inward. As for human nature, what is gained in stillness is ever liable to be lost in …

易則易知，簡則易從。易知則有親，易從則有功。有親則可久，有功則可大。可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡而天下之理得矣，天下之理得而成位乎其中矣。
陳大本
同考試官學正呂批：發明易簡德業數字，已見體認，後段筆力尤非衆作可到。
考試官教諭蕭批：詞氣疏暢而精密，可式。佳士！佳士！
考試官教授潘批：簡潔老健。

translation_en:
…in activity; thus the gentleman’s learning prizes taking stillness as its guiding principle. The six in the second place embodies the way of Kun, the utmost stillness under Heaven. Much inward nurturing and little outward distraction: is this not why its way of moving in accord with circumstances brings benefit without practice?

“Ease makes it easy to understand; simplicity makes it easy to follow. Being easy to understand wins affinity; being easy to follow brings achievement. With affinity, one can endure; with achievement, one can become great. Endurance constitutes the worthy person’s virtue; greatness constitutes the worthy person’s undertaking. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. Once those principles are grasped, one establishes one’s position in their midst.”

Chen Daben.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lü, School Director: “His elucidation of the terms ‘ease,’ ‘simplicity,’ ‘virtue,’ and ‘undertaking’ already reveals an understanding grounded in personal realization. The force of his writing in the latter section is especially beyond the reach of the other compositions.”

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “The expression and flow are free and fluent, yet precise and close-knit: worthy of emulation. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “Concise, mature, and vigorous.”

Fully embody the virtues of Qian and Kun, and the way of worthies and sages lies therein. The principles of ease and simplicity have their foundation in Qian and Kun, but their embodiment rests with human beings. Considering their ultimate destination, can one not gradually attain the stature of worthies and sages? The Great Commentary discusses the principles of Qian and Kun and how human beings embody both. It is as though it said: the ease and simplicity of Qian and Kun are already demonstrated in the achievements of the creative transformation of things, while we…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人之德業在盡乎效法之道是故易乾德也心
體之光大而不艱深者卽此易也人之存心也
以之則人情自通矣不易知耶簡坤德也心體
之平直而不矯僞者卽此簡也人之應物也以
之則人情自附矣不易從耶惟易知則同心者
衆益見其可親易從則多助之至自易於成功
矣由是驗人之同則自信益篤而德可久用人
之長則衆善悉有而業可大矣兼體易簡之道
不亦庶幾矣乎故語其所就也可久雖未至於
===
上達而深造者自得之機也可大雖未底於成
功而積累者富有之漸也德崇業廣皆可以稱
賢矣要諸其極也則成性存而道義出通之易
簡而无遺人道盡而天地參同諸造化而无外
功深理得誠足以爲聖矣賢聖所造不同易簡
之理固非二也吁易簡足以盡乾坤之德而復
有以該聖功之全天人合一之妙有如是夫考
之子思子亦甞有致中和之論矣其要惟在於
喜怒哀樂之間卽夫子易簡之說也夫子著其
punctuated: 人之德業在盡乎效法之道。是故易，乾德也；心體之光大而不艱深者，卽此易也。人之存心也以之，則人情自通矣，不易知耶？簡，坤德也；心體之平直而不矯僞者，卽此簡也。人之應物也以之，則人情自附矣，不易從耶？惟易知，則同心者衆，益見其可親；易從，則多助之至，自易於成功矣。由是驗人之同，則自信益篤，而德可久；用人之長，則衆善悉有，而業可大矣。兼體易簡之道，不亦庶幾矣乎？故語其所就也，可久雖未至於上達，而深造者自得之機也；可大雖未底於成功，而積累者富有之漸也。德崇業廣，皆可以稱賢矣。要諸其極也，則成性存而道義出，通之易簡而无遺；人道盡而天地參，同諸造化而无外。功深理得，誠足以爲聖矣。賢聖所造不同，易簡之理固非二也。吁！易簡足以盡乾坤之德，而復有以該聖功之全，天人合一之妙有如是夫！考之子思子，亦甞有致中和之論矣。其要惟在於喜怒哀樂之間，卽夫子易簡之說也。夫子著其
translation_en:
…our virtue and achievements lie in fully realizing the way of emulating them. Thus ease is the virtue of Qian: the luminous breadth of the mind’s underlying constitution, free of difficulty and obscurity, is precisely this ease. When people preserve their minds through it, others’ feelings naturally find understanding. Is this not easy to know? Simplicity is the virtue of Kun: the evenness and uprightness of the mind’s underlying constitution, free of affectation and falsity, is precisely this simplicity. When people respond to things through it, others naturally become attached to them. Is this not easy to follow? Because one is easy to know, many share one’s mind, making one’s approachability still more apparent; because one is easy to follow, abundant assistance arrives, naturally making success easy. Through this, finding confirmation in others’ agreement, one’s confidence grows firmer and one’s virtue can endure; employing others’ strengths, one possesses all their various excellences and one’s achievements can become great. In embodying together the way of ease and simplicity, does one not come close to the ideal?

Thus, speaking of what is attained: the capacity to endure, though not yet amounting to higher understanding, offers those who study deeply the opening for personal realization; the capacity for greatness, though not yet amounting to completed achievement, offers those who accumulate their efforts a gradual advance toward abundant possession. Those whose virtue is exalted and whose achievements are extensive may all be called worthy. Considering the ultimate attainment, however, one preserves one’s perfected nature, from which the Way and righteousness issue forth, comprehending everything through ease and simplicity without omission; one fulfills the human way and forms a triad with Heaven and Earth, becoming one with the transformations of creation, with nothing left outside. With profound accomplishment and grasp of principle, one is indeed fit to be a sage. Worthies and sages differ in their attainments, but the principle of ease and simplicity is certainly not two different things.

Ah! Ease and simplicity suffice to fulfill the virtues of Qian and Kun, and also encompass the entirety of sagely accomplishment. Such is the marvel of Heaven and humanity united as one! Examining the teachings of Master Zisi, we find that he too once discussed bringing equilibrium and harmony to their fullest realization. Its essential point lies solely within joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure: this is precisely the Master’s teaching of ease and simplicity. The Master set forth its…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
功效之大而未悉其求得之方觀子思戒懼愼
獨之訓可以相發明矣私欲不蔽則吾心易簡
之體自明賢而聖聖而天固馴以致之者也欲
盡易簡之道宜於戒懼愼獨始
書
日宣三德夙夜浚明有家日嚴祇敬六德
亮采有邦
郭敬賢
同考試官教諭黃批浚明亮采正見德宜於
治不涉效上說刻此以釋執經者之疑
考試官教諭蕭批得虞廷任德之旨
考試官教授潘批辭簡明而意明盡
===
大臣言常德者皆宜於治以為官人者告也夫
致治本於德也德不同而皆宜於家邦之治則
官人者宜知所重矣皐陶陳知人之謨者如此
今夫以人圖治者政之要也以德詔爵者君之
柄也人君之立政其可以弗審於是耶是故九
德有其三其德彰矣而未大也夫能不以三德
punctuated:
功效之大，而未悉其求得之方。觀子思戒懼愼獨之訓，可以相發明矣。私欲不蔽，則吾心易簡之體自明；賢而聖，聖而天，固馴以致之者也。欲盡易簡之道，宜於戒懼愼獨始。

書
「日宣三德，夙夜浚明有家；日嚴祇敬六德，亮采有邦。」
郭敬賢
同考試官教諭黃批：「浚明亮采，正見德宜於治，不涉效上說。刻此以釋執經者之疑。」
考試官教諭蕭批：「得虞廷任德之旨。」
考試官教授潘批：「辭簡明而意明盡。」

大臣言常德者皆宜於治，以為官人者告也。夫致治本於德也，德不同而皆宜於家邦之治，則官人者宜知所重矣。皐陶陳知人之謨者如此。今夫以人圖治者，政之要也；以德詔爵者，君之柄也。人君之立政，其可以弗審於是耶？是故九德有其三，其德彰矣，而未大也。夫能不以三德
translation_en:
…the greatness of their effects, but did not fully explain the means of attaining them. Zisi’s teachings on vigilance and apprehension, and on watchfulness over oneself when alone, can illuminate this teaching in turn. If selfish desires do not obscure it, the essential ease and simplicity of our mind will naturally become clear. From worthiness to sagehood, and from sagehood to Heaven: these are indeed attained through gradual progress. To realize fully the Way of ease and simplicity, one should begin with vigilance and apprehension, and with watchfulness over oneself when alone.

Book of Documents
“One who daily displays three virtues may profoundly illuminate them morning and night and possess a noble house; one who daily attends with reverent care to six virtues may discharge his duties faithfully and possess a state.”
Guo Jingxian
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “‘Profoundly illuminating’ and ‘discharging duties faithfully’ precisely show that virtue is suited to governing. The discussion does not concern effects [?]. This is printed to resolve the doubts of those who hold fast to the canonical text.”
Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “It grasps the intent of appointing men for their virtue at Shun’s court.”
Examiner Pan, Professor, comments: “The wording is concise and clear, and the meaning lucid and fully expressed.”

The great minister said that all those whose virtue is constant are suited to governing, offering this as counsel to those who appoint officials. Bringing about good government is rooted in virtue. Though virtues differ, they are all suited to governing noble houses and states; those who appoint officials should therefore know what to value. Such was Gaoyao’s counsel concerning the discernment of men.

Now, seeking good government through the right men is the essential task of administration; conferring ranks according to virtue is the ruler’s prerogative. In establishing his government, how could a ruler fail to examine this carefully? Thus, if a man possesses three of the nine virtues, his virtue is manifest, but not yet great. If he can avoid, on account of these three virtues…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
苟安而日宣之加懋昭之功于以擴充其所未
至務緝熈之學于以推廣其所未能蓋愈昭明
則愈盛大而德之在我斯有常矣若而人也使
之有家則能以三德而推之于政含章以從事
吾見夙夜之匪懈也而以致明作之功精白以
承休吾見朝夕之靡遑也而以翊寅亮之業蓋
其所浚明者即其所宣著者出之也而謂家之
政有弗成耶九德有其六其德彰矣而未恒也
夫能不以六德自滿而日嚴之寅恭自度範之
===
使歸于正而不踰莊敬日强約之使合於中而
不放蓋愈檢束則愈精密而德之在我斯有常
矣若而人也使之有邦則能以六德而推之于
政神以盡能而經制之顯設者錯爲經緯之章
化以盡利而禮樂之昭宣者奕爲休明之治蓋
其所亮采者即其所嚴敬者出之也而謂邦之
政有弗成耶夫三德宜于家是可爲大夫矣六
德宜于邦是可爲諸侯矣德不同而職因以異
此固官人者所當辨歟吁吾以是知隆古之盛
punctuated:
苟安而日宣之，加懋昭之功，于以擴充其所未至；務緝熈之學，于以推廣其所未能。蓋愈昭明則愈盛大，而德之在我斯有常矣。若而人也，使之有家，則能以三德而推之于政。含章以從事，吾見夙夜之匪懈也，而以致明作之功；精白以承休，吾見朝夕之靡遑也，而以翊寅亮之業。蓋其所浚明者，即其所宣著者出之也，而謂家之政有弗成耶？

九德有其六，其德彰矣而未恒也。夫能不以六德自滿而日嚴之，寅恭自度，範之使歸于正而不踰；莊敬日强，約之使合於中而不放。蓋愈檢束則愈精密，而德之在我斯有常矣。若而人也，使之有邦，則能以六德而推之于政。神以盡能，而經制之顯設者錯爲經緯之章；化以盡利，而禮樂之昭宣者奕爲休明之治。蓋其所亮采者，即其所嚴敬者出之也，而謂邦之政有弗成耶？

夫三德宜于家，是可爲大夫矣；六德宜于邦，是可爲諸侯矣。德不同而職因以異，此固官人者所當辨歟？吁！吾以是知隆古之盛
translation_en:
…rest content, but instead daily makes them manifest, adding efforts to illuminate them fully so as to extend his virtue into areas it has not yet reached, and diligently pursuing the learning that sustains and brightens it so as to develop capacities not yet attained. The brighter his virtue becomes, the greater it grows; thus the virtue within him acquires constancy. If such a man is entrusted with a noble household and its domain, he can extend his three virtues into its government. Keeping his excellence within as he undertakes his duties, he is, I see, unremitting day and night, thereby achieving the work of enlightened action. With a pure heart he receives favor; he is, I see, without respite morning and evening, thereby assisting the work of reverent service. For what he brings forth in manifest deeds proceeds from the virtue he has deeply illuminated. Could one then say that the government of his household would fail?

A man who possesses six of the nine virtues has made his virtue manifest, but has not yet made it constant. If he can avoid complacency over his six virtues and daily discipline them, reverently examining himself and bringing himself under rules that direct him toward what is right without overstepping, he will grow stronger each day through dignity and reverence, restraining himself to accord with the mean without becoming unbridled. The more he exercises restraint, the more refined and exact his virtue becomes; thus the virtue within him acquires constancy. If such a man is entrusted with a state, he can extend his six virtues into its government. Through a spirit-like efficacy he fully realizes his abilities, and the institutions he visibly establishes interweave into a pattern of warp and weft. Through transforming influence he fully realizes benefits, and the rites and music he clearly promulgates unfold into splendid and enlightened government. For his faithful discharge of duties proceeds from the virtue he has cultivated with rigor and reverence. Could one then say that the government of his state would fail?

Three virtues fit a man to govern a noble household: he may therefore serve as a grand master. Six virtues fit a man to govern a state: he may therefore serve as a regional lord. Virtues differ, and offices accordingly differ. Surely this is what those who appoint men to office ought to distinguish? Ah! From this I understand the flourishing of high antiquity…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也皐陶言知人必曰九德而夏之籲俊亦曰迪
知忱恂于九德之行至于成湯之克卽文武之
克知灼見凡以德而已彼古之治所以卓乎不
可及者非以是歟三代而下用人不以其德戰
國以縱橫秦以刑名而漢以詐力嗚呼德則蔑
如矣而安望其治之古也夫
昔周公師保萬民民懷其德往愼乃司兹
率厥常懋昭周公之訓惟民其乂
洪朝璋
===
同考試官敎諭黃批作此題者非塵俗可厭
則散漫不整是篇淸新簡健有醞藉之意錄之
考試官敎諭蕭批發揮懷德處可觀且得
周家仁厚立國之意
考試官敎授潘批格峻語莊是周書文字
賢王言聖臣所以得民因望大臣以法古之化
也蓋周公以德得民治之準也君陳法之以為
治而民焉有弗化哉此成王所以命君陳者此
意以治莫難於化民政莫善於師古我之命爾
punctuated:
也。皐陶言知人，必曰九德，而夏之籲俊，亦曰迪知忱恂于九德之行。至于成湯之克卽、文武之克知灼見，凡以德而已。彼古之治所以卓乎不可及者，非以是歟？三代而下，用人不以其德：戰國以縱橫，秦以刑名，而漢以詐力。嗚呼！德則蔑如矣，而安望其治之古也夫！
「昔周公師保萬民，民懷其德。往愼乃司，兹率厥常，懋昭周公之訓，惟民其乂。」
洪朝璋
同考試官敎諭黃批：「作此題者，非塵俗可厭，則散漫不整。是篇淸新簡健，有醞藉之意，錄之。」
考試官敎諭蕭批：「發揮懷德處可觀，且得周家仁厚立國之意。」
考試官敎授潘批：「格峻語莊，是周書文字。」
賢王言聖臣所以得民，因望大臣以法古之化也。蓋周公以德得民，治之準也；君陳法之以為治，而民焉有弗化哉？此成王所以命君陳者，此意以治莫難於化民，政莫善於師古。我之命爾
translation_en:
… was so. When Gao Yao spoke of understanding men, he invariably spoke of the nine virtues. When the Xia summoned outstanding men, they likewise spoke of truly recognizing those who sincerely and steadfastly practiced the nine virtues. As for Cheng Tang’s ability to draw close to worthy men, and Kings Wen and Wu’s ability to understand them and discern them clearly, all rested on virtue alone. Was this not why the governance of antiquity stood so lofty and beyond reach? After the Three Dynasties, men were employed without regard to their virtue: the Warring States relied on diplomatic maneuvering, the Qin on penal and administrative techniques, and the Han on deceit and force. Alas! Virtue was treated as nothing. How could one expect their governance to equal that of antiquity?
“Formerly, the Duke of Zhou instructed and protected the myriad people, and the people cherished his virtue. Go and attend carefully to your office; follow his constant principles and strive to make the Duke of Zhou’s teachings manifest. Then the people will be well governed.”
Hong Chaozhang
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Those who write on this topic are either tiresomely commonplace or rambling and disorganized. This essay is fresh, concise, and vigorous, with a sense of restrained depth. I have selected it for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “The elaboration of the people’s cherishing his virtue deserves attention. It also captures the idea that the house of Zhou founded its state upon benevolence and generosity.”
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “Its structure is elevated and its language solemn: this is writing in the manner of the Documents of Zhou.”
The worthy king spoke of how a sagely minister won the people’s hearts, thereby expressing his hope that a great minister would emulate the transforming influence of antiquity. The Duke of Zhou won the people through virtue: this was the standard for governance. If Jun Chen modeled his governance upon him, how could any of the people fail to be transformed? This was why King Cheng gave his charge to Jun Chen. Its meaning was this [?]: in governing, nothing is harder than transforming the people, and in administration, nothing is better than taking antiquity as one’s teacher. My charge to you …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
治殷也亦曰以周公爲法而已矣昔周公慮萬
民之弗率也以身師之而所以敎之者無不至
慮萬民之弗寧也以身保之而所以養之者無
不周夫其敎之至也故其澤不衰而民猶思之
殆有根心而不可解者矣夫其養之周也故其
仁不匱而民猶懷之信有沒世而不忍忘者矣
夫民懷周公之德如此今爾之往也其所司者
卽公師保之舊也而所守者卽公敎養之常也
爾其慎乃攸司而毋忽易之恒懼其不能稱焉
===
率由典常而勿紛更之恒懼其不能守焉亦曰
尊其所聞善繼公之志而使若彝之訓益以昭
著於當時行其所知善述公之事而使撫事之
訓益以顯明於今日夫然則立之經制者皆殷
民服習之常而推之無不準矣奚有駭而不信
者耶陳之藝極者皆殷民聞見之舊而動之無
不化矣奚有悖而不從者耶是何也殷民方懷
周公之深而君陳能行其政是宜從君陳之速
也吁至是而殷民之懷可慰而周公之德愈不
punctuated: 治殷也，亦曰以周公爲法而已矣。昔周公慮萬民之弗率也，以身師之，而所以敎之者無不至；慮萬民之弗寧也，以身保之，而所以養之者無不周。夫其敎之至也，故其澤不衰，而民猶思之，殆有根心而不可解者矣。夫其養之周也，故其仁不匱，而民猶懷之，信有沒世而不忍忘者矣。夫民懷周公之德如此，今爾之往也，其所司者卽公師保之舊也，而所守者卽公敎養之常也。爾其慎乃攸司，而毋忽易之，恒懼其不能稱焉；率由典常，而勿紛更之，恒懼其不能守焉。亦曰尊其所聞，善繼公之志，而使若彝之訓益以昭著於當時；行其所知，善述公之事，而使撫事之訓益以顯明於今日。夫然則立之經制者，皆殷民服習之常，而推之無不準矣，奚有駭而不信者耶？陳之藝極者，皆殷民聞見之舊，而動之無不化矣，奚有悖而不從者耶？是何也？殷民方懷周公之深，而君陳能行其政，是宜從君陳之速也。吁！至是而殷民之懷可慰，而周公之德愈不
translation_en:
…to govern Yin is simply to take the Duke of Zhou as your model. Formerly, the Duke of Zhou feared that the myriad people would not follow the right way, so he personally served as their teacher, leaving nothing undone in instructing them. He feared that the myriad people would not live in peace, so he personally served as their protector, leaving nothing unattended in nurturing them. Because his instruction was so thorough, his beneficence has not faded, and the people still think of him: it seems to have taken root in their hearts and cannot be loosened. Because his nurture was so comprehensive, his benevolence has not been exhausted, and the people still cherish him: truly, they cannot bear to forget him to the end of their lives.

Such is the people’s attachment to the Duke of Zhou’s virtue. Now that you go there, your charge is the very one in which the Duke formerly served as teacher and protector, and what you must preserve is his established practice of instruction and nurture. Be conscientious in your charge and do not treat it lightly, always fearing that you may fail to measure up to it. Follow the established rules and enduring norms, and do not change them heedlessly, always fearing that you may fail to uphold them. This means honoring what you have heard and worthily carrying forward the Duke’s intentions, so that his teaching to follow constant principles becomes still more manifest in your time; and putting what you know into practice and worthily continuing the Duke’s work, so that his teaching concerning the conduct of affairs becomes still clearer today.

If you do this, the institutions you establish will all accord with the enduring practices to which the people of Yin are accustomed; wherever you apply them, they will provide a proper standard. How could anyone be alarmed and distrustful? The standards you set forth will all be familiar from what the people of Yin have heard and seen; whenever you move them to act, they will be transformed. How could anyone resist and refuse to follow? Why is this so? The people of Yin still cherish the Duke of Zhou deeply, and Jun Chen can carry out his governance. It is fitting, then, that they should follow Jun Chen so readily. Ah! At this point the longing of the people of Yin can be comforted, and the Duke of Zhou’s virtue will be still less subject to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
窮矣君陳其勉之哉雖然周公之德殷民懷之
繼之君陳畢公世變風移宜可無慮矣然而反
側之習或未變焉是豈周之德猶未至耶亦曰
殷先王之德未之忘焉耳嗚呼周人能使殷民
之不忘周而不能使殷民之不忘殷吾於是知
殷周之德爲極盛也已
詩
南有樛木葛藟纍之樂只君子福履綏之
南有樛木葛藟荒之樂只君子福履將
===
之南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子福履
成之
謝頣
同考試官教諭陳批傳就字卽周禮圭璧就
采三就再就之義與縈類耳非全也錄此析疑矣
同考試官教諭吳批謂逮下爲樂只詩人善
於立言者也此篇詞意渾融不露是善作者
考試官教諭蕭批明切
考試官教授潘批溫厚
punctuated:
窮矣。君陳其勉之哉！雖然，周公之德，殷民懷之；繼之君陳、畢公，世變風移，宜可無慮矣。然而反側之習或未變焉，是豈周之德猶未至耶？亦曰殷先王之德未之忘焉耳。嗚呼！周人能使殷民之不忘周，而不能使殷民之不忘殷。吾於是知殷周之德爲極盛也已。
詩
南有樛木，葛藟纍之。樂只君子，福履綏之。南有樛木，葛藟荒之。樂只君子，福履將之。南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。
謝頣
同考試官教諭陳批：「傳就字，卽《周禮》圭璧就采三就再就之義，與縈類耳，非全也。錄此析疑矣。」
同考試官教諭吳批：「謂逮下爲樂只，詩人善於立言者也。此篇詞意渾融不露，是善作者。」
考試官教諭蕭批：「明切。」
考試官教授潘批：「溫厚。」

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詩人屢興后妃以德而致福其稱願者深矣蓋
德有致福之理也而屢形之詠歌焉不益信乎
樛木詩人有感於后妃而陳之以詩蓋曰南山
之上樛木生焉不期於葛藟也而覃延不已者
纍焉以其下援也惟我君子樂易以兼容物雖
微而必愛慈和以徧覆人雖賤而可親此德也
非心乎福履也但見帝降昭焉保佑萃安貞之
慶神相極焉和寧備元吉之休福與德胥屬之
矣何隉兀乎南有樛木榦曲而柯垂矣故萋萋
===
然如有感焉以荒之者葛藟也況乎君子以和
召和者吾見福履之來也參會於後先或啓以
知也周旋乎左右或翼以行也蓋如孤特而匡
翊之不已焉樛木在南條垂而枝委矣故莫莫
然如有應焉以縈之者葛藟也況乎君子以順
感順者吾見福履之集也相纏綿焉靜則與游
也相依附焉動則與俱也蓋如判渙而卽就之
弗遑焉是何也福本乎德而福爲德之徵相須
以必然者也向非遠取諸物孰能名言之若此
punctuated:
詩人屢興后妃以德而致福，其稱願者深矣。蓋德有致福之理也，而屢形之詠歌焉，不益信乎？

樛木，詩人有感於后妃而陳之以詩。蓋曰：南山之上，樛木生焉，不期於葛藟也，而覃延不已者纍焉，以其下援也。惟我君子，樂易以兼容，物雖微而必愛；慈和以徧覆，人雖賤而可親。此德也，非心乎福履也。但見帝降昭焉，保佑萃安貞之慶；神相極焉，和寧備元吉之休。福與德胥屬之矣，何隉兀乎？南有樛木，榦曲而柯垂矣，故萋萋然如有感焉，以荒之者葛藟也。況乎君子以和召和者，吾見福履之來也，參會於後先，或啓以知也；周旋乎左右，或翼以行也。蓋如孤特而匡翊之不已焉。樛木在南，條垂而枝委矣，故莫莫然如有應焉，以縈之者葛藟也。況乎君子以順感順者，吾見福履之集也，相纏綿焉，靜則與游也；相依附焉，動則與俱也。蓋如判渙而卽就之弗遑焉。是何也？福本乎德，而福爲德之徵，相須以必然者也。向非遠取諸物，孰能名言之若此？
translation_en:
The poets repeatedly use evocative imagery to show how the queen consort brings blessings through virtue. Profound indeed are their praise and good wishes! Virtue has within it the principle of bringing blessings; when this is repeatedly expressed in song, does it not become still more convincing?

In “The Drooping Tree” (Jiumu), the poet is moved by the queen consort and expresses his feelings in verse. He says, in effect: On the southern mountain grows a drooping tree. It expects nothing of the kudzu and other creepers, yet these endlessly spreading vines entwine it, because it reaches downward to support them. Our noble lady, with cheerful ease, embraces all: however insignificant a creature, she must cherish it. With kindness and gentleness, she shelters everyone: however lowly a person, she can draw close to them. This is virtue, with no thought of seeking blessings. Yet we see the Lord on High bestowing radiant favor, his protection gathering the blessings of peaceful steadfastness; the spirits grant their utmost assistance [?], and harmony and tranquility bring the full felicity of supreme good fortune. Blessings and virtue are thus joined together. How could there be any precariousness?

In the south there is a drooping tree, its trunk bent and its boughs hanging low. Thus the luxuriant kudzu and other creepers cover it, as though stirred by gratitude. How much more must this be so for our noble lady, whose harmony calls forth harmony! I see blessings coming to her, gathering before and behind: some enlighten her with understanding; others move about on either side, lending support to her actions. It is as though she stood alone, and they supported and assisted her without cease.

The drooping tree stands in the south, its shoots hanging down and its branches bending low. Thus the dense kudzu and other creepers entwine it, as though answering its call. How much more must this be so for our noble lady, whose gentleness evokes gentleness! I see blessings gathering about her, closely entwined, keeping company with her in repose; clinging to her, accompanying her in movement. It is as though they had been scattered apart and could not hasten quickly enough to draw near to her.

Why is this? Blessings are rooted in virtue, and blessings are the evidence of virtue: their mutual dependence is inevitable. Had the poet not reached afar for analogies among things, who could have put this into words so well?

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
吁詩人之感愛誠矣哉抑錄詩至樛木四詠后
妃矣而繼以螽斯何居蓋關雎敬也葛覃勤也
絺綌儉也師氏孝也采耳共敬之純乎樛木逮
下也其孝敬之流乎是故德至樛木而盛矣螽
斯樛木之祥也徽音嗣矣文昭武穆其委澤乎
向非聖人雝雝之化不息而久曷克臻此是故
觀女德之光徵教家之極明天人之妙廣胤祚
之原莫備於樛木斯孔子錄經之旨
蓼彼蕭斯零露湑兮旣見君子我心寫兮
===
燕笑語兮是以有譽處兮
李鍾亮
同考試官教諭陳批講譽處二字詞不繁而
意足迥異衆作
同考試官教諭吳批一寫字見周王平時思
慕此篇發明躍然而無冗贅可嘉
考試官教諭蕭批莊重
考試官教授潘批典雅
王者初燕諸侯而興來朝恩禮之渥也蓋朝而
punctuated:
吁！詩人之感愛誠矣哉！抑錄詩至樛木，四詠后妃矣，而繼以螽斯，何居？蓋關雎敬也，葛覃勤也，絺綌儉也，師氏孝也。采耳，共敬之純乎？樛木，逮下也，其孝敬之流乎？是故德至樛木而盛矣。螽斯，樛木之祥也。徽音嗣矣，文昭武穆，其委澤乎？向非聖人雝雝之化不息而久，曷克臻此？是故觀女德之光，徵教家之極，明天人之妙，廣胤祚之原，莫備於樛木。斯孔子錄經之旨。
蓼彼蕭斯，零露湑兮。旣見君子，我心寫兮。燕笑語兮，是以有譽處兮。
李鍾亮
同考試官教諭陳批：講譽處二字，詞不繁而意足，迥異衆作。
同考試官教諭吳批：一寫字，見周王平時思慕。此篇發明躍然而無冗贅，可嘉。
考試官教諭蕭批：莊重。
考試官教授潘批：典雅。
王者初燕諸侯，而興來朝恩禮之渥也。蓋朝而
translation_en:
Ah! How sincere was the poet’s affection! Yet, in compiling the Odes, by “Drooping Trees” (Jiu mu), four poems have celebrated the queen consort. Why follow them with “Locusts” (Zhong si)? “Ospreys” (Guan ju) expresses reverence; “Spreading Kudzu” (Ge tan), diligence; the fine and coarse kudzu cloth, frugality; and the governess, filial devotion. Does “Cai er” [apparently “Cocklebur,” Juan er; ?] express the purity of respectful reverence? “Drooping Trees” expresses care extending to those below: is this not the outflow of filial devotion and reverence? Thus, with “Drooping Trees,” virtue reaches its fullness. “Locusts” is the auspicious fulfillment of “Drooping Trees.” Her excellent reputation is carried on; the descendants of King Wen and King Wu, arranged in the zhao and mu ancestral lines, are surely her accumulated beneficence. Had the sage’s harmonious transforming influence not continued unceasingly over time, how could this have been attained? Thus, for beholding the radiance of womanly virtue, verifying the highest achievement of instruction within the family, understanding the subtle relationship between Heaven and humanity, and broadening the source of blessings upon descendants, nothing is more comprehensive than “Drooping Trees.” This was Confucius’s purpose in compiling the Classic.
Tall grows that southernwood;
the falling dew is abundant.
Having seen the noble lord,
my heart is relieved.
We feast, laugh, and converse;
thus there are good repute and repose.
Li Zhongliang
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “In explaining the two words ‘good repute’ and ‘repose,’ the language is concise yet conveys the meaning fully. It stands far apart from the other compositions.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The single word ‘relieved’ reveals the king of Zhou’s habitual longing. This essay brings out the meaning vividly, without redundant elaboration. Commendable.”
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “Dignified.”
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “Refined and elegant.”
As the king first feasts the regional lords, he poetically evokes the abundant favor and ceremonial courtesy bestowed upon those coming to court. For, when they attend court and…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
燕錫有休美焉則恩禮渥矣非慈惠而能然乎
周王燕諸侯而道達於初燕之頃若曰我觀蕭
之生也旣蓼然而長大矣乃天之垂澤也斯湑
然以零露焉夫承藉乎上物固有然者矣况我
於君子乎惟君子而來也王章求焉庶乎晉接
之願矣斯我心之慰也夙懷寫矣豈復睽違之
恨乎然我何以爲情也蓋君子非常常而見也
凡今之周旋乎殿陛者皆我所寤寐於江湖者
也豈但已哉乃金石陳而歌咢作焉尊壺列而
===
獻酬行焉相與以繾綣也且和氣溢而色笑形
焉樂意充而詞說盡焉相與以綢繆也如是而
君子有譽處矣何也燕行乎賓主者也笑語洽
乎家人者也今也以人臣得之吾見寵光被於
一旦而萬方之觀聽以新藩宣焉昭德也屏翰
焉昭功也不爲有譽矣乎知眷結於九重而一
國之榮懷以久優游焉守貴也泮奐焉守富也
不爲有處矣乎蓋如是則君子之休美無窮而
我亦庶乎懿好之盡矣豈徒燕哉吁王之慈惠
punctuated: 燕錫有休美焉，則恩禮渥矣，非慈惠而能然乎？周王燕諸侯而道達於初燕之頃，若曰：「我觀蕭之生也，旣蓼然而長大矣，乃天之垂澤也，斯湑然以零露焉。夫承藉乎上，物固有然者矣，况我於君子乎？惟君子而來也，王章求焉，庶乎晉接之願矣。斯我心之慰也，夙懷寫矣，豈復睽違之恨乎？然我何以爲情也？蓋君子非常常而見也，凡今之周旋乎殿陛者，皆我所寤寐於江湖者也。豈但已哉？乃金石陳而歌咢作焉，尊壺列而獻酬行焉，相與以繾綣也。且和氣溢而色笑形焉，樂意充而詞說盡焉，相與以綢繆也。如是而君子有譽處矣。何也？燕行乎賓主者也，笑語洽乎家人者也。今也以人臣得之，吾見寵光被於一旦，而萬方之觀聽以新。藩宣焉，昭德也；屏翰焉，昭功也，不爲有譽矣乎？知眷結於九重，而一國之榮懷以久。優游焉，守貴也；泮奐焉，守富也，不爲有處矣乎？蓋如是則君子之休美無窮，而我亦庶乎懿好之盡矣，豈徒燕哉？」吁！王之慈惠
translation_en:
…the banquet and its gifts confer blessings and honor: thus grace and ceremony are lavish. Could this be achieved without kindness and benevolence? As the king of Zhou feasted the feudal lords, he gave expression to his feelings at the opening of the banquet, as though saying:

“When I observe the southernwood growing, already tall and flourishing, it is Heaven that bestows its bounty, with falling dew glistening upon it. Even things in nature receive support from above; how much more should this apply to my dealings with these noble men! Now that these noble men have come, the royal ordinances are sought [?], and my wish to receive them is nearly fulfilled. This comforts my heart: my long-cherished feelings find release. How could any regret at our separation remain? Yet how am I to express my feelings? For these noble men are not people I can see frequently. All who now move about the palace halls and steps are those of whom I have thought, waking and sleeping, while they were far away among the rivers and lakes. Could I leave it at that? Bells and stone chimes are set out, and singing, both accompanied and unaccompanied, begins; wine vessels are arrayed, and offerings and return offerings of wine proceed. Together we share our deep affection. Moreover, harmony overflows and appears in smiling faces; joy fills our hearts and finds full expression in words. Together we share our close attachment. Thus these noble men enjoy honor and repose.

“Why is this so? A banquet is a ceremony conducted between host and guest; laughter and conversation are the intimacies enjoyed among family members. Now they receive these things as subjects. I see imperial favor shining upon them in a single day, renewing what people everywhere see and hear. Acting as bulwarks and disseminating royal influence, they make their virtue manifest; serving as screens and supports, they make their achievements manifest. Is this not to enjoy honor? They know that the sovereign’s affection is bound to them within the ninefold palace, so that the pride and grateful attachment of their entire domains endure. At leisure and ease, they preserve their noble standing; free and untroubled, they preserve their wealth. Is this not to enjoy repose? In this way, these noble men’s blessings and honor will be inexhaustible, and I too may come close to expressing fully my generous affection. How could this be merely a banquet?”

“Ah! The king’s kindness and benevolence …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
至矣抑周之諸侯類多忠信慈惠謹侯度師保
萬民有以為譽處地者是故天子嘉樂焉不然
不幾於昵乎若令德之爽兄弟之宜是又不以
私惠為德而進人於善者蓋祝頌而儆戒之也
馭臣之體備矣於乎此上下交德業成而為泰
也與
春秋
三月公及邾儀父盟于蔑隱公元年春公
會戎于潛隱公二年冬十月齊師滅譚
譚子奔莒莊公十年春王正月丙午衛
侯燬滅邢僖公二十有五年
馮仁
同考試官敎諭雷批分別內外親疏之旨明
悉其邃於經學者乎
考試官敎諭蕭批組織傳意成文得旨
考試官敎授潘批得謹嚴體不類眾作
春秋有因信好而異詞以明王道者有因覆小
而異詞以示王法者夫夷夏各安其所王者所
punctuated:
至矣！抑周之諸侯，類多忠信慈惠，謹侯度，師保萬民，有以為譽處地者。是故天子嘉樂焉，不然，不幾於昵乎？若令德之爽、兄弟之宜，是又不以私惠為德，而進人於善者，蓋祝頌而儆戒之也。馭臣之體備矣！於乎！此上下交，德業成，而為泰也與！

春秋

「三月，公及邾儀父盟于蔑。」隱公元年。「春，公會戎于潛。」隱公二年。「冬十月，齊師滅譚，譚子奔莒。」莊公十年。「春王正月丙午，衛侯燬滅邢。」僖公二十有五年。

馮仁

同考試官敎諭雷批：分別內外親疏之旨明悉，其邃於經學者乎！

考試官敎諭蕭批：組織傳意，成文得旨。

考試官敎授潘批：得謹嚴體，不類眾作。

春秋有因信好而異詞以明王道者，有因覆小而異詞以示王法者。夫夷夏各安其所，王者所
translation_en:
…has reached its utmost! Moreover, the regional lords of Zhou were generally loyal, trustworthy, kindly, and generous. They carefully observed the standards proper to their rank and served as teachers and protectors of the myriad people, thus providing grounds for enjoying honor and security. For this reason the Son of Heaven commended and delighted in them. Otherwise, would this not verge on favoritism? As for the words concerning the brightness of excellent virtue [?] and the proper affection between brothers, these, too, show that he did not regard personal favors as virtue, but encouraged others toward goodness: he offered admonition through blessings and praise. The principles of governing ministers were thus complete! Ah! Was this not the harmonious union of superiors and inferiors, through which virtuous achievements were accomplished and peace prevailed?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In the third month, the duke and Yifu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie.” First year of Duke Yin.
“In spring, the duke met the Rong at Qian.” Second year of Duke Yin.
“In winter, in the tenth month, the army of Qi destroyed Tan; the Viscount of Tan fled to Ju.” Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.
“In spring, in the first month according to the royal calendar, on the bingwu day, Hui, Marquis of Wei, destroyed Xing.” Twenty-fifth year of Duke Xi.

Feng Ren
