title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以防天下而君子篤于親則人道立矣此內外
親疎之間春秋所以致意也或曰天子與天地
參者也魯隱之盟邾于蔑會戎于潛也敦好同
也春秋於儀父書字而戎獨舉號覆載之內曷
為以夷夏分內外邪君子曰並育者王德之體
也內外之防否泰分焉先王設五服之制所以
辨族類而明王道也魯之盟邾雖法所深禁猶
曰同類戎並生于天地而實類于禽獸矧東郊
密邇攘斥是宜而奚以會為隱不能修文繩武
===
以迪猷昭烈而禮求于野比之匪人邦交聯夷
虜之陋屈體長猾夏之階大防一潰世道罔賴
苟以並育之故而同于待邾之禮則否甚而忘
泰矣春秋傾否致泰以衛世道者也是故儀父
書字而戎獨舉號蓋嚴外夷之旨以明王道之
用也或曰聖人與天地合德者也齊桓之滅譚
衛文之滅邢也覆國同也春秋於齊不名而衛
燬獨名仁愛之中曷為以親疎為差等邪君子
曰一本者生物之理也親疎之秩仁義分焉先
punctuated: 以防天下，而君子篤于親，則人道立矣。此內外親疎之間，《春秋》所以致意也。或曰：「天子與天地參者也。魯隱之盟邾于蔑、會戎于潛也，敦好同也。《春秋》於儀父書字，而戎獨舉號，覆載之內，曷為以夷夏分內外邪？」君子曰：「並育者，王德之體也；內外之防，否泰分焉。先王設五服之制，所以辨族類而明王道也。魯之盟邾，雖法所深禁，猶曰同類。戎並生于天地，而實類于禽獸，矧東郊密邇，攘斥是宜，而奚以會為？隱不能修文繩武，以迪猷昭烈，而禮求于野，比之匪人，邦交聯夷虜之陋，屈體長猾夏之階。大防一潰，世道罔賴。苟以並育之故，而同于待邾之禮，則否甚而忘泰矣。《春秋》傾否致泰，以衛世道者也。是故儀父書字，而戎獨舉號，蓋嚴外夷之旨，以明王道之用也。」或曰：「聖人與天地合德者也。齊桓之滅譚、衛文之滅邢也，覆國同也。《春秋》於齊不名，而衛燬獨名，仁愛之中，曷為以親疎為差等邪？」君子曰：「一本者，生物之理也；親疎之秩，仁義分焉。先
translation_en:
…thereby safeguarding all under Heaven; and when the noble man is devoted to his kin, the human moral order is established. These distinctions between inner and outer, close kin and distant relations, are therefore matters to which the Spring and Autumn Annals gives particular attention.
Someone asks: “The Son of Heaven stands alongside Heaven and Earth as their equal. Duke Yin of Lu’s covenant with Zhu at Mie and his meeting with the Rong at Qian were alike in fostering friendly relations. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals records Yifu by his courtesy name, while referring to the Rong only by their collective designation. Within the world sheltered by Heaven and borne by Earth, why distinguish inner from outer on the basis of the Yi and the Xia?”
The noble man replies: “Nurturing all together is the substance of kingly virtue; yet the boundary between inner and outer determines the distinction between obstruction and peace. The former kings established the system of five zones of submission to distinguish peoples and make manifest the kingly Way. Although Lu’s covenant with Zhu was strictly forbidden by the rules, Zhu could still be called a people of the same kind. The Rong are likewise born between Heaven and Earth, but in truth resemble birds and beasts. Moreover, they were very close to the eastern outskirts: they ought to have been repelled and driven away. What purpose, then, could a meeting with them serve? Duke Yin could not cultivate civil virtue and carry on martial achievement, thereby following the designs of his predecessors and displaying their glorious accomplishments. Instead, he sought ritual propriety in the wilderness and allied himself with unworthy men. In diplomatic relations he embraced the baseness of the alien tribes; by lowering himself, he opened the way for incursions against the Xia. Once this great boundary collapsed, the moral order of the age had nothing on which to depend. If, on the grounds that all are nurtured together, one accorded the Rong the same ritual treatment as Zhu, one would aggravate obstruction and forget peace. The Spring and Autumn Annals overturns obstruction and brings about peace, thereby defending the moral order of the age. Thus it records Yifu by his courtesy name but refers to the Rong only by their collective designation. Its purpose is to insist strictly on treating the Yi as outsiders, thereby making clear the operation of the kingly Way.”
Someone asks: “The sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth. Duke Huan of Qi’s destruction of Tan and Duke Wen of Wei’s destruction of Xing were alike in overthrowing states. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals does not give the personal name of the ruler of Qi, while it specifically names Hui of Wei. Within benevolent love, why establish different degrees according to closeness or distance of kinship?”
The noble man replies: “Having a single root is the principle by which living things are generated; the ordering of close and distant kin defines the distinctions of benevolence and righteousness. The former…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王制五服之節所以辨世類而示王法也齊之
滅譚雖法所必誅猶曰異姓邢非周公之胤邪
衞非文之昭邪矧菟圃連兵干戈宜省而何以
滅之燬不能反躬修睦以敦本蕃周而恣其悖
心遷怒已甚禮至仕而禍機成國子戮而宗姓
滅天理旣絕人道遂隳苟以一本之故而同于
滅譚之罰則兼愛而失義矣春秋由仁義行以
立人道者也是故於齊不名而衞燬獨名蓋重
覆親之罪以示王法之正也是則明王道之用
===
則夷夏安而王德之體亦全矣知王法之正則
親疎序而仁愛之施亦博矣體用兼該仁義不
悖此春秋所以爲天子之事乎雖然隱公之立
實攝焉故于邾于宋于戎而求好會盟未已吾
固不敢以膺懲之義望之也及觀木瓜之賦衞
文感桓公忘亡之賜而從宋襄之伐忍于背桓
何有于邢邪報者天下之利也略于報德而刻
於報怨其何以勸秉心塞淵易乎初矣是故治
外者先治內而君子之宅心也于其厚無于其
punctuated: 王制五服之節，所以辨世類而示王法也。齊之滅譚，雖法所必誅，猶曰異姓；邢非周公之胤邪？衞非文之昭邪？矧菟圃連兵，干戈宜省，而何以滅之？燬不能反躬修睦，以敦本蕃周，而恣其悖心，遷怒已甚。禮至仕而禍機成，國子戮而宗姓滅，天理旣絕，人道遂隳。苟以一本之故，而同于滅譚之罰，則兼愛而失義矣。《春秋》由仁義行以立人道者也。是故於齊不名，而衞燬獨名，蓋重覆親之罪，以示王法之正也。是則明王道之用，則夷夏安，而王德之體亦全矣；知王法之正，則親疎序，而仁愛之施亦博矣。體用兼該，仁義不悖，此《春秋》所以爲天子之事乎！雖然，隱公之立，實攝焉，故于邾、于宋、于戎，而求好會盟未已，吾固不敢以膺懲之義望之也。及觀《木瓜》之賦，衞文感桓公忘亡之賜，而從宋襄之伐，忍于背桓，何有于邢邪？報者，天下之利也。略于報德，而刻於報怨，其何以勸？秉心塞淵，易乎初矣。是故治外者先治內，而君子之宅心也，于其厚，無于其
translation_en:
…kings established the gradations of the five mourning obligations to distinguish degrees of kinship and make manifest royal law. Although Qi’s destruction of Tan certainly merited punishment under that law, Tan could still be described as a state of a different surname. But was Xing not descended from the Duke of Zhou? Was Wei not of King Wen’s zhao lineage? Moreover, after the fighting at Tupu, warfare should have been curtailed: why, then, destroy Xing? Hui failed to examine himself and cultivate harmony, strengthening the ancestral foundation and defending Zhou. Instead, he indulged his perverse impulses and went much too far in venting his anger upon others. When Li Zhi entered office, the mechanism of disaster was set in place; when Guozi was slain, the state of the kindred surname was destroyed. Once Heaven’s principles were severed, the human moral order collapsed. If, on the grounds that all share a single origin, one imposed the same punishment as for the destruction of Tan, this would be indiscriminate love at the expense of righteousness. The Spring and Autumn Annals proceeds through benevolence and righteousness to establish the human moral order. Thus it does not record the personal name of Qi’s ruler, but singles out Hui of Wei by name, emphasizing the gravity of destroying one’s kin and demonstrating the correctness of royal law.

Thus, when the operation of the kingly Way is understood, the Yi and the Xia are secure, and the substance of royal virtue is also complete. When the correctness of royal law is understood, nearer and more distant kin take their proper places, and benevolent love also extends widely. Encompassing both substance and operation, with benevolence and righteousness in harmony—is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals constitutes the business of the Son of Heaven? Nevertheless, Duke Yin’s accession was in fact a regency. Hence he continually sought friendly relations, meetings, and covenants with Zhu, Song, and the Rong. I certainly would not presume to expect him to fulfill the duty of punitive chastisement.

Yet consider the poem “Quince”: Duke Wen of Wei was grateful for Duke Huan’s beneficence, which allowed him to forget his state’s destruction [?]. Nevertheless, he joined Duke Xiang of Song’s campaign. If he could bear to betray Duke Huan, what scruples would he have about Xing? Reciprocity benefits all under Heaven. If one is careless in repaying kindness but exacting in repaying resentment, how can one encourage goodness? His heart, once “sincere and profound,” had changed from what it was at first. Thus those who would put external affairs in order must first put their own house in order; and the gentleman, in setting his heart, inclines toward generosity, never toward its…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
薄
夏公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕
何鴻
同考試官教諭雷批惇禮明信聖人化強之
績此作模寫明切宜錄以式
考試官教諭蕭批詞嚴義正可法
考試官教授潘批發明傳意殆盡錄之
聖人相君出會而化可見矣夫至誠能化亦人
心同然之理而勢有弗與焉者夾谷之會孔子
===
所以化齊也茲會也孔子相定公晏子相景公
再侵之怨雖平而齊之君臣未嘗一日不欲得
志於魯也犁彌劫魯之謀既有以動景公輕逞
之心而左右司馬之勢未足以當萊人鼓譟之
釁魯于是乎危矣然天下安危之幾有弗與于
勢者聖人以理為勇而不恃力以為武有見於
理之順逆而無見於勢之強弱是故歷階而升
動容中禮孚號有眾不怒而威以謀夏亂華干
盟偪好者為不祥為愆義為失禮而夷夏之防
punctuated:
薄。
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。〔定公十年〕
何鴻
同考試官教諭雷批：「惇禮明信，聖人化強之績，此作模寫明切，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭蕭批：「詞嚴義正，可法。」
考試官教授潘批：「發明傳意殆盡，錄之。」
聖人相君出會，而化可見矣。夫至誠能化，亦人心同然之理，而勢有弗與焉者。夾谷之會，孔子所以化齊也。茲會也，孔子相定公，晏子相景公。再侵之怨雖平，而齊之君臣未嘗一日不欲得志於魯也。犁彌劫魯之謀，既有以動景公輕逞之心，而左右司馬之勢，未足以當萊人鼓譟之釁，魯于是乎危矣。然天下安危之幾，有弗與于勢者。聖人以理為勇，而不恃力以為武；有見於理之順逆，而無見於勢之強弱。是故歷階而升，動容中禮，孚號有眾，不怒而威。以謀夏亂華、干盟偪好者為不祥，為愆義，為失禮，而夷夏之防
translation_en:
…meanness.

“In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu.” 〔The tenth year of Duke Ding〕

He Hong

Comment by Associate Examiner Lei, Instructor: “Upholding ritual and making good faith manifest: these were the sage’s achievements in transforming the powerful. This composition depicts them clearly and precisely. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “Its language is rigorous and its meaning correct; it merits emulation.”

Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “It elucidates almost fully the meaning of the commentary. Record it.”

The sage assisted his lord at a meeting abroad, and his transforming influence could be seen. Perfect sincerity can transform others: this is a principle common to all human hearts. Yet circumstances of power may offer it no support. The meeting at Jiagu was the means by which Kongzi transformed Qi. At this meeting, Kongzi assisted Duke Ding, and Yanzi assisted Duke Jing. Although the resentment arising from the two invasions had been settled, not a day passed when the ruler and ministers of Qi did not wish to impose their will upon Lu. Li Mi’s plan to coerce Lu had already stirred Duke Jing’s rash and self-indulgent impulses, while the strength of the Marshals of the Left and Right was insufficient to counter the threatening uproar of the men of Lai. Lu was thus in danger.

Yet the crucial turning points between security and peril in the world do not always depend on superior power. The sage drew his courage from principle and did not rely on force for martial strength. He considered whether conduct accorded with or violated principle, without regard to relative strength or weakness. Thus he ascended the steps, his every movement conforming to ritual; he called out sincerely before the assembled multitude and commanded awe without anger. He declared that plotting against the Xia and bringing disorder upon the Hua, violating a covenant and coercing friendly relations, were inauspicious, transgressed righteousness, and offended against ritual. And the boundary between the Yi and the Xia…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嚴神人之訓明矣獨立不懼諭之于道以齊之
心奪齊之氣也合好以盟罷享而退以古之禮
律今之人也彼齊則亦有同然者故其君愧悟
而責臣以古人之道其臣逢善而道君以謝過
之實離心離德者相好而不相猶干戈俶擾之
際遂成揖讓之風以力以詐者革面而且革心
一言折衝之間爰收俄頃之化人見齊之暴也
而不知理之在人可以感而通齊自是失其衆
失其强矣人見魯之危也而不知人心之理可
===
以順而服魯自是不有齊之衆齊之强矣聖人
固未甞曰吾恃此理以遏萊兵屈齊之勢而寢
其謀顧其盛德之至有以感其同然之心而直
詞正理又有以奪其横暴之氣至誠則動動則
變變則化齊固不能自已其順德之忱而魯亦
不知其所以感孚之速矣非聖人而能若是乎
是故可以觀聖人之神化矣可以觀人心同然
之理矣嗟夫文武一怒而安天下孔子一怒而
革齊皆天下之大勇也自古可恃者理不可恃
punctuated: 嚴，神人之訓明矣。獨立不懼，諭之于道，以齊之心奪齊之氣也。合好以盟，罷享而退，以古之禮律今之人也。彼齊則亦有同然者，故其君愧悟而責臣以古人之道，其臣逢善而道君以謝過之實。離心離德者，相好而不相猶；干戈俶擾之際，遂成揖讓之風。以力以詐者，革面而且革心；一言折衝之間，爰收俄頃之化。人見齊之暴也，而不知理之在人可以感而通，齊自是失其衆、失其强矣。人見魯之危也，而不知人心之理可以順而服，魯自是不有齊之衆、齊之强矣？聖人固未甞曰：「吾恃此理以遏萊兵，屈齊之勢而寢其謀。」顧其盛德之至，有以感其同然之心，而直詞正理，又有以奪其横暴之氣。至誠則動，動則變，變則化。齊固不能自已其順德之忱，而魯亦不知其所以感孚之速矣。非聖人而能若是乎？是故可以觀聖人之神化矣，可以觀人心同然之理矣。嗟夫！文武一怒而安天下，孔子一怒而革齊，皆天下之大勇也。自古可恃者理，不可恃
translation_en:
…was made strict, and the admonitions governing spirits and men were made clear. Standing alone without fear, he instructed them in the Way, using the hearts of the people of Qi to break Qi’s aggressive spirit. He cemented friendly relations through a covenant, declined the banquet, and withdrew, thus judging the men of his own day by the ritual standards of antiquity. The people of Qi, too, shared this common moral understanding. Thus their ruler, awakened to shame, called his ministers to account by the Way of the ancients; his ministers encouraged his goodness and guided him toward concrete acts of apology. Those formerly divided in heart and purpose became friendly and ceased to scheme against one another. Amid the turmoil of arms, a spirit of deference and courtesy emerged. Those who relied on force and deceit changed not only their outward conduct but also their hearts. A single utterance repelled aggression and brought about transformation in an instant.

People saw Qi’s violence but did not understand that the moral principle present in human beings could be stirred and brought into accord. From that point, Qi lost its multitude and its strength. People saw Lu’s peril but did not understand that the moral principle in human hearts could be followed to win their submission. Did not Lu thereby come to possess Qi’s multitude and Qi’s strength? The sage certainly never said, “I shall rely on this principle to check the troops of Lai, subdue Qi’s power, and thwart its designs.” Rather, the perfection of his abundant virtue moved the moral understanding they shared, while his forthright words and correct principles broke their overbearing spirit. Perfect sincerity moves others; being moved leads to change; change leads to transformation. Qi could not restrain its sincere impulse to submit to virtue, while even Lu did not understand how he had so swiftly moved others and won their trust. Could anyone but a sage have achieved this?

Here, therefore, one may behold the sage’s wondrous power to transform, and the moral principle common to all human hearts. Alas! Kings Wen and Wu, once aroused to anger, brought peace to all under Heaven; Confucius, once aroused to anger, reformed Qi. These were all instances of the greatest courage under Heaven. Since antiquity, what can be relied upon is moral principle; what cannot be relied upon…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者勢維時犁兵鼓譟雖敬仲子犯輦而出亦窮
已不大聲以色而順之帝則齊且章章歸我侵
疆王道大哉景公君臣謂鄰國有聖人而恣度
詆議乃以女樂沮魯君之用夫子不能專且久
雖有桓子遺言之悔竟亦無及使天下未見聖
人之大順大化與天地同流於萬世功德敎化
亦無窮矣
禮記
善敎者使人繼其志
羅鴻
考試官敎諭蕭批繼志處最難說此篇發
揮詳盡當是作手錄之
考試官敎授潘批詞意純雅亦善學而得
其志者乎
善爲師者必使人有默契之妙焉夫授受之道
以契爲神也然非爲師者之善敎焉則何以致
是哉且夫學之有師所以傳道授業也師之有
敎所以長善救失也然瀆之以言則感之也已
punctuated:
者勢。維時犁兵鼓譟，雖敬仲、子犯輦而出，亦窮已。不大聲以色，而順之帝則，齊且章章歸我侵疆。王道大哉！景公君臣謂鄰國有聖人，而恣度詆議，乃以女樂沮魯君之用夫子，不能專且久。雖有桓子遺言之悔，竟亦無及。使天下未見聖人之大順大化，與天地同流於萬世，功德敎化亦無窮矣。

禮記
善敎者使人繼其志
羅鴻

考試官敎諭蕭批：「繼志處最難說，此篇發揮詳盡，當是作手，錄之。」

考試官敎授潘批：「詞意純雅，亦善學而得其志者乎！」

善爲師者，必使人有默契之妙焉。夫授受之道，以契爲神也。然非爲師者之善敎焉，則何以致是哉？且夫學之有師，所以傳道授業也；師之有敎，所以長善救失也。然瀆之以言，則感之也已
translation_en:
… is force. At that moment, when the troops of Li [?] beat their drums and raised a clamour, even Jing Zhong and Zi Fan, had they ridden forth in their chariots, would have exhausted their resources. Yet, without raising his voice or assuming a stern expression, and following the standards of the Lord on High, Confucius brought Qi openly to restore our occupied territory. How great is the Kingly Way! Duke Jing and his ministers acknowledged that the neighbouring state had a sage, yet indulged in conjecture and disparagement. They then used female musicians to obstruct the ruler of Lu’s employment of the Master, so that it could be neither wholehearted nor lasting. Although Huanzi expressed regret in his dying words, it was ultimately too late. Thus the world never witnessed the sage’s supreme harmony and transforming influence flowing together with Heaven and Earth through ten thousand generations; his achievements, virtue, and moral instruction would likewise have been inexhaustible [?].

Book of Rites
“Those skilled in teaching enable others to carry on their purpose.”
Luo Hong

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “The point about carrying on the teacher’s purpose is the hardest to explain. This essay develops it thoroughly and exhaustively. Its author must be an accomplished writer. Include it.”

Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “Its language and ideas are pure and elegant. Is its author also one who learns well and grasps his teacher’s purpose?”

One skilled in being a teacher must enable others to attain the subtle wonder of tacit understanding. In the transmission and reception of learning, it is this accord that gives the process its spiritual efficacy. Yet without a teacher skilled in instruction, how could this be achieved? Learners have teachers so that the Way may be transmitted and their studies imparted; teachers provide instruction so that good qualities may be fostered and failings remedied. Yet if one overwhelms learners with words, the impression made upon them is already …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
淺庸之以力則治之也過詳善敎者知循序而
進固下學之事而啓之以妙悟則在吾有以握
其機知隨問而答固設科之常而因之以微言
則在彼得以極其趣進而顧其安使而由其誠
惓惓焉以成物爲巳任也施之也無悖求之也
無拂循循然以誘人爲巳事也故能使爲弟子
者承夫詔迪之餘而意義之深長能繹思而自
得黜夫口耳之贅而精神之體會直脗合而不
殊吾雖引而不發而躍如之妙巳迎則觸處而
===
洞達應感以心足以得助我之益也吾惟時之
以化而沛然之機巳達則應速而無疑相授以
道足以爲得人之慶也不然則爲弟子者得吾
之言而不得吾之意格焉而莫之通矣猶歌者
之敎人盡吾之辭而不盡吾之變倡焉而莫之
和矣曾是以爲善敎者乎吁敎立則善類益衆
志繼則吾道不孤不責吾之不善敎而責學者
之不善學亦不足以爲人師矣抑古之善敎者
莫踰於孔子孔子之徒三千進而請問莫不退
punctuated: 淺，庸之以力，則治之也過詳。善敎者知循序而進，固下學之事，而啓之以妙悟，則在吾有以握其機；知隨問而答，固設科之常，而因之以微言，則在彼得以極其趣。進而顧其安，使而由其誠，惓惓焉以成物爲巳任也；施之也無悖，求之也無拂，循循然以誘人爲巳事也。故能使爲弟子者承夫詔迪之餘，而意義之深長，能繹思而自得；黜夫口耳之贅，而精神之體會，直脗合而不殊。吾雖引而不發，而躍如之妙巳迎，則觸處而洞達，應感以心，足以得助我之益也。吾惟時之以化，而沛然之機巳達，則應速而無疑，相授以道，足以爲得人之慶也。不然，則爲弟子者得吾之言，而不得吾之意，格焉而莫之通矣。猶歌者之敎人，盡吾之辭，而不盡吾之變，倡焉而莫之和矣。曾是以爲善敎者乎？吁！敎立則善類益衆，志繼則吾道不孤。不責吾之不善敎，而責學者之不善學，亦不足以爲人師矣。抑古之善敎者，莫踰於孔子。孔子之徒三千，進而請問，莫不退
translation_en:
…shallow; if one presses them through force [?], one directs them in excessive detail. A good teacher knows that advancing in due sequence is indeed the business of elementary learning, but awakening students to subtle understanding depends on the teacher’s grasping the opportune moment. He knows that answering questions as they arise is indeed a regular part of establishing a course of instruction, but using the occasion to offer subtle words depends on the students’ being able to fathom their full import. He advances them while considering whether they are at ease, and sets them tasks in accordance with their sincerity, earnestly taking the fulfillment of others as his own responsibility. What he imparts does not run counter to them, and what he asks does not thwart them; patiently and methodically, he makes guiding others his own work.

Thus, after receiving his instruction and guidance, his disciples can ponder the depth and far-reaching significance of its meaning and attain understanding for themselves. Discarding the superfluities of merely hearing and repeating words, they achieve a spiritual comprehension that accords directly with his own, without divergence. Though I draw the bow without releasing the arrow, they already apprehend the subtle meaning poised to emerge. They then penetrate whatever they encounter, responding inwardly with their hearts, and can thereby bring me the benefit of furthering my own understanding. I simply transform them through timely instruction, and the impulse that flows abundantly has already reached them. They then respond swiftly and without doubt; as the Way is transmitted between us, there is ample cause to rejoice in having found worthy recipients.

Otherwise, disciples acquire my words but fail to grasp my meaning: obstructed, they cannot achieve understanding. It is like a singer teaching others: they master all my lyrics but not all my variations; when I lead, none can join in harmony. Could this be considered good teaching? Ah! When teaching is established, the ranks of the good grow ever more numerous; when its purpose is carried on, our Way is not left solitary. If one blames students for failing to learn well without blaming oneself for failing to teach well, one is unfit to be a teacher.

Now, among the good teachers of antiquity, none surpassed Kongzi. Kongzi had three thousand disciples; whenever they came forward to ask questions, none withdrew…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而有所得也速肖之徒皆繼志之具而顏子之
四勿曾子之一貫則繼志之大者非聖人而能
若是乎雖然學者亦不可以不自力也是故使
人繼志者謂之善教能繼師之志者謂之善學
禮義立則貴賤等矣樂文同則上下和矣
好惡著則賢不肖別矣刑禁暴爵舉賢
則政均矣
張子翼
考試官教諭蕭批禮之義樂之文類皆忽
===
之條暢明悉毋踰此篇
考試官教授潘批講好惡刑爵為禮樂之
輔渾融有味
論治人之道禮樂相資刑政為輔也夫禮樂有
偏勝之弊則救弊之術不可緩也然術豈多乎
哉亦不過禮樂刑政之具而已樂記言此以為
道本無弊而用之者弊之聖人固不得不為之
所也是故人情之所以流與離以禮樂之偏勝
也樂勝而流者資禮以飾其貌而中正以為質
punctuated:
而有所得也。速肖之徒，皆繼志之具；而顏子之四勿、曾子之一貫，則繼志之大者。非聖人而能若是乎？雖然，學者亦不可以不自力也。是故，使人繼志者謂之善教，能繼師之志者謂之善學。

禮義立則貴賤等矣，樂文同則上下和矣，好惡著則賢不肖別矣，刑禁暴、爵舉賢則政均矣。

張子翼

考試官教諭蕭批：「禮之義、樂之文，類皆忽之。條暢明悉，毋踰此篇。」

考試官教授潘批：「講好惡、刑爵為禮樂之輔，渾融有味。」

論治人之道，禮樂相資，刑政為輔也。夫禮樂有偏勝之弊，則救弊之術不可緩也。然術豈多乎哉？亦不過禮樂刑政之具而已。《樂記》言此，以為道本無弊，而用之者弊之，聖人固不得不為之所也。是故，人情之所以流與離，以禮樂之偏勝也。樂勝而流者，資禮以飾其貌，而中正以為質，
translation_en:
…and gained something. The disciples described as su xiao 速肖 [?] were all capable of carrying on his aspirations; Yan Zi’s Four Prohibitions and Zeng Zi’s single unifying thread were the greatest instances of doing so. Could anyone other than a sage achieve this? Even so, learners must also exert themselves. Thus, one who enables others to carry on his aspirations is called a good teacher; one who can carry on his teacher’s aspirations is called a good learner.

“When the principles of ritual are established, the noble and the lowly occupy their proper ranks; when the patterns of music are shared, superiors and inferiors are harmonious; when likes and dislikes are made manifest, the worthy and unworthy are distinguished; when punishments restrain violence and ranks elevate the worthy, government is equitable.”

Zhang Ziyi 張子翼

Comment by Examiner Xiao 蕭, Instructor: “The principles of ritual and the patterns of music are generally overlooked. In lucid organization and thorough explanation, no essay surpasses this one.”

Comment by Examiner Pan 潘, Professor: “It explains likes and dislikes, punishments and ranks, as supports for ritual and music. Seamlessly integrated and rich in meaning.”

In discussing the way to govern people, ritual and music support each other, while punishments and administration serve as auxiliaries. When undue predominance of either ritual or music produces harmful effects, measures to remedy them cannot be delayed. Yet can these measures be many? They amount to no more than the instruments of ritual, music, punishments, and administration. The Record of Music speaks of this, holding that the Way itself has no defects: those who employ it introduce the defects. The sage therefore cannot but make provision to address them. Thus, human feelings lapse into license or estrangement because either ritual or music predominates unduly. Where the predominance of music leads to license, ritual is employed to regulate outward demeanor, with centrality and correctness as its substance…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
莊敬以為制則禮之義立矣由是禮敎達而名
分不渝治典修而官爵自序孰有紊貴賤以蕩
而無節者乎禮勝而離者資樂以合其情而審
一以定和比物以飾節則樂之文同矣由是和
敬和順而顯比之道行不僭不偪而一體之恩
著孰有暌上下以遠而不交者乎是禮資於樂
樂資於禮所以約之於中也然敎化或尼則刑
政當修矣是故禮樂之所以過不及正以刑政
之未舉也於吾禮樂之敎有能否則示之以好
===
惡能者吾好之否者吾惡之使曉然知所趨也
則賢者克知而益得以自勉不肖者莫掩而不
得以自容旌別具而勸懲之道著矣於吾禮樂
之敎有從違則用之以刑爵違者吾刑之從者
吾爵之使凜然不可越也則刑不及善人而民
咸服爵罔及惡德而民作愿賞罰明而董戒之
道得矣是政以行之刑以防之所以齊之於一
也吁先王救弊之術如此所以卒歸無弊而禮
樂之用不窮也歟大抵禮樂之說管乎人情矣
punctuated: 莊敬以為制，則禮之義立矣。由是禮敎達而名分不渝，治典修而官爵自序，孰有紊貴賤以蕩而無節者乎？禮勝而離者，資樂以合其情，而審一以定和，比物以飾節，則樂之文同矣。由是和敬和順，而顯比之道行；不僭不偪，而一體之恩著。孰有暌上下以遠而不交者乎？是禮資於樂，樂資於禮，所以約之於中也。然敎化或尼，則刑政當修矣。是故禮樂之所以過不及，正以刑政之未舉也。於吾禮樂之敎有能否，則示之以好惡：能者吾好之，否者吾惡之，使曉然知所趨也。則賢者克知而益得以自勉，不肖者莫掩而不得以自容，旌別具而勸懲之道著矣。於吾禮樂之敎有從違，則用之以刑爵：違者吾刑之，從者吾爵之，使凜然不可越也。則刑不及善人而民咸服，爵罔及惡德而民作愿，賞罰明而董戒之道得矣。是政以行之，刑以防之，所以齊之於一也。吁！先王救弊之術如此，所以卒歸無弊而禮樂之用不窮也歟！大抵禮樂之說管乎人情矣。
translation_en:
…and solemnity and reverence provide its regulation; then the proper principles of ritual are established. Thus ritual instruction takes effect and distinctions of status remain unaltered; the institutions of government are put in order, and offices and ranks naturally fall into their proper sequence. Who, then, would confuse noble and lowly through unrestrained excess? When the predominance of ritual causes estrangement, music is drawn upon to unite people’s feelings: the fundamental unity of sound is examined to establish harmony, and objects are coordinated to embellish its measures [?]; then the patterned forms of music become concordant. Thus harmonious reverence and harmonious obedience prevail, and the way of manifest mutual attachment is practiced; neither overstepping nor encroaching occurs, and the benevolence that unites all as one body becomes evident. Who, then, would separate superior and subordinate, keeping them distant and without intercourse? Ritual thus draws upon music, and music upon ritual, thereby restraining both within the proper mean. Yet if moral transformation is obstructed, punishments and government must be put in order.

The reason ritual and music become excessive or deficient is precisely that punishments and government have not been brought into operation. Where people prove capable or incapable of following our instruction in ritual and music, we show them approval and disapproval: those who are capable we approve, and those who are not we disapprove, so that they clearly understand the course they should take. The worthy can then be recognized and gain further encouragement to exert themselves; the unworthy cannot conceal themselves or find a place to remain complacent. With distinctions fully marked, the way of encouragement and deterrence becomes manifest. Where people obey or defy our instruction in ritual and music, we employ punishments and ranks: those who defy it we punish, and those who obey it we ennoble, so that they stand in awe and dare not transgress. Punishments then do not reach good people, and the people all submit; ranks do not reach those of evil character, and the people become upright. Rewards and punishments are made clear, and the proper means of supervision and admonition are attained. Government thus puts this instruction into practice, and punishment guards against its violation, thereby bringing people into uniform accord.

Ah! Such were the former kings’ methods for remedying abuses. Is this not why they ultimately achieved freedom from abuses, while the efficacy of ritual and music remained inexhaustible? Broadly speaking, the teachings concerning ritual and music govern human feelings.

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
先王豈待人情之弊而後救之言此以見禮樂
交相為用之妙以著竝行不悖之實也然政刑
亦先王所不廢特不以先於禮樂耳孔子不以
政刑先德禮亦此意也讀者不可不知
第貳場
論
君子無所不用其極
謝頤
同考試官教諭陳批題本平易而含蓄貫通
===
渾成精密此作體認發揮兼得之矣高薦何忝
同考試官教諭吳批詞氣雄偉格力高古抑
揚開闔俱有法度其邃於文者乎
考試官教諭蕭批道理近易宏深正欲觀
學者用心之極子能檃括而要之以敬具見學識
考試官教授潘批大學立極千古此作發
之而末言嚮往鑿鑿皆實地錄之不獨以文云爾
君子之學所以大成者無他焉體用之一也内
外之合也顯微之無間也何也道一也言乎己
punctuated:
先王豈待人情之弊而後救之？言此以見禮樂交相為用之妙，以著竝行不悖之實也。然政刑亦先王所不廢，特不以先於禮樂耳。孔子不以政刑先德禮，亦此意也。讀者不可不知。
第貳場
論
君子無所不用其極
謝頤
同考試官教諭陳批：題本平易，而含蓄貫通、渾成精密，此作體認發揮兼得之矣。高薦何忝！
同考試官教諭吳批：詞氣雄偉，格力高古，抑揚開闔俱有法度，其邃於文者乎！
考試官教諭蕭批：道理近易宏深，正欲觀學者用心之極。子能檃括而要之以敬，具見學識。
考試官教授潘批：《大學》立極千古，此作發之，而末言嚮往，鑿鑿皆實地。錄之不獨以文云爾。
君子之學所以大成者，無他焉：體用之一也，内外之合也，顯微之無間也。何也？道一也。言乎己
translation_en:
Would the former kings have waited until human feelings became corrupted before remedying them? This is said to reveal the subtle way in which rites and music function together, and to demonstrate that they operate side by side without conflict. Yet government and punishments were also things the former kings did not discard; they merely did not give them precedence over rites and music. Confucius likewise did not place government and punishments before virtue and rites: his intent was the same. Readers must understand this.
Second Session
Discourse
“There Is Nothing in Which the Gentleman Does Not Exert Himself to the Utmost”
Xie Yi
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The topic itself is straightforward. This essay achieves both thoughtful comprehension and full exposition, combining implicit meaning and thorough coherence with seamless unity and precision. It fully deserves a high recommendation!
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Its language and spirit are magnificent; its style and force are lofty and antique. Its modulations, openings, and conclusions all follow proper rules. Surely this is someone deeply versed in composition!
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: The principles are accessible and straightforward, yet broad and profound. The very purpose is to observe how fully the student applies his mind. You have been able to draw them together and make reverent attentiveness their essential point, fully displaying your learning and understanding.
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: The Great Learning establishes the ultimate standard for all ages. This essay elucidates it, and its concluding words express an aspiration toward it; every assertion is firmly grounded in actual practice. It is selected for more than its literary qualities alone.
There is no other reason why the gentleman’s learning attains full accomplishment than this: the unity of substance and function, the joining of the inner and outer, and the absence of any divide between the manifest and the subtle. Why is this so? The Way is one. Speaking of oneself …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則曰明德而新民之體以立言乎人則曰新民
而明德之用以行其理皆至善也而通極于天
是之謂體用之一也學有內外理無內外君子
者要之明德而未始有內也理純吾內利用吾
外也要之新民而未始有外也理純吾外致養
吾內也是之謂內外之合也內外合矣而理貫
乎心則無顯無微是內也外也顯微皆不可有
間也是之謂學之大成而無所不用其極矣何
也至善也者心之極也知至善而止之學之極
===
也彼世之自私而忘情於民物者貿貿於人己
之學惟近小者之狃而安也是故明德非以新
民新民非以明德明德新民矣而弗至善之止
皆非一體用而合內外者也然使一而合也不
從事於吾心之敬又何以顯微無間也是故敬
也者聖學成始而成終者也君子之學如弗大
成也則已矣君子而大成焉又豈可以偏曲而
致也哉故曰君子無所不用其極大成之學也
今夫極之義弘矣吾無取於象焉而觀乎其理
punctuated:
則曰明德，而新民之體以立；言乎人，則曰新民，而明德之用以行。其理皆至善也，而通極于天，是之謂體用之一也。學有內外，理無內外。君子者，要之明德，而未始有內也：理純吾內，利用吾外也；要之新民，而未始有外也：理純吾外，致養吾內也。是之謂內外之合也。內外合矣，而理貫乎心，則無顯無微，是內也、外也、顯微皆不可有間也。是之謂學之大成，而無所不用其極矣。何也？至善也者，心之極也；知至善而止之，學之極也。彼世之自私而忘情於民物者，貿貿於人己之學，惟近小者之狃而安也。是故明德非以新民，新民非以明德，明德新民矣而弗至善之止，皆非一體用而合內外者也。然使一而合也，不從事於吾心之敬，又何以顯微無間也？是故敬也者，聖學成始而成終者也。君子之學如弗大成也，則已矣；君子而大成焉，又豈可以偏曲而致也哉？故曰：「君子無所不用其極。」大成之學也。

今夫極之義弘矣，吾無取於象焉，而觀乎其理。
translation_en:
…then it is called illuminating luminous virtue, whereby the substance underlying the renewal of the people is established. Speaking of others, it is called renewing the people, whereby the operation of illuminating luminous virtue is put into effect. The principle in both is the highest good, reaching all the way to Heaven. This is what is meant by the unity of substance and function. Learning has an inner and an outer dimension; principle has neither. For the gentleman, its essential aim is to illuminate luminous virtue, yet this has never been confined to the inner: principle is made pure within oneself and put to use outside oneself. Its essential aim is to renew the people, yet this has never been confined to the outer: principle is made pure outside oneself, and nourishment is brought to what is within. This is what is meant by joining the inner and the outer. Once the inner and the outer are joined and principle pervades the heart, there is no distinction between the manifest and the subtle: neither inner nor outer, manifest nor subtle, can admit any separation. This is what is meant by the great consummation of learning, leaving nothing in which one does not exert oneself to the utmost. Why is this so? The highest good is the ultimate standard of the heart; knowing the highest good and abiding in it is the ultimate attainment of learning.

Those in the world who are selfish and indifferent to the people and other beings are benighted concerning learning that embraces both others and oneself; they are habituated to, and content with, what is shallow and petty. Thus, to illuminate luminous virtue without doing so for the renewal of the people, to renew the people without doing so for the illumination of luminous virtue, or to illuminate luminous virtue and renew the people without abiding in the highest good—none of these unifies substance and function or joins the inner and the outer. Yet, to bring about this unity and conjunction, unless one applies oneself to reverent attentiveness in one's own heart, how can there be no separation between the manifest and the subtle? Reverent attentiveness, therefore, is what brings the learning of the sages to fulfillment from beginning to end. If the gentleman's learning is not to reach great consummation, then there is nothing further to say; but if the gentleman is to achieve that consummation, how could he attain it through partiality and distortion? Hence the saying: “There is nothing in which the gentleman does not exert himself to the utmost.” This is learning brought to great consummation.

Now, the meaning of “the ultimate” is vast. I do not seek it in images, but examine its principle…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
是故觀易明天極於乾矣觀簡明地極於坤矣
觀至德明人極於心矣而至德又易簡之配也
道是以爲大也夫惟大也則此學與此心會焉
此心與此理會焉明德新民而皆止至善則心
也理也立極於我矣是豈可以易易言哉蓋一
體用合內外通貫顯微而後可以語此學也且
何謂明德之極也至虛也而至靈也至寂也應
天下之至感也至無也受天下之至有也天未
始不爲人人未始不爲天也一而萬萬統而一
===
也而物也知也意也心也身也莫不由乎本然
而格之致之誠之正之脩之善有一毫弗至弗
止也是明德之極也而新民者豫乎其內矣又
何謂新民之極也至公也而至順也由之皆得
也體之各足也靡者以之起淆者以之一渙者
以之萃也至動寔天下之至靜至化寔天下之
至神而家也國也天下也莫不由乎本然而齊
之治之平之善有一毫弗至弗止也是新民之
極也而明德者利乎其外矣是何也學之體用
punctuated:
是故觀易，明天極於乾矣；觀簡，明地極於坤矣；觀至德，明人極於心矣。而至德又易簡之配也，道是以爲大也。夫惟大也，則此學與此心會焉，此心與此理會焉。明德新民而皆止至善，則心也理也，立極於我矣。是豈可以易易言哉？蓋一體用，合內外，通貫顯微，而後可以語此學也。且何謂明德之極也？至虛也，而至靈也；至寂也，應天下之至感也；至無也，受天下之至有也。天未始不爲人，人未始不爲天也。一而萬，萬統而一也。而物也、知也、意也、心也、身也，莫不由乎本然而格之、致之、誠之、正之、脩之。善有一毫弗至，弗止也。是明德之極也，而新民者豫乎其內矣。
又何謂新民之極也？至公也，而至順也；由之皆得也，體之各足也。靡者以之起，淆者以之一，渙者以之萃也。至動寔天下之至靜，至化寔天下之至神。而家也、國也、天下也，莫不由乎本然而齊之、治之、平之。善有一毫弗至，弗止也。是新民之極也，而明德者利乎其外矣。是何也？學之體用
translation_en:
Thus, by contemplating ease, we see clearly that Heaven’s ultimate standard lies in Qian; by contemplating simplicity, we see clearly that Earth’s ultimate standard lies in Kun; and by contemplating consummate virtue, we see clearly that humanity’s ultimate standard lies in the heart-mind. Consummate virtue, moreover, is the counterpart of ease and simplicity. This is why the Way is great. Precisely because it is great, this learning accords with this heart-mind, and this heart-mind accords with this principle. When manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people both come to rest in the highest good, heart-mind and principle establish the ultimate standard within oneself. How could this be spoken of lightly? Only after unifying substance and function, joining the inner and the outer, and comprehending both the manifest and the subtle can one discuss this learning. What, then, is the ultimate standard in manifesting luminous virtue? It is utterly empty yet utterly numinous; utterly still, yet responsive to all the stirrings of the world; utterly without anything, yet receptive to everything in the world. Heaven has never been separate from humanity, nor humanity from Heaven. The one becomes the myriad, and the myriad are gathered into one. Things, knowledge, intentions, the heart-mind, and the person are all addressed according to their original nature: things are investigated, knowledge extended, intentions made sincere, the heart-mind rectified, and the person cultivated. If even the slightest measure of goodness remains unattained, one does not stop. This is the ultimate standard in manifesting luminous virtue, and renewing the people is already included within it.
What, then, is the ultimate standard in renewing the people? It is utterly impartial and utterly harmonious. All who follow it attain what is proper to them, and all who embody it find sufficiency within themselves. Through it the dispirited rise, the confused become unified, and the scattered gather together. The utmost activity is truly the world’s utmost stillness; the utmost transformation is truly the world’s utmost spiritual efficacy. Family, state, and all under Heaven are all addressed according to their original nature: the family is regulated, the state governed, and all under Heaven brought to peace. If even the slightest measure of goodness remains unattained, one does not stop. This is the ultimate standard in renewing the people, while manifesting luminous virtue brings benefit outwardly [?]. Why is this so? The substance and function of learning…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
本無不一也内外本無不合也其不一不合者
人也所謂自私而忘情於民物者也而吾之學
不如是也使吾之學如是則窒乎内不能虛而
靈矣滯乎外不能公而順矣其能免於虧缺滲
漏而無累乎本然也哉嗚乎此君子必無所不
用其極也然則明德之用極也如之何曰敬以
明之也夫心者性之郛廓也而聲色臭味皆動
於性之欲而客氣又乗之於此乎弗敬也則陽
明少而陰濁勝德性昧而物欲行塞乎空洞瑩
===
徹者矣必也持之主一無適焉居之整齊嚴肅
焉懋昭以式趨焉緝熈以引緒焉宥密以宏蓄
焉不略於精微焉不蔽於廣大焉自欺自慊之
戒且求焉十目十手之視且指焉好樂忿懥憂
患恐懼之必察焉親愛賤惡畏敬哀矜傲惰之
無僻焉而孰非敬之防閑翼衞以極之也蓋倡
猷而錫極者也是以為新民地也新民之用極
也如之何曰敬以新之也夫民胞物與天責乎
我者也而理一分殊親疎賢不肖固倍蓰而千
punctuated:
本無不一也，内外本無不合也。其不一不合者，人也，所謂自私而忘情於民物者也。而吾之學不如是也。使吾之學如是，則窒乎内，不能虛而靈矣；滯乎外，不能公而順矣。其能免於虧缺滲漏，而無累乎本然也哉？嗚乎！此君子必無所不用其極也。
然則明德之用極也，如之何？曰：敬以明之也。夫心者，性之郛廓也，而聲色臭味皆動於性之欲，而客氣又乗之。於此乎弗敬也，則陽明少而陰濁勝，德性昧而物欲行，塞乎空洞瑩徹者矣。必也持之主一無適焉，居之整齊嚴肅焉，懋昭以式趨焉，緝熈以引緒焉，宥密以宏蓄焉，不略於精微焉，不蔽於廣大焉。自欺自慊之戒且求焉，十目十手之視且指焉，好樂忿懥憂患恐懼之必察焉，親愛賤惡畏敬哀矜傲惰之無僻焉。而孰非敬之防閑翼衞以極之也？蓋倡猷而錫極者也，是以為新民地也。
新民之用極也，如之何？曰：敬以新之也。夫民胞物與，天責乎我者也，而理一分殊，親疎賢不肖，固倍蓰而千
translation_en:
…are fundamentally always one, and the inner and outer fundamentally always accord. Where they fail to be one or to accord, this is due to people: those who, as the saying goes, are selfish and lose their fellow feeling for other people and things. Our learning is not like this. If our learning were like this, we would be obstructed within, unable to remain open and spiritually responsive, and impeded without, unable to remain impartial and act in accord with things. Could we then avoid deficiencies and leakages and leave our original nature unimpaired? Alas! This is why the gentleman must exert himself to the utmost in everything.
How, then, does one exert oneself to the utmost in manifesting luminous virtue? The answer is: through reverent attentiveness, one makes it shine. The mind is the outer wall of human nature. Sounds, sights, smells, and tastes all stir the desires of that nature, and adventitious vital impulses further take advantage of them. If one fails to maintain reverent attentiveness here, brightness diminishes and dark turbidity prevails; moral nature is obscured and material desires run free, blocking what was empty, open, luminous, and clear. One must hold fast to singleness of purpose without straying, and maintain orderliness, gravity, and solemnity in one's bearing. One must strive for illumination to guide one's conduct, sustain that brightness to carry forward its thread, and cultivate profound stillness to enlarge what is stored within. One must neglect nothing subtle and minute, nor be obscured in one's grasp of what is broad and great. One must heed the warning against self-deception and seek satisfaction within oneself [?]; bear in mind the scrutiny of ten eyes and the pointing of ten hands; examine one's fondness and delight, anger and resentment, anxiety and fear; and avoid partiality arising from affection, contempt and dislike, awe and respect, pity, or arrogance and indifference. Which of these is not a way in which reverent attentiveness guards and protects one, enabling one to reach the utmost? This is to set forth the Way and establish the highest standard, thereby laying the foundation for renewing the people.
How does one exert oneself to the utmost in renewing the people? The answer is: through reverent attentiveness, one renews them. To regard the people as one's siblings and all things as one's companions is the responsibility Heaven places upon us. Yet principle is one while particular allotments differ: between the closely related and the distant, the worthy and the unworthy, differences are indeed twofold, fivefold, and a thousandfold…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
萬也而弗敬焉則情所在而溺肆殊焉勢所在
而輕重判焉舍厚而敦薄焉舉近而遺遠焉而
鹵莽滅裂者作矣必也嚴恭寅畏以臨也必也
齋莊中正以觀也必也以離照以咸感以同人
而亨也不以疎間親也不以賤妨貴恩揜義也
孝弟慈以成敎也上下四旁以絜矩也好惡必
協也藏身必恕也進忠信而飭驕泰也內本外
末以經賦也彥聖媚嫉以辨官也而孰非敬之
周流運用以極之也蓋刑于而作孚者也又自
===
新之成也蓋至是不惟極之用而極且建於君
子矣然而君子未已也蓋極矣猶懼乎遷也故
必曰不及焉必曰未見焉不以德爲已明也必
曰猶病焉必曰如傷焉不以民爲已新也推而
參天地也贊化育也而其心兢兢焉業業焉果
而確焉猶一日也是故自十五而百年此學也
自一身而子孫臣庶此學也自沒世而千萬世
此學也是故自效驗而觀之明德而曰克曰峻
曰顧諟新民而曰日新曰振新所開來何如也
punctuated:
萬也。而弗敬焉，則情所在而溺肆殊焉，勢所在而輕重判焉，舍厚而敦薄焉，舉近而遺遠焉，而鹵莽滅裂者作矣。必也嚴恭寅畏以臨也，必也齋莊中正以觀也，必也以離照，以咸感，以同人而亨也。不以疎間親也，不以賤妨貴、恩揜義也。孝弟慈以成敎也，上下四旁以絜矩也，好惡必協也，藏身必恕也，進忠信而飭驕泰也，內本外末以經賦也，彥聖媚嫉以辨官也。而孰非敬之周流運用以極之也？蓋刑于而作孚者也，又自新之成也。

蓋至是，不惟極之用，而極且建於君子矣。然而君子未已也，蓋極矣，猶懼乎遷也。故必曰不及焉，必曰未見焉，不以德爲已明也；必曰猶病焉，必曰如傷焉，不以民爲已新也。推而參天地也，贊化育也，而其心兢兢焉、業業焉，果而確焉，猶一日也。是故自十五而百年，此學也；自一身而子孫臣庶，此學也；自沒世而千萬世，此學也。是故自效驗而觀之，明德而曰克、曰峻、曰顧諟，新民而曰日新、曰振新，所開來何如也？
translation_en:
…ten thousandfold. Yet without reverent attentiveness, personal affections lead to differing degrees of indulgence and license, and relations of power determine differences in the weight accorded to people. One abandons those to whom greater obligations are owed and treats generously those to whom less is owed; one attends to those nearby and neglects those far away. Thus carelessness and negligence arise. One must approach them with solemn respect and vigilant awe, and regard them with dignified composure, balance, and rectitude. One must illuminate through Li (Clinging Fire), move others through Xian (Mutual Influence), and attain free passage through Tongren (Fellowship with Others). One must not let the distant come between the close, nor let the lowly obstruct the honored or personal favor eclipse righteousness. Through filial devotion, respect for elder brothers, and parental kindness, one brings moral instruction to completion. In dealings with those above, below, and on every side, one applies the measuring square of reciprocity. One’s likes and dislikes must accord with those of the people; safeguarding oneself must rest on consideration for others. One advances loyalty and trustworthiness and curbs arrogance and extravagance. One manages revenues by treating the root as central and the branches as peripheral, and distinguishes officials according to whether they cherish or envy the worthy and wise. Which of these is not reverent attentiveness circulating everywhere and operating to bring matters to the utmost standard? This is to set an example and inspire trust; it is also the fulfillment of renewing oneself.

At this point, not only is the utmost standard put into practice: it is also established in the noble person himself. Yet the noble person does not cease his efforts. Even after reaching that standard, he still fears departing from it. Thus he must speak of not having attained it and of not yet having seen it, never considering his virtue already fully illuminated. He must speak of still finding the task difficult and of treating the people as though they were injured, never considering the people already fully renewed. Extending his efforts, he takes his place alongside Heaven and Earth and assists their transforming and nurturing work. Yet his heart remains cautious and watchful, resolute and firm, just as on the first day. Thus, from the age of fifteen to a hundred years, it is this learning; from his own person to his descendants, ministers, and common people, it is this learning; from the end of his life through a thousand and ten thousand generations, it is this learning. Therefore, considered in terms of its demonstrated effects, illuminating virtue is expressed as ‘being able,’ ‘making lofty,’ and ‘keeping constantly in view’; renewing the people is expressed as ‘daily renewal’ and ‘rousing to renewal.’ How great, then, is what this opens up for those to come!

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明德而聞武之克也聞堯之峻也聞顧諟於太
甲也新民而聞銘於殷誥若詩於周也所繼往
何如也德明而命以明則神明與居民新而天
命以新則造化與游所立心於天地何如也彪
炳以盛德威儀則為精華為馨香浸漬以親賢
樂利則為鴻恩為大化所立命於生民何如也
蓋至是一人之德之民天下萬世之德之民莫
不明且新於君子矣而君子猶用極而已耳非
有所加也故曰君子之學一體用合內外貫顯
===
微而為大成也是學也二三帝王所已試者也
孔子不得君師之位故以詔萬世使萬世知為
已試而弗疑也而曾氏子發乎其蘊是二三帝
王建一世之極者也孔子以萬世建極者也然
則學者又何以詣極也曰審幾也定志而養氣
也必愼獨而德可明也必以義為利而民可新
也亶乎其學問自脩也裕乎其定靜安慮也優
游厭飫融之以漸也勿助勿忘需之以化也而
始終以一敬則幾於極矣蓋心一也理一也學
punctuated: 明德而聞武之克也，聞堯之峻也，聞顧諟於《太甲》也；新民而聞銘於殷，誥若詩於周也，所繼往何如也？德明而命以明，則神明與居；民新而天命以新，則造化與游，所立心於天地何如也？彪炳以盛德威儀，則為精華、為馨香；浸漬以親賢樂利，則為鴻恩、為大化，所立命於生民何如也？蓋至是，一人之德之民，天下萬世之德之民，莫不明且新於君子矣。而君子猶用極而已耳，非有所加也。故曰：君子之學，一體用，合內外，貫顯微，而為大成也。是學也，二三帝王所已試者也。孔子不得君師之位，故以詔萬世，使萬世知為已試而弗疑也。而曾氏子發乎其蘊，是二三帝王建一世之極者也，孔子以萬世建極者也。然則學者又何以詣極也？曰：審幾也，定志而養氣也。必愼獨而德可明也，必以義為利而民可新也。亶乎其學問自脩也，裕乎其定靜安慮也，優游厭飫，融之以漸也；勿助勿忘，需之以化也。而始終以一敬，則幾於極矣。蓋心一也，理一也，學
translation_en:
In illuminating virtue, we hear of Wu’s “being able,” of Yao’s “making lofty,” and of “keeping constantly in view” in the Tai Jia; in renewing the people, we hear of the inscription under the Yin and of proclamations and poems under the Zhou. How great, then, is the inheritance they carried forward from the past! When virtue is illuminated and the Mandate is thereby made bright, one dwells with spiritual intelligence; when the people are renewed and Heaven’s Mandate is thereby renewed, one roams with the transforming powers of creation. How great is this establishing of a mind for Heaven and Earth! Shining forth in abundant virtue and dignified bearing, it becomes refined brilliance and fragrant offering; pervading all through affection for worthy men and delight in benefits, it becomes vast beneficence and profound transformation. How great is this establishing of a destiny for the people!

At this point, the virtue and people of one person, and the virtue and people of the whole world through ten thousand generations, are all illuminated and renewed through the gentleman. Yet the gentleman merely applies the ultimate standard; he adds nothing beyond it. Thus it is said: the gentleman’s learning unifies substance and function, joins the inner and outer, and connects the manifest and subtle, bringing them to complete fulfillment. This learning had already been put into practice by the ancient emperors and kings. Kongzi did not obtain the position of ruler and teacher, so he instructed ten thousand generations, ensuring that they would know it had already been tried and would not doubt it. Master Zeng then brought out its hidden significance. Those ancient emperors and kings established the ultimate standard for their own age; Kongzi established it for ten thousand generations.

How, then, can learners attain this ultimate standard? The answer is: by discerning the first stirrings, settling their purpose, and nourishing their vital energy. Only by being watchful over themselves when alone can they illuminate virtue; only by regarding righteousness as benefit can they renew the people. They must be sincere in study, inquiry, and self-cultivation, and ample in steadfastness, stillness, repose, and deliberation. At ease in their learning and fully steeped in it, they gradually assimilate it; neither forcing its growth nor forgetting it, they await its transforming effect. If, from beginning to end, they maintain undivided reverence, they will come close to the ultimate standard. For the mind is one, principle is one, and learning…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一也嗚乎此學之為大也
表

四六而已佳士佳士

punctuated:
一也。嗚乎，此學之為大也！

translation_en:
…is one. Ah, how great this learning is!

Memorial
A congratulatory memorial in the voices of the assembled ministers on Cao Bin’s pacification of Jiangnan under the Song [Eighth year of Kaibao, 975]
By Yan Wenfu

Comment by Associate Examiner Lü, School Instructor: Those composing memorials in the examination hall generally produce prolix, derivative works, which are exceedingly tiresome. This composition is elegant and dignified in form, with richly wrought language [?]. Without forced ornament or strained connections, it conveys profound and lasting meaning. It embeds loyalty and devotion within a memorial of praise: it is more than merely accomplished four-and-six-character parallel prose. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner Xiao, Instructor: Its facts are accurate and its language beautiful. Include it.
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: Its praise and narration are methodically arranged. It is worthy to serve as a model of four-and-six-character parallel prose.

On a certain day of the twelfth month of the eighth year of Kaibao, your servants, so-and-so and the others, submit: On the yiwei day of the eleventh month, Cao Bin, Commander-in-Chief of the Southwest Route Expeditionary Army, captured Shengzhou, and Jiangnan was pacified.
The plans of the imperial court are grand and far-reaching: You embrace the realm in unity and occupy its center. The imperial path is clear and level: Through campaigns in the four directions, the regional states have been brought to peace. Military strategy has thus borne fruit beyond the gates of the capital; dispatches announcing victory have sped to the imperial presence. Joy stirs all at court, and celebration extends equally throughout the land. Your servants, so-and-so and the others, rejoice and clap their hands, bowing low and knocking their heads upon the ground. We humbly reflect that Li Bian took over the dominion of Yang Wu and thereupon founded the Southern Tang…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
景通擅山海之饒頗窺中土自世宗蹙其
北境始畫江為自守之謀及我
朝事於南淮乃遷國效圖存之計邇當子煜
之嗣立外修臣節以稱藩奉表貢琛貶卑
彌激聚兵峻壘包蓄漸章惟
聖德無所不容爰修文告彼庸人迷而弗悟罔
效駿奔勞
赫怒以徂征用壯猶而問罪
推轂而將心自厲鑿門而士氣益增取道上
===
游共集堂堂之陣誓師橫海期成善善之
功虎旅飈飛萬騎從天而下龍船雲護千
艘不日而成駕彼靈鼉信憑虛而飛渡緩
茲餓鶻仍寬𥡴而招攜徒勤一介之來未
悉四封而至及師環於戶外始面縛於軍
前籍丁稅而入版圖拯泥塗以奠衽席未
冒蔡城之雪遄開楚國之氛幕府風清秦
淮月白茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
punctuated: 景通擅山海之饒，頗窺中土。自世宗蹙其北境，始畫江為自守之謀；及我朝事於南淮，乃遷國效圖存之計。邇當子煜之嗣立，外修臣節以稱藩，奉表貢琛，貶卑彌激；聚兵峻壘，包蓄漸章。惟聖德無所不容，爰修文告。彼庸人迷而弗悟，罔效駿奔，勞赫怒以徂征，用壯猶而問罪。推轂而將心自厲，鑿門而士氣益增。取道上游，共集堂堂之陣；誓師橫海，期成善善之功。虎旅飈飛，萬騎從天而下；龍船雲護，千艘不日而成。駕彼靈鼉，信憑虛而飛渡；緩茲餓鶻，仍寬𥡴而招攜。徒勤一介之來，未悉四封而至。及師環於戶外，始面縛於軍前。籍丁稅而入版圖，拯泥塗以奠衽席。未冒蔡城之雪，遄開楚國之氛。幕府風清，秦淮月白。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇
translation_en:
…In the Jingtong era, he monopolized the wealth of the mountains and seas and harbored ambitions toward the Central Plain. Only after Shizong pressed back his northern frontier did he make the river a boundary and devise a strategy of self-defense. When our dynasty undertook operations south of the Huai, he moved his capital in an attempt to preserve his state. More recently, when his son Yu succeeded to the throne, he outwardly observed a subject’s duties and professed himself a vassal. He submitted memorials and offered precious tribute, making ever greater displays of humility; yet he amassed troops and strengthened fortifications, gradually revealing his concealed designs.

Your sagely virtue encompasses all, and thus written admonitions were issued. But that mediocre man remained deluded and failed to awaken; he would not hasten to render service. He provoked Your thunderous wrath and compelled a punitive expedition, in which a mighty plan was employed to call him to account. As the chariot wheels were pushed forward to send off the commanders, their resolve grew keener; as a gate was breached for their departure, the soldiers’ spirit rose still higher. Advancing by the upper reaches, they assembled their imposing formations; pledging the troops to cross the sea, they sought to accomplish the work of honoring goodness.

The tiger-like host swept forward like a whirlwind, ten thousand horsemen descending as if from heaven. Clouds sheltered the dragon ships, a thousand vessels completed in scarcely any time. Riding those wondrous water dragons, they truly seemed to fly across empty space. Restraining these hungry falcons, they still allowed a respite [?] to summon those estranged from allegiance. In vain did he trouble a lone envoy to come; he did not come bringing the whole territory within his borders. Only when the army surrounded his very doors did he appear before it with his hands bound behind his back in surrender.

They registered the taxable population and revenues and incorporated the land into the imperial registers and maps, rescuing the people from misery and settling them in comfort. Without having to brave the snows of Cai’s walls, they swiftly dispelled the dark atmosphere over the land of Chu. A pure breeze filled the military headquarters; bright moonlight shone over the Qinhuai. This was surely because we humbly had the good fortune to encounter [four circles in the transcription: 〇〇〇〇]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
應圖受曆
濟世安民
寬裕溫柔蕩配天之大德
剛健中正握宰物之玄機謂
王者稱域中之至尊化靡遺於六合而
聖人以天下而爲度治可分乎一家用是廓
帝紘而恢
王綱次第削四方之僭割荷天衢而提地理指
麾息五代之紛爭首定西川孟昶貽羞於
===
寶器繼平南粵劉鋹呈技於珠鞍
軫念江南本同赤縣承塵
輦下敢效彤軒方期四海之會同豈許一江
之限隔
恩每徠其歸順義曲示乎包荒詎謂不悛果成
自掇師徒用
命陋京觀於鯨鯢川嶽效靈震
神威於草木方且憐其正朔之曾稟露布勿宣
憫彼鋒刃之橫罹
punctuated:
應圖受曆，濟世安民，寬裕溫柔，蕩配天之大德；剛健中正，握宰物之玄機。謂王者稱域中之至尊，化靡遺於六合；而聖人以天下而爲度，治可分乎一家？用是廓帝紘而恢王綱，次第削四方之僭割；荷天衢而提地理，指麾息五代之紛爭。首定西川，孟昶貽羞於寶器；繼平南粵，劉鋹呈技於珠鞍。
軫念江南，本同赤縣；承塵輦下，敢效彤軒。方期四海之會同，豈許一江之限隔？恩每徠其歸順，義曲示乎包荒。詎謂不悛，果成自掇！師徒用命，陋京觀於鯨鯢；川嶽效靈，震神威於草木。方且憐其正朔之曾稟，露布勿宣；憫彼鋒刃之橫罹，
translation_en:
… responding to the prophetic charts and receiving the imperial calendar, saving the age and bringing peace to the people. Your generosity, magnanimity, gentleness, and mildness display a vast virtue matching Heaven; your strength, vigor, balance, and rectitude grasp the mysterious workings that govern all things. You hold that the true king is supreme within the realm, his transforming influence leaving nothing untouched throughout the six directions; and that the sage takes all under Heaven as his measure—could government be partitioned among individual ruling houses? Thus you extended the imperial bonds and enlarged the kingly order, successively eliminating the usurping regimes that divided the four quarters. Upholding Heaven’s thoroughfares and grasping the patterns of the earth [?], with a gesture you ended the strife of the Five Dynasties. First you subdued Xichuan, where Meng Chang brought shame upon himself through his precious vessels; next you pacified Nanyue, where Liu Chang displayed his craftsmanship in a pearl-studded saddle.
You thought with concern of Jiangnan, which likewise belonged to the central realm. Beneath the canopy of your imperial carriage, it dared imitate the vermilion carriage of sovereignty [?]. Just when you looked forward to the union of all within the four seas, how could you allow a single river to keep them apart? Your benevolence repeatedly drew them toward submission; your righteousness showed every consideration in tolerating their uncultivated ways. Who could have imagined that they would remain unrepentant and indeed bring disaster upon themselves! Your troops obeyed your commands, yet you disdained to heap the bodies of the great rebels into a victory mound. Rivers and mountains manifested their numinous power, and your divine might struck awe even into grass and trees. Moreover, pitying them because they had once accepted your calendar and acknowledged your sovereignty, you ordered that no public proclamation of victory be issued; grieving for those who had suffered the unforeseen violence of swords and blades…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天顏為動
好生協德風行遐圻
大統書元化均殊裔設此座而待行見獻俘近
臥榻而鼾孰敢越志昔晉代奏燒炬之績
得之惟艱隋人成窺井之功掩其不備事
慙
今日語不同年臣等幸覩
鴻休欣逢
景運仰
===
靈明而作頌才謝揚雄欽
允塞而陳詩功懷召穆伏願
南歸吳越
北定漢遼桂海冰天盡尊親於夷夏金縢玉
策紀
謨烈於登閎包干戈以虎皮千載慶
文明之嘉鬯
敘彝倫於龜範萬方拱
皇極而會歸臣某等無任瞻
punctuated:
天顏為動。好生協德，風行遐圻；大統書元，化均殊裔。設此座而待，行見獻俘；近臥榻而鼾，孰敢越志？昔晉代奏燒炬之績，得之惟艱；隋人成窺井之功，掩其不備。事慙今日，語不同年。
臣等幸覩鴻休，欣逢景運。仰靈明而作頌，才謝揚雄；欽允塞而陳詩，功懷召穆。伏願南歸吳越，北定漢遼，桂海冰天，盡尊親於夷夏；金縢玉策，紀謨烈於登閎。包干戈以虎皮，千載慶文明之嘉鬯；敘彝倫於龜範，萬方拱皇極而會歸。臣某等無任瞻
translation_en:
…the imperial countenance was moved. Your love of life accords with virtue, spreading like the wind to distant frontiers; the great unified succession establishes the first year, and your transforming influence reaches even remote peoples equally. With this seat prepared in readiness, we shall soon witness the presentation of captives. Who would dare snore beside your couch and harbor ambitions beyond his station? Formerly, the Jin dynasty reported its achievement with blazing torches, but victory was won only with difficulty; the men of Sui accomplished their feat of peering into the well by catching their enemy unprepared. Those deeds pale before today’s; they cannot be spoken of in the same breath.
We, your servants, are fortunate to behold this magnificent blessing and rejoice to encounter this glorious era. Looking up to your spiritual brilliance, we compose a eulogy, though our talent falls short of Yang Xiong’s; revering your abundant sincerity, we present a poem, recalling the achievements of Duke Mu of Shao.
We humbly wish that Wu and Yue in the south may submit, and Han and Liao in the north be pacified; that throughout the southern seas and frozen northern lands, both non-Chinese and Chinese may honor and cherish you; and that metal-bound documents and jade tablets may record your plans and glorious deeds in exalted grandeur [?]. May shields and spears be wrapped in tiger skins, and a thousand years celebrate the flourishing of civil virtue. May the enduring human relationships be ordered according to the norm revealed by the tortoise, and all regions converge in allegiance around the imperial standard. We, your servants So-and-so and the others, cannot contain our feelings as we gaze…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖欣躍屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
謝頤
===
同考試官教諭陳批我
高皇帝曁我
皇上心法治功所匹休帝王垂憲
後聖皆得乎大學者子能榆揚之其涵濡有得者乎
同考試官教諭吳批條答詳盡末復以臣隣
交儆為言可以占子他日試用矣
考試官教諭關批
聖學精微不帝言語文字間也子獨觀其大者可以占嚮用矣
考試官教授潘批善鋪張揚厲収之
punctuated:
天仰聖，欣躍屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第叁塲，策，第一問。謝頤。
同考試官教諭陳批：我高皇帝曁我皇上，心法治功所匹休帝王、垂憲後聖，皆得乎《大學》者。子能榆揚之，其涵濡有得者乎？
同考試官教諭吳批：條答詳盡，末復以臣隣交儆為言，可以占子他日試用矣。
考試官教諭關批：聖學精微，不帝言語文字間也。子獨觀其大者，可以占嚮用矣。
考試官教授潘批：善鋪張揚厲，収之
translation_en:
…toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, we rejoice and leap with delight, in the utmost reverence and trepidation. We respectfully present this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third session: policy essay, first question. Xie Yi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Our Emperor Gao and our present emperor have derived from the Great Learning the methods of cultivating the mind and achievements in government through which they rival the glory of ancient emperors and kings and bequeath models to future sages. You can extol these [?]; surely you have immersed yourself in this learning and gained something from it?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Your responses to the several points are thorough and complete. At the end, you further speak of ministers close to the throne admonishing one another. This allows us to anticipate how you will perform when entrusted with office in the future.”
Comment by Examiner Guan, Instructor: “The learning of the sages is subtle and profound; it is not [confined to?] speech and writing. You alone have perceived its larger aspects, allowing us to anticipate your future employment.”
Comment by Examiner Pan, Professor: “You skilfully expound and celebrate the subject, bringing it to a close with…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大哉帝王之學乎其握樞而總要者其千
聖之眞傳乎其廣業而崇功者其百王之
大法乎是故其事則人己交修也其功則
身心兼體也其始也師資啓沃至精而至
一則内聖之德於是乎立其終也匡翊贊
襄至純而至備則外王之業於是乎成作
乎千萬世之下繼乎千萬世之上所當啓
佑憲章而不容已者此我
皇祖典學之法
===
皇上家學之承
立極而繼
天君治而師敎皆與帝王同其盛矣請得而敬
陳之今夫大學者孔氏之書也非孔氏之
書也二帝三王之書也行二帝三王之道
致二帝三王之治信不可不講也然而春
秋未試也秦漢無聞也豈其書不足徵且
信哉春秋秦漢之君固未志乎二帝三王
之治也韓愈李翱之徒尊信於原道復性
punctuated:
大哉，帝王之學乎！其握樞而總要者，其千聖之眞傳乎！其廣業而崇功者，其百王之大法乎！是故其事則人己交修也，其功則身心兼體也。其始也，師資啓沃，至精而至一，則内聖之德於是乎立；其終也，匡翊贊襄，至純而至備，則外王之業於是乎成。作乎千萬世之下，繼乎千萬世之上，所當啓佑憲章而不容已者，此我皇祖典學之法、皇上家學之承。立極而繼天，君治而師敎，皆與帝王同其盛矣。請得而敬陳之。
今夫《大學》者，孔氏之書也，非孔氏之書也，二帝三王之書也。行二帝三王之道，致二帝三王之治，信不可不講也。然而春秋未試也，秦漢無聞也，豈其書不足徵且信哉？春秋秦漢之君，固未志乎二帝三王之治也。韓愈、李翱之徒，尊信於《原道》《復性》
translation_en:
Great indeed is the learning of emperors and kings! In grasping the pivot and comprehending the essentials, is it not the true transmission of the myriad sages? In extending their undertakings and exalting their achievements, is it not the great model of the hundred kings? Thus its practice involves cultivating both oneself and others, and its accomplishment involves embodying it in both body and mind. At the outset, teachers provide instruction and nurture understanding, bringing it to the utmost refinement and singleness of purpose; thereby the virtue of inward sagehood is established. In the end, ministers correct, support, assist, and advance it, bringing it to the utmost purity and completeness; thereby the enterprise of outward kingship is accomplished. Arising thousands upon thousands of generations later, yet continuing what began thousands upon thousands of generations before, one must receive their guidance and take them as one's model, without ever ceasing. Such was our imperial ancestor’s method of attending to learning, and such is His Majesty’s inheritance of his house’s learning. Establishing the supreme standard and carrying on Heaven’s work, governing as sovereign and instructing as teacher, they equal the ancient emperors and kings in their magnificence. Allow me respectfully to set this forth.
Now the Great Learning is a book of Confucius. Yet it is not merely a book of Confucius: it is a book of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. To practice their Way and achieve their good government, one assuredly must study and expound it. Yet it was not put to the test in the Spring and Autumn period, nor was it heard of under the Qin and Han. Could this have been because the book lacked sufficient authority and credibility? The rulers of the Spring and Autumn period and of the Qin and Han simply never set their aspirations on the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Men such as Han Yu and Li Ao revered and trusted it in their writings, Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao) and Recovering the Nature (Fu xing) …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之篇而不及於政非樂乎其學樂乎其文
也程朱大儒之出發明於學問思辨之功
而未究其施蓋阨乎其時非阨乎其志也
眞德秀氏者作為衍義羽翼聖經既能韓
愈李翺之未能又備程朱大儒之未備自
今觀之以綱則二以目則四首之以典謨
訓誥與思齊之詩家人之卦子思孟子荀
况董仲舒揚雄周敦頤之說則帝王治之
序也次之以堯舜禹湯文武商高宗周成
===
王漢唐以下數君之賢則帝王學之本也
所謂綱也明道術辨人材審治體察民情
格物致知其要矣崇敬畏戒逸慾誠意正
心其要矣謹言行正威儀修身其要矣重
配匹嚴內治定國本教戚屬齊家其要矣
所謂目也蓋古今之精英治亂之龜鑑也
是故一陳於理宗端平之朝再見於吳澄
進講之日然悅而不繹聽而不行則誠有
如我
punctuated:
之篇，而不及於政，非樂乎其學，樂乎其文也。程朱大儒之出，發明於學問思辨之功，而未究其施，蓋阨乎其時，非阨乎其志也。眞德秀氏者，作為《衍義》，羽翼聖經，既能韓愈李翺之未能，又備程朱大儒之未備。自今觀之，以綱則二，以目則四。首之以典謨訓誥與《思齊》之詩、《家人》之卦、子思孟子荀况董仲舒揚雄周敦頤之說，則帝王治之序也；次之以堯舜禹湯文武商高宗周成王漢唐以下數君之賢，則帝王學之本也，所謂綱也。

明道術，辨人材，審治體，察民情，格物致知其要矣；崇敬畏，戒逸慾，誠意正心其要矣；謹言行，正威儀，修身其要矣；重配匹，嚴內治，定國本，教戚屬，齊家其要矣。所謂目也。蓋古今之精英，治亂之龜鑑也。是故一陳於理宗端平之朝，再見於吳澄進講之日。然悅而不繹，聽而不行，則誠有如我
translation_en:
…in their essays, yet did not extend it to government: they delighted not in its learning, but in its literary expression. When the great Confucian scholars Cheng and Zhu emerged, they elucidated the work of study, inquiry, reflection, and discrimination, but did not fully realize its application. They were constrained by their times, not by their aspirations. Zhen Dexiu composed the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) to support the sagely classic. He accomplished what Han Yu and Li Ao had been unable to accomplish, and supplied what even the great scholars Cheng and Zhu had left incomplete. Viewed today, it has two main divisions and four subordinate categories. It begins with the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations, together with the poem “Thinking of the Worthy” (Si qi), the hexagram “The Family” (Jia ren), and the teachings of Zisi, Mengzi, Xun Kuang, Dong Zhongshu, Yang Xiong, and Zhou Dunyi: these set out the proper sequence of imperial and royal government. Next come the worthiness of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, Gaozong of Shang, Cheng of Zhou, and several rulers from the Han and Tang onward: these establish the foundation of imperial and royal learning. These are what are called the main divisions.

Clarifying the methods of the Way, distinguishing human talent, examining the principles of government, and understanding the people's circumstances: these are the essentials of investigating things and extending knowledge. Honoring reverence and awe, and guarding against ease and desire: these are the essentials of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind. Exercising care in speech and conduct, and maintaining proper dignity and deportment: these are the essentials of cultivating oneself. Attaching due weight to the choice of a spouse, strictly ordering the inner household, securing the foundation of the state through the succession, and instructing one's relatives: these are the essentials of regulating the family. These are what are called the subordinate categories. The work is the distilled wisdom of past and present, a guide and mirror for order and disorder. Thus it was first presented at the court of Lizong during the Duanping reign period, and appeared again when Wu Cheng delivered lectures before the throne. Yet if one takes pleasure in it without pondering its meaning, and listens without putting it into practice, then matters are indeed as our …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上所諭者彼烏足以語帝王之盛也哉蓋聖
學之顯晦氣數之盛衰固皆有待而非偶
然也洪惟我
聖祖高皇帝投戈講藝
覃精帝王之學嘉宋濂之請
令左右大書揭之廡壁以代丹青是心也卽
殷湯銘盤之儆武王几豆之箴也一日
御西廡
令濂條析衍義中司馬遷之論濂曰人主能
===
以義理養性則邪僻不能侵興學校敎民
則外侮無從作
聖祖因謂濂曰朕之爲君上畏天地下畏兆民
兢兢業業不敢自逸又嘗觀衍義中鼂錯之
語德秀解之曰人君不窮兵黷武則能生
之而不傷
聖祖顧謂侍臣曰鼂錯之言其所該者廣眞氏
之言其所見者切朕常思爲君恤民所重者
兵與刑爾濫刑者陷人于無辜黷兵者驅人
punctuated:
皇上所諭者，彼烏足以語帝王之盛也哉？蓋聖學之顯晦、氣數之盛衰，固皆有待而非偶然也。
洪惟我聖祖高皇帝，投戈講藝，覃精帝王之學。嘉宋濂之請，令左右大書揭之廡壁，以代丹青。是心也，卽殷湯銘盤之儆、武王几豆之箴也。一日，御西廡，令濂條析《衍義》中司馬遷之論。濂曰：「人主能以義理養性，則邪僻不能侵；興學校敎民，則外侮無從作。」聖祖因謂濂曰：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」又嘗觀《衍義》中鼂錯之語，德秀解之曰：「人君不窮兵黷武，則能生之而不傷。」聖祖顧謂侍臣曰：「鼂錯之言，其所該者廣；眞氏之言，其所見者切。朕常思爲君恤民，所重者兵與刑爾。濫刑者陷人于無辜，黷兵者驅人
translation_en:
…as Your Majesty has admonished. How could they possibly be spoken of as exemplifying the greatness of emperors and kings? Indeed, the illumination or obscuration of sagely learning, and the flourishing or decline of dynastic fortunes, depend upon their proper circumstances; they do not occur by chance.
We reverently reflect that our Sagely Ancestor, the Gao Emperor, laid aside his weapons to discuss the classical arts and devoted his utmost attention to the learning of emperors and kings. Approving Song Lian’s request, he ordered his attendants to write it out in large characters and display it on the corridor walls in place of paintings. This intention was precisely that embodied in the admonition inscribed on the basin of Tang of Yin and the injunctions inscribed on King Wu’s table and ritual vessels. One day, while in the western corridor, he ordered Song Lian to analyze, point by point, Sima Qian’s discussion in the Amplification of the Great Learning (Yanyi). Song Lian said: “If a ruler nourishes his nature through moral principles, depravity cannot intrude; if he establishes schools to instruct the people, foreign aggression will have no opportunity to arise.” The Sagely Ancestor thereupon told Song Lian: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth, and below I stand in awe of the myriad people. Ever vigilant and diligent, I dare not indulge in ease.”
On another occasion, he read Chao Cuo’s words in the Amplification, which Zhen Dexiu explained as follows: “If a ruler does not exhaust his forces and recklessly wage war, he can sustain the people’s lives without harming them.” The Sagely Ancestor turned to his attendant officials and said: “Chao Cuo’s words are broad in their scope; Master Zhen’s words are incisive in their insight. I often reflect that, for a ruler concerned for his people, the weightiest matters are warfare and punishment. Those who impose punishments indiscriminately condemn innocent people; those who recklessly wage war drive people…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于死地有國者所當深戒也由前則心正身
脩之力而敬畏尤慎獨審幾之發誠意之
實功也由後則物格知致之端而兵刑尤
畏天畏民之要治平之絜矩也大哉
皇言其得於觀剔體驗之深者乎嗣是我
昭皇喜楊士奇之言而以監戒目之既善繼而
善述
純皇定
經筵之例而
===
命儒臣讀之尤日就而月將即文武作之於上
孔曾承之於下徽猷莫之尚矣我
皇上上嘉下樂
銳意帝王之治乃資益是書又取
先朝之制而損益之月有常期章有定限是心
也即大禹寸陰之惜高宗時敏之修也伏
覩
聖諭有曰是書綱舉目張治亂興亡罔不該括
朕勉循是言為修己治人之則豈不大有裨
punctuated: 于死地，有國者所當深戒也。由前則心正身脩之力，而敬畏尤慎獨審幾之發、誠意之實功也；由後則物格知致之端，而兵刑尤畏天畏民之要、治平之絜矩也。大哉，皇言！其得於觀剔體驗之深者乎！嗣是，我昭皇喜楊士奇之言，而以監戒目之，既善繼而善述；純皇定經筵之例，而命儒臣讀之，尤日就而月將。即文武作之於上，孔曾承之於下，徽猷莫之尚矣。我皇上上嘉下樂，銳意帝王之治，乃資益是書，又取先朝之制而損益之，月有常期，章有定限。是心也，即大禹寸陰之惜、高宗時敏之修也。伏覩聖諭有曰：「是書綱舉目張，治亂興亡，罔不該括。朕勉循是言，為修己治人之則，豈不大有裨
translation_en:
…to their deaths. Those who possess a state must take this deeply to heart as a warning.” The former remarks reveal the efficacy of rectifying the mind and cultivating the person; reverence and awe, especially, express vigilance when alone and discernment of the first stirrings of action, and constitute the actual work of making the intentions sincere. The latter remarks reveal the beginnings of investigating things and extending knowledge; military affairs and punishments, especially, are central to fearing Heaven and standing in awe of the people, and embody the principle of the measuring square for governing the state and bringing peace to the world. Great indeed are these imperial words! Were they not gained through profound scrutiny [?] and personal experience?

Thereafter, our Emperor Zhao welcomed Yang Shiqi’s words and regarded this book as a mirror and a warning: he excelled both in carrying on his predecessor’s work and in giving it expression. Emperor Chun established the rules for the Classics Colloquium and commanded Confucian officials to read the book aloud, making still further progress day by day and month by month. Even with Kings Wen and Wu initiating the work above, and Confucius and Zengzi carrying it forward below, no splendid example could surpass this.

Our present Emperor, with approval above and rejoicing below [?], resolutely seeks the government of the ancient emperors and kings, drawing benefit from this book. He has also adopted and modified the institutions of previous reigns: each month has regularly appointed dates, and the chapters to be covered have fixed limits. This intention is precisely that of Great Yu cherishing every moment, and of Gaozong cultivating himself through constant diligence. I have reverently read an imperial instruction which says: “This book raises the main threads and spreads out the mesh: order and disorder, rise and fall—there is nothing it does not encompass. I strive to follow these words as the standard for cultivating myself and governing others. Would this not be of great benefit…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉又曰匪徒知之實欲行之尚賴卿等竭誠
協恭輔導朕躬則衍義之功不在眞氏而在
卿等矣聽講之餘充然有得因賦詩一章曰
帝王所圖治務學當為先下作民之主上乃
承乎
天致治貴有本本端化自平人君所學者其序
有後前正心誠其意志定必不遷吾志旣能
定理道豈復顛身修本心正家國治同然國
治乃昭明萬邦斯協焉於變帝堯典思齊文
===
王篇萬化修身始朕念方拳拳旣又
親灑
宸翰以
賜輔臣
命賡和之而其詞有曰無欲德乃明主靜志不
遷一理散萬殊察見毫芒顛有曰聖學能
敬止帝業可光前釋玆恒在念知止固無
遷有曰孔論述蕩蕩箕疇賛平平致此術
非遠大道存目前有曰大學示綱目燦然
punctuated:
哉！」又曰：「匪徒知之，實欲行之。尚賴卿等竭誠協恭，輔導朕躬，則衍義之功不在眞氏，而在卿等矣。」聽講之餘，充然有得，因賦詩一章，曰：「帝王所圖治，務學當為先。下作民之主，上乃承乎天。致治貴有本，本端化自平。人君所學者，其序有後前。正心誠其意，志定必不遷。吾志旣能定，理道豈復顛？身修本心正，家國治同然。國治乃昭明，萬邦斯協焉。於變帝堯典，思齊文王篇。萬化修身始，朕念方拳拳。」
旣又親灑宸翰，以賜輔臣，命賡和之。而其詞有曰：「無欲德乃明，主靜志不遷。一理散萬殊，察見毫芒顛。」有曰：「聖學能敬止，帝業可光前。釋玆恒在念，知止固無遷。」有曰：「孔論述蕩蕩，箕疇賛平平。致此術非遠，大道存目前。」有曰：「大學示綱目，燦然

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
羅目前功至德自固外物詎能遷有曰乾
乾自不息安安而能遷升堂入其室登山
陟其巔
君倡臣和彙爲一帙而
翊學詩名焉大哉
皇言又有得於學問自修者乎由是二紀以來
遵道者丕變觀
聖者奕新而
大典微言揭如星日則顧諟緝熙之顯德薄海
内外禮備樂和刑清政舉而
鴻恩濊澤同乎天地則親賢樂利之成功即堯
舜都俞於當時三王煕皥於前古美業無
以加矣而執事尤有厚望焉又以
聖子
神孫所當祗遹紹聞者爲問此詢蕘采菲之過
也海隅末學何足以知之雖然我
皇祖之表章至矣繼我
皇上之規式詳矣他日
punctuated: 羅目前，功至德自固，外物詎能遷？」有曰：「乾乾自不息，安安而能遷；升堂入其室，登山陟其巔。」君倡臣和，彙爲一帙，而《翊學詩》名焉。大哉，皇言！又有得於學問自修者乎？由是二紀以來，遵道者丕變，觀聖者奕新，而大典微言揭如星日，則顧諟緝熙之顯德；薄海内外，禮備樂和，刑清政舉，而鴻恩濊澤同乎天地，則親賢樂利之成功。即堯舜都俞於當時，三王煕皥於前古，美業無以加矣。而執事尤有厚望焉，又以聖子神孫所當祗遹紹聞者爲問，此詢蕘采菲之過也。海隅末學何足以知之？雖然，我皇祖之表章至矣，繼我皇上之規式詳矣。他日……
translation_en:
…arrayed before one's eyes. When accomplishment is attained, virtue becomes firm of itself; how could external things move it?” Another passage says: “Ever diligent, never ceasing of oneself; at ease, yet able to change [?]. Ascend the hall and enter its inner chamber; climb the mountain and reach its summit.” The ruler initiated the verses and his ministers composed responses; these were gathered into one volume, entitled Poems in Aid of Learning (Yixue shi). How great are the imperial words! Do they not also embody insights gained through study and self-cultivation?

Thus, over the past twenty-four years, those who follow the Way have undergone a profound transformation, and those who look to the sage have been renewed in splendor. The subtle teachings of the great classics stand manifest like the stars and sun: this is the illustrious virtue of keeping Heaven's mandate constantly in view and continuously advancing in brightness. Throughout the realm and beyond, to the seas, ritual is complete, music harmonious, punishments just, and government effective. The vast imperial bounty and abundant beneficence equal those of Heaven and Earth: this is the accomplished result of cherishing the worthy, enjoying happiness, and sharing its benefits. Even the splendid achievements of Yao and Shun, exchanging counsels and assent in their day, and of the Three Kings, bringing radiant harmony in ancient times, could not surpass these.

Yet you, honored examiners, hold still greater hopes, and further ask what the sage sons and divine grandsons ought reverently to follow and receive as transmitted instruction. This is carrying too far the practice of consulting woodcutters and gathering humble plants—that is, seeking counsel from the lowly. How could an insignificant student from this coastal corner know enough to answer? Nevertheless, our imperial ancestor's work of honoring and elucidating the teachings was consummate; subsequently, the standards established by our reigning emperor have been comprehensive. In days to come…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
閣幃之獻納
宮職之論思必有賛
睿知於方來守
成憲以萬世而程朱之發明眞氏之衍義信乎
其爲遇矣然眞氏又謂君臣者皆不可不
知大學蓋君以清出治之源臣以盡正君
之法也此又在中外之臣洗濯精明共承
休德協恭篤棐寅亮天工於以仰體
兢業之衷於以祇佩
===
本端之訓如是則
上下一於至善功化極於新民與帝王竝休與
天地同久庶乎
聖學萬一之助也詩不云乎世德作求永言配
命成王之孚下土之式愚請誦此以爲
獻
第二問
嚴文輔
同考試官學正呂批五經異同處塲中作者
punctuated:
閣幃之獻納，宮職之論思，必有賛睿知於方來，守成憲以萬世，而程朱之發明、眞氏之衍義，信乎其爲遇矣。然眞氏又謂君臣者皆不可不知大學，蓋君以清出治之源，臣以盡正君之法也。此又在中外之臣洗濯精明，共承休德，協恭篤棐，寅亮天工，於以仰體兢業之衷，於以祇佩本端之訓。如是則上下一於至善，功化極於新民，與帝王竝休，與天地同久，庶乎聖學萬一之助也。《詩》不云乎：「世德作求，永言配命。成王之孚，下土之式。」愚請誦此以爲獻。
第二問
嚴文輔
同考試官學正呂批：五經異同處，塲中作者
translation_en:
…The counsel offered in the study chambers and the deliberations of palace officials will surely assist sagely understanding in the years ahead and preserve established statutes for ten thousand generations. The elucidations of Cheng and Zhu and Zhen’s Extended Meaning will then truly have met with their proper reception. Yet Zhen also said that neither ruler nor minister could afford to be ignorant of the Great Learning: the ruler uses it to purify the source from which governance proceeds, and the minister to fulfill the methods for rectifying his ruler. This further depends upon officials at court and in the provinces cleansing themselves and attaining clarity, together upholding excellent virtue, cooperating reverently and offering steadfast assistance, and respectfully assisting Heaven’s work. By these means they may reverently embody Your Majesty’s vigilant concern and respectfully cherish your instruction to rectify the root. Thus those above and below will be united in the highest good, and their achievements and transforming influence will culminate in renewing the people. Their glory will equal that of the ancient emperors and kings and endure as long as Heaven and Earth. Perhaps this may provide some infinitesimal assistance to Your Majesty’s sagely learning. Does not the Book of Odes say: “Seek to carry forward the virtue of generations, forever matching Heaven’s mandate. King Cheng’s trustworthiness is a model for all below”? I humbly ask to recite these words as my offering.
Second Question
Yan Wenfu

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
率多撫綴浮泛獨此篇能總羣言而折中之詞義
明備卓有定見讀之斂衽尊經之學子蓋用心者
考試官教諭蕭批詞氣老竪剖析精明足
破千古不決之疑宜刻以傳
考試官教授潘批條答詳明博洽之士也
學者有讀經之要有尊經之實夫分章析
句非所以讀經也黨同伐異非所以尊經
也讀經者貴舉其要尊經者貴致其實夫
讀經者莫不有疑焉裁之以吾之心是故
===
其要可得而舉也亦莫不有得焉體之以
吾之身是故其實可得而致也請因執事
之問之所及而質之易之分上下經也先
儒韓康伯孔穎達程伊川頤朱晦菴熹吳
草廬澄皆嘗求之矣而未有以得其至當
之歸者元泰定間泰和有蕭漢中者為易
學攷原之書以發之其說以乾坤坎離為
上經之主震巽艮兌為下經之主乾坤坎
離本體之卦居於上經其體之分出於上
punctuated:
率多撫綴浮泛，獨此篇能總羣言而折中之，詞義明備，卓有定見，讀之斂衽。尊經之學，子蓋用心者。
考試官教諭蕭批：詞氣老竪，剖析精明，足破千古不決之疑，宜刻以傳。
考試官教授潘批：條答詳明，博洽之士也。
學者有讀經之要，有尊經之實。夫分章析句，非所以讀經也；黨同伐異，非所以尊經也。讀經者貴舉其要，尊經者貴致其實。夫讀經者莫不有疑焉，裁之以吾之心，是故其要可得而舉也；亦莫不有得焉，體之以吾之身，是故其實可得而致也。請因執事之問之所及而質之。《易》之分上下經也，先儒韓康伯、孔穎達、程伊川頤、朱晦菴熹、吳草廬澄皆嘗求之矣，而未有以得其至當之歸者。元泰定間，泰和有蕭漢中者，為《易學攷原》之書以發之。其說以乾坤坎離為上經之主，震巽艮兌為下經之主。乾坤坎離本體之卦居於上經，其體之分出於上
translation_en:
…Most merely patch together material [?] and remain superficial. This essay alone brings together the various interpretations and adjudicates among them. Its language and meaning are clear and complete, and it displays outstandingly firm judgments. Reading it, one straightens one’s robes in respect. You have evidently devoted care to the study of honoring the Classics.
Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “The language and spirit are seasoned [?], and the analysis is penetrating and clear. It is sufficient to resolve doubts left unsettled for ages and deserves to be printed for circulation.”
Examiner Pan, Professor, comments: “The answers to the individual points are detailed and clear. This is a man of broad and thorough learning.”
For scholars, there are essentials to grasp in reading the Classics and concrete practice through which to honor them. Dividing chapters and dissecting sentences is not the way to read the Classics; siding with those who agree and attacking those who differ is not the way to honor them. In reading the Classics, what matters is grasping their essentials; in honoring them, what matters is realizing them in practice. Everyone who reads the Classics encounters doubts. By judging these with one’s own mind, one can grasp their essentials. Everyone also gains insights. By embodying these in one’s own person, one can realize them in practice. Allow me to examine this in light of the matters raised in your question.
As for the division of the Book of Changes into upper and lower sections, earlier Confucian scholars—Han Kangbo, Kong Yingda, Cheng Yi (Yichuan), Zhu Xi (Hui’an), and Wu Cheng (Caolu)—all investigated it, but none arrived at a fully satisfactory explanation. During the Taiding era of the Yuan dynasty, a man of Taihe named Xiao Hanzhong wrote Investigating the Origins of the Study of the Changes (Yixue kaoyuan) to elucidate it. His explanation takes Qian, Kun, Kan, and Li as the governing hexagrams of the upper section, and Zhen, Xun, Gen, and Dui as those of the lower section. The hexagrams in which Qian, Kun, Kan, and Li appear in their fundamental forms occupy the upper section; those derived by dividing their constituent forms that appear in the upper…

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
經者用於內也分出於下經者用於外也
震巽艮兌本體之卦居於下經其體之分
出於下經者用於內也分出於上經者用
於外也用於內為主用於外為客嘗考其
卦體之所以分又考其卦體之所以合則
知上下經一體不可多不可少而兩經中
一卦不可先不可後矣是其說雖若有異
於儒先者然邵康節雍嘗曰乾坤坎離上
篇之用兌艮震巽下篇之用則蕭氏亦因
===
而推極之耳非無稽也況分合序次燦然
有章豈得以異於程朱而否之耶先正朱
升氏稱其為古今之絕學蓋亦非虛譽矣
書之有今古文也其在於伏生之所授鼂
錯之所受者為今文其在於孔壁之所藏
安國之所序梅賾之所上者為古文今文
多艱深古文反平易此世之所疑也朱子
曰小序決非孔門之舊安國序亦非西漢
文章是疑其序矣吳氏曰伏氏書辭義古
punctuated:
經者，用於內也；分出於下經者，用於外也。震巽艮兌本體之卦居於下經，其體之分出於下經者，用於內也；分出於上經者，用於外也。用於內為主，用於外為客。嘗考其卦體之所以分，又考其卦體之所以合，則知上下經一體，不可多，不可少，而兩經中一卦不可先，不可後矣。是其說雖若有異於儒先者，然邵康節雍嘗曰：「乾坤坎離，上篇之用；兌艮震巽，下篇之用。」則蕭氏亦因而推極之耳，非無稽也。況分合序次，燦然有章，豈得以異於程朱而否之耶？先正朱升氏稱其為古今之絕學，蓋亦非虛譽矣。
書之有今古文也，其在於伏生之所授、鼂錯之所受者為今文；其在於孔壁之所藏、安國之所序、梅賾之所上者為古文。今文多艱深，古文反平易，此世之所疑也。朱子曰：「小序決非孔門之舊，安國序亦非西漢文章。」是疑其序矣。吳氏曰：「伏氏書辭義古
translation_en:
…those distributed within the Upper Classic function internally; those distributed within the Lower Classic function externally. The hexagrams embodying the fundamental forms of Zhen, Xun, Gen, and Dui occupy the Lower Classic. Those derived from their forms and distributed within the Lower Classic function internally; those distributed within the Upper Classic function externally. Those functioning internally are hosts; those functioning externally are guests. Having examined how the hexagram forms are divided, and then how they are combined, one knows that the Upper and Lower Classics constitute a single whole, to which nothing can be added and from which nothing can be taken away; nor can any hexagram in either Classic be placed earlier or later. Although this explanation may seem to differ from those of earlier Confucian scholars, Shao Yong, known as Kangjie, once said: “Qian, Kun, Kan, and Li provide the functioning of the upper section; Dui, Gen, Zhen, and Xun provide the functioning of the lower section.” Thus Master Xiao merely developed this to its fullest extent; his account is not without foundation. Moreover, its divisions, combinations, and sequence display a clear pattern. How could one reject it merely because it differs from Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi? The former worthy Zhu Sheng called it a learning unrivaled in ancient or modern times. This was surely no empty praise.
As for the modern-script and ancient-script versions of the Book of Documents: what Fu Sheng transmitted and Chao Cuo received constitutes the modern-script version; what was concealed in the wall of Confucius’s residence, prefaced by Kong Anguo, and presented to the throne by Mei Ze constitutes the ancient-script version. The modern-script text is often difficult and abstruse, whereas the ancient-script text is, on the contrary, plain and accessible. This is what people find suspect. Master Zhu said: “The minor prefaces certainly do not descend from the school of Confucius, and Anguo’s preface is likewise not a Western Han composition.” Thus he doubted the prefaces. Master Wu said: “The wording and meaning of Master Fu’s Book of Documents are ancient …

title: 嘉靖二十五年廣東鄉試錄
text:
奧其爲古書無疑梅賾所增雖無一字無
所本而平緩卑弱不類先漢以前之文是
弁疑其書矣愚嘗論之錯之受書也所不
知者十二三略以意屬讀而已則今文固
不能無訛孔壁書出而不能有所是正其
能免於儒先之疑乎然以爲張霸僞爲則
舜典汩作九共等二十四篇當時已覺其
僞矣以爲梅賾擬作則網羅逸書從容理
道賾何人也而能之乎人心惟危十六字
===
者萬世道學之源德無常師十六字者千
聖心法之要賾何人也而知之乎意者科
斗隸古文或不能相通斷簡殘編言未免
於附會謂之皆孔壁之舊固未敢謂之非
孔壁之物亦豈敢乎要之不詭聖言有裨
吾道固不害其爲經也詩之有大小序自
毛學傳而說詩者宗之至朱子詩傳始盡
去其序而經是求東萊呂氏讀詩記則宗
毛氏以立訓考註疏以纂言若大相異者
punctuated:
奧，其爲古書無疑。梅賾所增，雖無一字無所本，而平緩卑弱，不類先漢以前之文。」是弁疑其書矣。愚嘗論之：錯之受書也，所不知者十二三，略以意屬讀而已，則今文固不能無訛。孔壁書出，而不能有所是正，其能免於儒先之疑乎？然以爲張霸僞爲，則《舜典》《汩作》《九共》等二十四篇，當時已覺其僞矣；以爲梅賾擬作，則網羅逸書，從容理道，賾何人也，而能之乎？「人心惟危」十六字者，萬世道學之源；「德無常師」十六字者，千聖心法之要。賾何人也，而知之乎？意者科斗、隸古文或不能相通，斷簡殘編，言未免於附會。謂之皆孔壁之舊，固未敢；謂之非孔壁之物，亦豈敢乎？要之，不詭聖言，有裨吾道，固不害其爲經也。

《詩》之有大小序，自毛學傳，而說《詩》者宗之。至朱子《詩傳》，始盡去其序，而經是求。東萊呂氏《讀詩記》，則宗毛氏以立訓，考註疏以纂言，若大相異者。
translation_en:
…profound: there is no doubt that it is an ancient text.
